*dhattūrakaṃ karṇikāraṃ śaṇapuṣpaṃ ca mallikām \|\| 49 \|\|*

*kuśāpāmārgatulasīmādhavīcaṃpakādikam \|*  
*bṛhatīkaravīrāṇi yathālabdhāni sādhakaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

*nivedayetsugaṃdhīni mālyāni vividhāni ca \|*  
*dhūpaṃ kālāgarūtpannaṃ dīpaṃ ca vimalaṃ śubham \|\| 51 \|\|*

45-51. The Lord should be bathed by means of the holy waters from five conchshells as well as Pañcāmṛta. While bathing the Rudrasūkta should be recited with single-pointed devotion. Āsana (offering of seats) and other services should be rendered while the requisite Mantras are being recited. The seat offered should be a gold one covered with divine garments. The Arghya should have the eight requisite qualities. The Pādya (washing the feet) should be with clear water. The same thing for ritualistic rinsing of the mouth. Madhuparka should abound in honey. Ācamana should be offered again and the holy ablution be conducted by means of Mantras. Similarly a sacred thread, garments and ornaments should be offered. Pure sweet scents with eight ancillaries should be offered.

The Sādhaka (devotee) then should offer different kinds of sweet-smelling flowers and garlands of flowers as and when obtained such as Bilva, Mandāra, Kalhāra, Lotus, Dhattūra, Karṇikāra, Śaṇa flower, Jasmine, Darbha, Apāmārga, Tulasī, Mādhavī, Caṃpaka etc., Bṛhatī and Karavīra. The incense offered should be of black agallochum and the lamp shall be splendid.

## \|\| 3.7.52-56 \|\|

*viśeṣakam \|*  
*atha pāyasanaivedyaṃ saghṛtaṃ sopadaṃśakam \|*  
*modakāpūpasaṃyuktaṃ śarkarāguḍasaṃyutam \|\| 52 \|\|*

*madhunāktaṃ dadhiyutaṃ jalapānasamanvitam \|*  
*tenaiva haviṣā vahnau juhuyānmaṃtrabhāvite \|\| 53 \|\|*

*āgamoktena vidhinā guruvākyaniyaṃtritaḥ \|*  
*naivedyaṃ śaṃbhave bhūyo dattvā tāṃbūlamuttamam \|\| 54 \|\|*

*dhūpaṃ nīrājanaṃ ramyaṃ chatraṃ darpaṇamuttamam \|*  
*samarpayitvā vidhivanmaṃtrairvedikatāṃtrikaiḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*yadyaśaktaḥ svayaṃ niḥsvo yathāvibhavamarcayet \|*  
*bhakttyā dattena gaurīśaḥ puṣpamātreṇa tuṣyati \|\| 56 \|\|*

52-56. The next item is the offering of Naivedya with milkpudding along with ghee and side dishes and also sweetmeat with cooked pie together with sugar and jaggery. It should be soaked in honey and the snacks should be blended with curds. With this alone as Havis (what is offered into the sacred fire) the devotee should consign it to the fire sanctified by means of Mantras. In accordance with the injunctions contained in the Āgama texts, the devotee should be restrained by the instructions of the preceptor and should offer Naivedya once again along with an excellent Tāṃbūla. He should then dedicate incense, Nīrājana (offering of lights in a circular waving motion), a beautiful umbrella and an excellent mirror while reciting different kinds of Mantras both Vedic and Tāntrika.

If the devotee is physically incapable or if he is poor, he should worship only as per his monetary capacity. The Lord of Gaurī becomes satisfied even with a mere flower given with ardent devotion.

## \|\| 3.7.57 \|\|

*athāṃgabhūtānsakalāngaṇeśādīnprapūjayet \|*  
*stavairnānāvidhaiḥ stutvā sāṣṭāṃgaṃ praṇamedbudhaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Thereafter, he should worship all the subsidiary deities, Gaṇeśa and others. The wise man should eulogize with different kinds of hymns and prayers and should prostrate himself with his eight limbs touching the ground.

## \|\| 3.7.58 \|\|

*tataḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya vṛṣacaṃḍeśvarādikān \|*  
*pūjāṃ samarpya vidhivatprārthayedgirijāpatim \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Thereafter, the devotee should circumambulate Vṛṣa (bull), Caṇḍeśvara and others. After concluding the adoration duly, he should pray to the Consort of the Daughter of the Mountain.

The Eulogy and the Prayer:

## \|\| 3.7.59 \|\|

*jaya deva jagannātha jaya śaṃkara śāśvata \|*  
*jaya sarva surādhyakṣa jaya sarvasurārcita \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. “Be victorious, O Lord; O Lord of the universe. Glory to (you), O Śaṅkara, the eternal one. Be victorious, O presiding deity of all Suras. Be victorious, O Lord worshipped by all Suras.

## \|\| 3.7.60 \|\|

*jaya sarvaguṇātīta jaya sarvavaraprada \|*  
*jaya nitya nirādhāra jaya viśvaṃbharāvyaya \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Glory to you, O Lord transcending all the attributes. Be victorious, O bestower of all boons. Glory to you, O eternal one having no need of support. Be victorious, O immutable one, O sustainer of the entire universe.

## \|\| 3.7.61 \|\|

*jaya viśvaikavedyeśa jaya nāgeṃdrabhūṣaṇa \|*  
*jaya gaurīpate śaṃbho jaya caṃdrārdhaśekhara \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Be victorious, O Lord, the sole one to be known in the whole universe. Glory to you, O Lord wearing the serpent king as an ornament. Be victorious, O Lord of Gaurī, O Śaṃbhu. Be victorious, O Lord with the semicircular moon as your crest-jewel.

## \|\| 3.7.62 \|\|

*jaya koṭyarkasaṃkāśa jayānaṃtaguṇāśraya \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Hail to you (who are) brilliant like ten million suns (combined); to you, the receptacle of infinite good qualities.

## \|\| 3.7.63 \|\|

*jaya rudra virūpākṣa jayāciṃtya niraṃjana \|*  
*jaya nātha kṛpāsiṃdho jaya bhaktārtibhañjana \|*  
*jaya dustarasaṃsārasāgarottāraṇa prabho \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Victory to Rudra of uneven (three) eyes, one beyond comprehension, the pure (unsullied one). Be victorious, O Lord, O ocean of mercy. Glory to you, O destroyer of the distress of the devotee. Be victorious, O Lord who redeem us from the impassable ocean of worldly existence.

## \|\| 3.7.64 \|\|

*prasīda me mahādeva saṃsārārttasya khidyataḥ \|*  
*sarvapāpabhayaṃ hṛtvā rakṣa māṃ parameśvara \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Be pleased with me, O great Lord. I am distressed and disgusted with the world. Remove all the fear due to sin, and protect me, O great Lord.

## \|\| 3.7.65-66 \|\|

*mahādāridryamagnasya mahāpāpahatasya ca \|*  
*mahāśokavinaṣṭasya mahārogāturasya ca \|\| 65 \|\|*

*ṛṇabhāraparītasya dahyamānasya karmabhiḥ \|*  
*grahaiḥ prapīḍyamānasya prasīda mama śaṃkara \|\| 66 \|\|*

65-66. I am sinking in the mire of great poverty. I am blighted by great sins. I am ruined by intense grief. I am engulfed by the weight of indebtedness. I am being burned by (my) actions. O Śaṅkara, be pleased with me afflicted by malignant Planets.”

## \|\| 3.7.67 \|\|

*daridraḥ prārthayedevaṃ pūjāṃte girijāpatim \|*  
*arthāḍhyo vāpi rājā vā prārthayeddevamīśvaram \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. If the devotee is poor, he should request thus the Lord of Girijā, at the conclusion of the adoration. The king though possessing much wealth should request Lord Īśvara as follows:

A Prayer:

## \|\| 3.7.68 \|\|

*dīrghamāyuḥ sadārogyaṃ kośavṛddhirbalonnatiḥ \|*  
*mamāstu nityamānandaḥ prasādāttava śaṃkara \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. “O Śaṅkara, with thy favour, let me have a long life, freedom from diseases, ever increasing treasury, progress in might and bliss forever.

## \|\| 3.7.69 \|\|

*śatravaḥ saṃkṣayaṃ yāṃtu prasīdantu mama grahāḥ \|*  
*naśyantu dasyavo rāṣṭre janāḥ saṃtu nirāpadaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. May the enemies perish. May the Planets be favourable to me. Let the marauders and robbers perish. Let all the people of the nation be free from adversity.

## \|\| 3.7.70 \|\|

*durbhikṣamārīsaṃtāpāḥ śamaṃ yāṃtu mahītale \|*  
*sarvasasyasamṛddhiśca bhūyātsukhamayā diśaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. May famine, pestilence and distress subside all over the earth. Let there be food-grains in plenty. Let all the quarters be happy and cheerful.”

## \|\| 3.7.71 \|\|

*evamārādhayeddevaṃ pradoṣe girijāpatim \|*  
*brāhmaṇānbhojayetpaścāddakṣiṇābhiśca toṣayet \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Thus the devotee shall propitiate the Lord of Girijā at the time of Pradoṣa. Thereafter, he should feed Brāhmaṇas and please them with monetary gifts.

## \|\| 3.7.72 \|\|

*sarvapāpakṣayakarī sarvadāridryanāśinī \|*  
*śivapūjā mayā khyātā sarvābhīṣṭavarapradā \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Thus the worship of Śiva has been narrated by me. It bestows all cherished desires as a boon. It destroys all sins. It is destructive of all poverty.

## \|\| 3.7.73 \|\|

*mahāpātakasaṃghātamadhikaṃ copapātakam \|*  
*śivadravyāpaharaṇādanyatsarvaṃ nivārayet \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. It shall eradicate all major sins and most of the minor sins except that resulting from misappropriating Śiva’s assets.

## \|\| 3.7.74 \|\|

*brahmahatyādipāpānāṃ purāṇeṣu smṛtiṣvapi \|*  
*prāyaścittāni dṛṣṭāni na śivadravyahāriṇām \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Expiations for all the sins including that of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter are shown in the Purāṇas and Smṛtis, but none for the sins of those who misappropriate Śiva’s property.

## \|\| 3.7.75 \|\|

*bahunātra kimuktena ślokārdhena bravīmyaham \|*  
*brahmahatyāśataṃ vāpi śivapūjā vināśayet \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Why speak too much? I shall summarise everything in half a verse. The worship of Śiva shall eradicate hundreds of (sins of) Brāhmaṇa-slaughter.

## \|\| 3.7.76 \|\|

*mayā kathitametatte pradoṣe śivapūjanam \|*  
*rahasyaṃ sarvajaṃtūnāmatra nāstyeva saṃśayaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Thus the procedure of the worship of Śiva at the time of Pradoṣa has been narrated to you. It is a secret to all living beings. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 3.7.77 \|\|

*etābhyāmapi bālābhyāmevaṃ pūjā vidhīyatām \|*  
*ataḥ saṃvatsarādeva parāṃ siddhimavāpsyatha \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Let the adoration be performed by these two boys. Within a year you will all attain the highest achievements.

## \|\| 3.7.78 \|\|

*iti śāṃḍilyavacanamākarṇya dvijabhāminī \|*  
*tābhyāṃ tu saha bālābhyāṃ praṇanāma muneḥ padam \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. On hearing these words of Śāṇḍilya, the Brāhmaṇa lady bowed down to the feet of the sage along with the two boys.

## \|\| 3.7.79 \|\|

*viprastryuvāca \|*  
*ahamadya kṛtārthāsmi tava darśanamātrataḥ \|*  
*etau kumārau bhagavaṃstvāmeva śaraṇaṃ gatau \|\| 79 \|\|*

The Brāhmaṇa lady said:

79\. O holy Sir, I am contented and blessed today merely by your vision. These two boys have sought refuge in you.

## \|\| 3.7.80 \|\|

*eṣa me tanayo brahmañchucivrata itīritaḥ \|*  
*eṣa rājasuto nāmnā dharmaguptaḥ kṛto mayā \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. This is my son named Śucivrata. This is the prince named by me as Dharmagupta.

## \|\| 3.7.81 \|\|

*etāvahaṃ ca bhagavanbhavaccaraṇakiṃkarāḥ \|*  
*samuddharāsminpatitānghore dāridryasāgare \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. These two and I, O holy Sir, are servants at your feet. Save us who have fallen into the terrible ocean of poverty.

## \|\| 3.7.82 \|\|

*iti prapannāṃ śaraṇaṃ dvijāṃganāmāśvāsya vākyairamṛtopamānaiḥ \|*  
*upādideśātha tayoḥ kumārayormuniḥ śivārādhanamaṃtra vidyām \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. When the Brāhmaṇa lady sought refuge in him thus, the sage consoled her with nectar-like sweet words. Thereafter, the sage imparted the specific Mantras for the propitiation of Śiva.

## \|\| 3.7.83 \|\|

*athopadiṣṭau muninā kumārau brāhmaṇī ca sā \|*  
*taṃ praṇamya samāmaṃtrya jagmuste śivamaṃdirāt \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Then the boys who had been instructed by the sage and the Brāhmaṇa lady, bowed and took leave of them. Then they departed from that Śiva temple.

## \|\| 3.7.84 \|\|

*tataḥ prabhṛti tau bālau munivaryopadeśataḥ \|*  
*pradoṣe pārvatīśasya pūjāṃ cakraturaṃjasā \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Thereafter those two boys began to perform the adoration of Pārvatī’s Consort (Śiva) at the time of Pradoṣa in accordance with the instructions of the excellent sage.

## \|\| 3.7.85 \|\|

*evaṃ pūjayatordevaṃ dvijarājakumārayoḥ \|*  
*sukhenaiva vyatīyāya tayormāsacatuṣṭayam \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Even as the Brāhmaṇa boy and the prince began to adore the Lord, four months passed by very happily.

## \|\| 3.7.86 \|\|

*kadācidrājaputreṇa vināsau dvijanaṃdanaḥ \|*  
*snātuṃ gato nadītīre cacāra bahulīlayā \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Once the Brāhmaṇa boy, unaccompanied by the prince, went to the river to take his bath. He roamed about playfully.

## \|\| 3.7.87 \|\|

*tatra nirjharanirghātanirbhinne vapra kuṭṭime \|*  
*nidhānakalaśaṃ sthūlaṃ prasphuraṃtaṃ dadarśa ha \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. There in a paved platform near the bank of the river, that had been eroded by the continuous flow of the stream, he saw a treasure trove shining.

## \|\| 3.7.88 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā sahasāgatya harṣakautukavihvalaḥ \|*  
*daivopapannaṃ manvāno gṛhītvā śirasā yayau \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. On seeing it and considering it a divine legacy, the boy took it on his head and went home highly delighted.

## \|\| 3.7.89 \|\|

*sasaṃbhramaṃ samānīya nidhāya kalaśaṃ balāt \|*  
*nidhāya bhavanasyāṃte mātaraṃ samabhāṣata \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. With great excitement, he brought the treasure trove inside the house and spoke to his mother:

## \|\| 3.7.90 \|\|

*mātarmātarimaṃ paśya prasādaṃ girijāpateḥ \|*  
*nidhānaṃ kumbharūpeṇa darśitaṃ karuṇātmanā \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. “Mother, mother, see the favour of (gift from) the Lord of Girijā. A treasure in the form of a pot has been shown by the merciful one.”

## \|\| 3.7.91 \|\|

*atha sā vismitā sādhvī samāhūya nṛpātmajam \|*  
*svaputraṃ pratinaṃdyāha mānayantī śivārcanam \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. That chaste lady who got surprised, called the prince and congratulating her son said, acknowledging (the efficacy of) the worship of Śiva:

## \|\| 3.7.92 \|\|

*śṛṇutāṃ me vacaḥ putrau nidhānakalaśīmimām \|*  
*samaṃ vibhajya gṛhṇītaṃ mama śāsanagauravāt \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. “Listen to me, dear sons. Share this treasure trove equally between you two. That is my order.”

## \|\| 3.7.93 \|\|

*iti māturvacaḥ śrutvā tutoṣa dvija naṃdanaḥ \|*  
*pratyāha rājaputrastāṃ visrabdhaḥ śaṃkarārcane \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. On hearing these words of his mother, the Brāhmaṇa boy was glad. But the prince who was confident of the worship of Śaṅkara, replied thus:

## \|\| 3.7.94-95 \|\|

*mātastava sutasyaiva sukṛtena samāgatam \|*  
*nāhaṃ grahītumicchāmi vibhaktaṃ dhanasaṃca yam \|\| 94 \|\|*

*ātmanaḥ sukṛtāllabdhaṃ svayameva bhunaktvasau \|*  
*sa eva bhagavānīśaḥ kariṣyati kṛpāṃ mayi \|\| 95 \|\|*

94-95. “O mother, this has come to your son due to his own merit. I do not wish to share the acquisition. Let him alone enjoy what has been obtained through his own merit. The same Lord will be merciful to me.”

## \|\| 3.7.96 \|\|

*evamarcayatoḥ śaṃbhuṃ bhūyopi parayā mudā \|*  
*saṃvatsaro vyatīyāya tasminneva gṛhe tayoḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. Then they continued their worship in the same house with extreme delight. Thus a year passed by.

## \|\| 3.7.97 \|\|

*athaikadā rājasūnuḥ saha tena dvijanmanā \|*  
*vasaṃtasamaye prāpte vijahāra vanāṃ tare \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. Once, when spring season had set in, the prince was sporting about in the forest along with the Brāhmaṇa boy.

## \|\| 3.7.98 \|\|

*atha dūraṃ gatau kvāpi vane dvijanṛpātmajau \|*  
*gandharvakanyāḥ krīḍaṃtī śataśastāvapaśyatām \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. They went far into the forest. Both of them saw Gandharva maidens in hundreds playing there.

## \|\| 3.7.99 \|\|

*tāḥ sarvāścārusarvāṃgyo viharaṃtyo manoharam \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā dvijātmajo dūrāduvāca nṛpanaṃdanam \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. Seeing from a long distance those comely damsels playing about, the Brāhmaṇa boy spoke to the prince:

## \|\| 3.7.100-103 \|\|

*itaḥ puro na gaṃtavyaṃ viharaṃtyagrataḥ striyaḥ \|*  
*strīsaṃnnidhānaṃ vibudhāstyajaṃti vimalāśayāḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

*etāḥ kaitavakāriṇyo dhanayauvanadurmadāḥ \|*  
*mohayantyo janaṃ dṛṣṭvā vācānunayakovidāḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

*ataḥ parityajettstrīṇāṃ sannidhiṃ sahabhāṣaṇam \|*  
*nija़dharmarato vidvanbrahmacārī viśeṣataḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

*atohaṃ notsahe gantuṃ krīḍāsthānaṃ mṛgīdṛśām \|*  
*ityuktvā dvijaputrastu nivṛtto dūrataḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

100-103a. “Beyond this you should not go. Some females are playing there. Learned men with hearts free from impurities avoid proximity with women. These are proud of their prime of youth. They fraudulently delude the people they see. They are great experts in the art of speaking coaxing words. Hence a scholar engaged in his own duty and particularly a Brahmacārin (religious student) should avoid the proximity of women and conversation with them. Hence I am not enthusiastic to go to the place of sport of these fawn-eyed ones.”

103b. Saying so, the Brāhmaṇa boy returned and stood at a distance.

## \|\| 3.7.104 \|\|

*athāsau rājaputrastu kautukāviṣṭamānasaḥ \|*  
*tāsāṃ vihārapadavīmeka evābhayo yayau \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. But the prince was overcome by curiosity. He fearlessly proceeded towards their sporting ground.

## \|\| 3.7.105 \|\|

*tatra gaṃdharvakanyānāṃ madhye tvekā varānanā \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā'yāṃtaṃ rājaputraṃ ciṃtayāmāsa cetasā \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. Amongst those Gandharva girls, there was a girl of very lovely face. Seeing the prince approaching in her own direction, she thought thus:

## \|\| 3.7.106-107 \|\|

*aho koyamudārāṃgo yuvā sarvāṃgasundaraḥ \|*  
*mattamātaṃga gamano lāvaṇyāmṛtavāridhiḥ \|\| 106 \|\|*

*līlālolaviśālākṣī madhurasmitapeśalaḥ \|*  
*madanopamarūpaśrīḥ sukumārāṃgalakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 107 \|\|*

106-107. ‘Oh, how wonderful! Who is this youth of lovely limbs, handsome in his bodily features? He is walking majestically like an elephant in rut. Verily he is the ocean of the nectar of beauty of form. His eyes are large and tremulously roving. Sweet smile adds to his attractiveness. He can be compared to the god of Love in his glorious form. His body is characterised by tenderness of limbs.’

## \|\| 3.7.108 \|\|

*ityāścaryayutā bālā dūrāddṛṣṭvā nṛpātmajam \|*  
*sarvāḥ sakhīḥ samālokya vacanaṃ cedamabravīt \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. Thinking thus with increasing wonder, on seeing the prince from far, she turned to her friends and spoke these words:

## \|\| 3.7.109-110 \|\|

*ito vidūre he sakhyo vanamastyekamuttamam \|*  
*vicitracaṃpakāśokapunnāgabakulairyutam \|\| 109 \|\|*

*tatra gatvā vanaṃ sarvāḥ saṃcīya kusumotkaram \|*  
*bhavatyaḥ punarāyāṃtu tāvattiṣṭhāmyahaṃ tviha \|\| 110 \|\|*

109-110. “Dear friends, a little away from this place there is an excellent forest full of Campaka, Aśoka, Punnāga and Bakula trees of various sorts. All of you go to that forest and gather flowers. I shall wait for you here till you return.”

## \|\| 3.7.111 \|\|

*ityādiṣṭaḥ sakhīvargo jagāma vipināṃtaram \|*  
*sāpi gaṃdharvajā tasthau nyastadṛṣṭirnṛpātmaje \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. On being commanded thus, the friends proceeded towards the other forest. With her eyes fixed on the prince, the Gandharva girl stood there waiting.

## \|\| 3.7.112-113 \|\|

*tāṃ samālokya tanvaṃgīṃ navayauvanaśālinīm \|*  
*bālāṃ svarūpasaṃpattyā paraiिbhūtatilottamām \|\| 112 \|\|*

*rājaputraḥ samāgamya kautukotphullalocanaḥ \|*  
*avāpa daivayogena madanasya śaravyathām \|\| 113 \|\|*

112-113. On seeing that girl of tender limbs blooming in the prime of her youth far excelling Tilottamā in the richness of beautiful form, the prince stared at her with curiosity. As luck would have it, he experienced the pain of the arrows of Madana (the god of Love).

## \|\| 3.7.114 \|\|

*gandharvatanayā sāpi prāptāya nṛpasūnave \|*  
*utthāya tarasā tasmai pradadau pallavāsanam \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. As the prince arrived, the Gandharva girl quickly got up and offered him a seat of tender foliage.

## \|\| 3.7.115-116 \|\|

*kṛtopacāramāsīnaṃ tamāsādya sumadhyamā \|*  
*papraccha tadrūpaguṇairdhvastadhairyākuleṃdriyā \|\| 115 \|\|*

*kastvaṃ kamalapatrākṣa kasmāddeśādihāgataḥ \|*  
*kasya putra iti premṇā pṛṣṭaḥ sarvaṃ nyavedayat \|\| 116 \|\|*

115-116. All her patience and restraint had already gone at the sight of the handsome features of the prince. Her senses were disturbed. Still the slender-waisted girl offered all formalities (of reception). After he was seated, she began to ask him: “Who are you, O lotus-eyed one? From which land have you come? Whose son are you?” On being asked thus lovingly he related to her everything.

## \|\| 3.7.117 \|\|

*vidarbha rājatanayaṃ vidhvastapitṛmātṛkam \|*  
*śatrubhiśca hṛtasthānamātmānaṃ pararāṣṭragam \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. He revealed his identity as the son of the king of Vidarbha orphaned due to the death of both the parents. He told that his original region had been captured by enemies and that he had been compelled to live in a foreign realm.

## \|\| 3.7.118-124 \|\|

*sarvamāvedya bhūyastāṃ papraccha nṛpanaṃdanaḥ \|*  
*kā tvaṃ vāmoru kiṃ cātra kāryaṃ te kasya cātmajā \|\| 118 \|\|*

*kimavadhyāyasi hṛdā kiṃ vā vaktumihecchasi \|*  
*ityuktā sā punaḥ prāha śṛṇu rājeṃdrasattama \|\| 119 \|\|*

*astyeko dravikonāma gaṃdharvāṇāṃ kulāgraṇīḥ \|*  
*tasyāhamasmi tanayā nāmnā cāṃśumatī smṛtā \|\| 120 \|\|*

*tvāmāyāṃtaṃ vilokyāhaṃ tvatsaṃbhāṣaṇa lālasā \|*  
*tyaktvā sakhījanaṃ sarvamekaivāsmi mahāmate \|\| 121 \|\|*

*sarvasaṃgītavidyāsu na matto'nyāsti kācana \|*  
*mama yogena tuṣyaṃti sarvā api surastriyaḥ \|\| 122 \|\|*

*sāhaṃ sarvakalābhijñā jñātasarvajaneṃgitā \|*  
*tavāhamīpsitaṃ vedmi mayi te saṃgataṃ manaḥ \|\| 123 \|\|*

*tathā mamāpi cautsukyaṃ daivena pratipāditam \|*  
*āvayoḥ snehabhedo'tra nābhibhūyāditaḥ param \|\| 124 \|\|*

118-119a. After mentioning everything, the prince asked her in return: “O beautiful girl, who are you? What is the purpose of your being here? Whose daughter are you? What are you thinking in your heart? What do you wish to speak?”

119b-124. On being asked thus, she said: “Listen, O most excellent prince, there is an eminent Gandharva named Dravika. I am his daughter named Aṃśumatī. On seeing you come, I became eagerly desirous of speaking with you. I have sent away all my friends. I am now alone, O highly intelligent one. There is no one who excels me in all musical arts. All the celestial damsels are happy in my company. I am an expert in all fine arts. I am able to understand the innermost workings of everyone. I know what you wish. Your mind has united in love with me. In the same manner my eagerness towards you has been ordained by destiny. Henceforth, there will be no separation between our affections.”

## \|\| 3.7.125 \|\|

*iti saṃbhāṣya tenāśu premṇā gandharvanaṃdinī \|*  
*muktāhāraṃ dadau tasmai svakucāṃtarabhūṣaṇam \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. After speaking to him thus with great love, the Gandharva girl presented him with a pearl necklace that had adorned her breasts.

## \|\| 3.7.126 \|\|

*tamādāyādbhutaṃ hāraṃ sa tasyāḥ praṇayākulaḥ \|*  
*gāḍhaharṣabharotsiktāmidamāha nṛpātmajaḥ \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. Taking that wonderful necklace from her, the love-lorn prince spoke to her as she stood there full of excessive delight:

## \|\| 3.7.127-128 \|\|

*satyamuktaṃ tvayā bhīru tathāpyekaṃ vadāmyaham \|*  
*tyaktarājyasya niḥsvasya kathaṃ me bhavasi priyā \|\| 127 \|\|*

*sā tvaṃ pitṛmatī bālā vilaṃghya pitṛśāsanam \|*  
*svacchaṃdā caraṇaṃ kartuṃ mūḍheva kathamarhasi \|\| 128 \|\|*

127-128. “O timid girl, what you said is true. Still I have something to say. I am a poor prince deprived of my realm. How can you be my beloved? You are a girl with a father to look after you. How can you transgress his instructions? It does not behove you to do as you please like a deluded girl.”

## \|\| 3.7.129-130 \|\|

*iti tasya vacaḥ śrutvā taṃ pratyāha śucismitā \|*  
*astu nāma tathaivāhaṃ kariṣye paśya kautukam \|\| 129 \|\|*

*gaccha svabhavanaṃ kāṃta paraśvaḥ prātareva tu \|*  
*āgaccha punaratraiva kāryamasti ca no mṛṣā \|\| 130 \|\|*

129-130. On hearing these words of the prince, the girl spoke with a pure smile: “Let it be so. I shall do like that. See my fancy. O my lover, go home now. Come back in the morning day-aftertomorrow. Come here itself. This is a serious matter. It is no joke.”

## \|\| 3.7.131 \|\|

*ityuktvā taṃ nṛpasutaṃ sā saṃgatasakhījanā \|*  
*apākrāmata cārvaṃgī sa cāpi nṛpanandanaḥ \|\| 131 \|\|*

131\. After saying this to the prince, that comely girl went away in the company of her friends. So did the prince.

## \|\| 3.7.132 \|\|

*sa samabhyetya harṣeṇa dvijaputrasya sannidhim \|*  
*sarvamākhyāya tenaiva sārdhaṃ svabhavanaṃ yayau \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. He approached his friend, the Brāhmaṇa boy, with delight and told him everything. In his company he went home too.

## \|\| 3.7.133 \|\|

*tāṃ ca viprasatīṃ bhūyo harṣayitvā nṛpātmajaḥ \|*  
*paraśvo dvijaputreṇa sārdhaṃ tena vanaṃ yayau \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. The prince delighted the chaste Brāhmaṇa lady (with his story), and went to the forest along with the Brāhmaṇa boy the day after the next day.

## \|\| 3.7.134 \|\|

*sa tayā pūrvanirdiṣṭaṃ sthānaṃ prāpya nṛpātmajaḥ \|*  
*gandharvarājamadrākṣītsvaduhitrā samanvitam \|\| 134 \|\|*

134\. Reaching the place indicated by her before, the prince saw the king of Gandharvas accompanied by his daughter.

## \|\| 3.7.135 \|\|

*sa gaṃdharvapatiḥ prāptāvabhinaṃdya kumārakau \|*  
*upaveśyāsane ramye rājaputramabhāṣata \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. The king of Gandharvas heartily welcomed the boys, and made them sit in a charming seat. He then spoke to the prince:

## \|\| 3.7.136-137 \|\|

*gaṃdharva uvāca \|*  
*rājeṃdraputra pūrvedyuḥ kailāsaṃ gatavānaham \|*  
*tatrāpaśyaṃ mahādevaṃ pārvatyā sahitaṃ prabhum \|\| 136 \|\|*

*āhūya māṃ sa deveśaḥ sarveṣāṃ tridivaukasām \|*  
*sannidhāvāha bhagavānkaruṇāmṛtavāridhiḥ \|\| 137 \|\|*

The Gandharva said:

136-137. O son of an eminent king, yesterday I had been to Kailāsa. There I saw Lord Mahādeva accompanied by Pārvatī. That Lord of Devas called me and in the presence of the heaven-dwellers the Lord, the ocean of sympathy, said:

## \|\| 3.7.138-140 \|\|

*dharmaguptāhvayaḥ kaścidrājaputro'sti bhūtale \|*  
*akiñcano bhraṣṭarājyo hṛtadeśaśca śatrubhiḥ \|\| 138 \|\|*

*sa bālo guruvākyena madarccāyāṃ rataḥ sadā \|*  
*adya tatpitaraḥ sarve māṃ prāptāstatprabhāvataḥ \|\| 139 \|\|*

*tasya tvamapi sāhāyyaṃ kuru gandharvasattama \|*  
*athāsau nijarājyastho hataśatrurbhaviṣyati \|\| 140 \|\|*

138-140. “There is a prince on the earth named Dharmagupta. He is poor. He has been ousted from his kingdom. His realm has been occupied by his enemies. At the instance of his preceptor that boy is always engaged in adoring me. Due to his power all his ancestors attained to me today. O excellent Gandharva, you must help him. Let him be reinstated in his kingdom after killing his enemies.”

## \|\| 3.7.141-142 \|\|

*ityājñapto maheśena saṃprāpto nijamadiram \|*  
*anayā madduhitrā ca bahuśo'bhyarthitastathā \|\| 141 \|\|*

*jñātvemaṃ sakalaṃ śaṃbhorniyogaṃ karuṇātmanaḥ \|*  
*ādāyemāṃ duhitaraṃ prāpto'smīdaṃ vanāṃtaram \|\| 142 \|\|*

141-142. On being commanded thus by Maheśa, I returned to my palace. I have been repeatedly requested by my daughter too. Realizing that all these things constitute the will and command of Śaṃbhu, the compassionate one, I have hence taken my daughter and come to this forest.

## \|\| 3.7.143 \|\|

*ata enāṃ prayacchāmi kanyāmaṃśumatīṃ tava \|*  
*hatvā śatrūnsvarāṣṭe tvāṃ sthāpayāmi śivājñayā \|\| 143 \|\|*

143\. I am now giving my daughter Aṃśumatī to you. After killing your enemies, I shall establish you in your own kingdom at the behest of Śiva.

## \|\| 3.7.144 \|\|

*tasminpure tvamanayā bhuktvā bhogānyathepsitān \|*  
*daśavarṣasahasrānte gantāsi giriśālayam \|\| 44 \|\|*

144\. You shall enjoy all pleasures in that city along with this my daughter. At the end of ten thousand years, you will go to Śiva’s abode.

## \|\| 3.7.145 \|\|

*tatrāpi mama kanyeyaṃ tvāmeva pratipatsyate \|*  
*anenaiva svadehena divyena śivasannidhau \|\| 145 \|\|*

145\. There too my daughter will rejoin you with this very divine body in the presence of Śiva.

## \|\| 3.7.146 \|\|

*iti gandharvarājastamābhāṣya nṛpanandanam \|*  
*tasminvane svaduhituḥ pāṇigrahamakārayat \|\| 146 \|\|*

146\. Addressing the prince thus, the king of Gandharvas gave his daughter in marriage to him.

## \|\| 3.7.147-148 \|\|

*pāribarhamadāttasmai ratnabhārānmahojjvalān \|*  
*cūḍāmaṇiṃ candranibhaṃ muktāhārāṃśca bhāsurān \|\| 147 \|\|*

*divyālaṃkāravāsāṃsi kārttasvaraparicchadān \|*  
*gajānāmayutaṃ bhūyo niyutaṃ nīlavājinām \|\| 148 \|\|*

147-148. He gave as present dazzlingly brilliant jewels in plenty, a crest-jewel resembling the moon, shining pearl necklaces, divine ornaments and garments, gold utensils, ten thousand elephants and hundred thousand blue horses.

## \|\| 3.7.149 \|\|

*syandanānāṃ sahasrāṇi sauvarṇāni mahāṃti ca \|*  
*punarekaṃ rathaṃ divyaṃ dhanuścendrāyudhopamam \|\| 149 \|\|*

149\. He gave him thousands of chariots made of gold and very huge in size. (He gave him) a divine chariot also and a bow too comparable to Indra’s weapon.

## \|\| 3.7.150 \|\|

*astrāṇāṃ ca sahasrāṇi tūṇī cākṣayyasāyakau \|*  
*abhedyaṃ varma sauvarṇaṃ śaktiṃ ca ripumardinīm \|\| 150 \|\|*

150\. He gave him thousands of miraculous weapons, two quivers with inexhaustible supply of arrows, an unbreakable golden shield and a Śakti (javelin) that could devastate enemies.

## \|\| 3.7.151 \|\|

*duhituḥ paricaryārthaṃ dāsīpañcasahasrakam \|*  
*dadau prītamanāstasmai dhanāni vividhāni ca \|\| 151 \|\|*

151\. In order to attend upon his daughter, he gladly gave five thousand slave-girls and wealth of different types.

## \|\| 3.7.152 \|\|

*gaṃdharvasainyamatyugraṃ caturaṃgasamamanvitam \|*  
*punaśca tatsahāyārthe gandharvādhipatirdadau \|\| 152 \|\|*

152\. In order to help him, the king of Gandharvas gave him a formidable army of Gandharvas with all the four conventional divisions.

## \|\| 3.7.153 \|\|

*itthaṃ rājendratanayaḥ saṃprāptaḥ śriyamuttamām \|*  
*abhīṣṭajāyāsahito mumude nijasaṃpadā \|\| 153 \|\|*

153\. Thus the son of the eminent king attained excellent glory. Accompanied by a loving and lovable wife, he rejoiced with his wealth.

## \|\| 3.7.154 \|\|

*kārayitvā svaduhiturvivāhaṃ samayocitam \|*  
*yayau vimānamāruhya gaṃdharvādhipatirdivam \|\| 154 \|\|*

154\. After celebrating the marriage of his daughter at the proper time, the king of Gandharvas ascended an aerial chariot and went to heaven.

## \|\| 3.7.155 \|\|

*dharmaguptaḥ kṛtodvāhaḥ saha gaṃdharvasenayā \|*  
*punaḥ svanagaraṃ prāpya jaghāna ripuvāhinīm \|\| 155 \|\|*

155\. After his marriage Dharmagupta went to his city again accompanied by the army of Gandharvas and killed the army of the enemies.

## \|\| 3.7.156 \|\|

*durdharṣaṇaṃ raṇe hatvā śaktyā gaṃdharvasenayā \|*  
*niḥ śeṣitārātibalaḥ praviveśa nijaṃ puram \|\| 156 \|\|*

156\. After killing Durdharṣaṇa in battle by means of Śakti, and with the help of the Gandharva army, he annihilated the armies of his enemy and entered his own city.

## \|\| 3.7.157 \|\|

*tatobhiṣiktaḥ sacivairbrāhmaṇaiśca mahottamaiḥ \|*  
*ratnasiṃhāsanārūḍhaścakre rājyamakaṇṭakam \|\| 157 \|\|*

157\. Then he was crowned by the ministers and excellent Brāhmaṇas. Seated on a gemset throne, he ruled the kingdom free from thorns (enemies).

## \|\| 3.7.158 \|\|

*yā vipravanitā pūrvaṃ tamapuṣṇātsvaputravat \|*  
*saiva mātābhavattasya sa bhrātā dvijanandanaḥ \|\| 158 \|\|*

158\. The Brāhmaṇa lady who had looked after and brought him up like her own son, continued to be his mother and the Brāhmaṇa boy his own brother.

## \|\| 3.7.159 \|\|

*gaṃdharvatanayā jāyā vidarbhanagareśvaraḥ \|*  
*ārādhya devaṃ giriśaṃ dharmagupto nṛpo'bhavat \|\| 159 \|\|*

159\. His wife was the daughter of Gandharva. Thus the lord of Vidarbha propitiated Lord Giriśa and became king by the name Dharmagupta.

## \|\| 3.7.160 \|\|

*evamanye samārādhya pradoṣe girijāpatim \|*  
*labhaṃtebhīpsitānkāmāndehāṃte tu parāṃ gatim \|\| 160 \|\|*

160\. Thus others too, by propitiating the Lord of the Daughter of the Mountain at the time of Pradoṣa, acquire desired objects and attain salvation on death.

## \|\| 3.7.161 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*etanmahāvrataṃ puṇyaṃ pradoṣe śaṃkarārcanam \|*  
*dharmārthakāmamokṣāṇāṃ yadetatsādhanaṃ param \|\| 161 \|\|*

Sūta said:

161\. This is a great meritorious act of devotion—the worship of Śaṅkara at the time of Pradoṣa. It is the greatest means of attaining moral excellence, wealth, worldly enjoyment and salvation.

## \|\| 3.7.162-164 \|\|

*ya etacchṛṇuyātpuṇyaṃ māhātmyaṃ paramādbhutam \|*  
*pradoṣe śivapūjāṃte kathayedvā samāhitaḥ \|\| 162 \|\|*

*bhavenna tasya dāridryaṃ janmāntaraśateṣvapi \|*  
*jñānaiśvaryasamāyuktaḥ sonte śivapuraṃ vrajet \|\| 163 \|\|*

*ye prāpya durlabhataraṃ manujāḥ śarīraṃ kurvaṃti haṃta parameśvarapādapūjām \|*  
*dhanyāsta eva nijapuṇyajitatrilokāsteṣāṃ padāṃbujarajo bhuvanaṃ punāti \|\| 164 \|\|*

162-164. If anyone listens to this meritorious, extremely wonderful greatness of Pradoṣa, or narrates it with mental and physical purity at the end of the worship, at the time of Pradoṣa, he will never be tormented by poverty in the course of hundreds of births. Endowed with knowledge and prosperity, he will go to Śiva’s city at the end.

After attaining the very rare human body those who perform the worship of the feet of Parameśvara are really blessed. They have conquered the three worlds by means of their own merit. The dust of their lotus-like feet sanctifies the entire universe.

## Chapter 8 - The Religious Vow to be Observed on Mondays: The Story of Sīmantinī

## \|\| 3.8.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*nityānaṃdamayaṃ śāṃtaṃ nirvikalpaṃ nirāmayam \|*  
*śivatattvamanādyaṃtaṃ ye viduste paraṃ gatāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: The chapter illustrates the efficacy of this Vrata by the story of Sīmantinī’s restoration to Saubhāgya by fasting etc. on Mondays.

Sūta said:

1\. Those who know the truth called ‘Śiva’, who is eternal bliss, quiescent, devoid of doubts, free from ailments, and bereft of beginning and end, have reached the highest state.

## \|\| 3.8.2 \|\|

*viraktāḥ kāmabhogebhyo ye prakurvaṃtyahaitukīm \|*  
*bhaktiṃ parāṃ śive dhīrāsteṣāṃ muktirna saṃsṛtiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Those who have no worldly entanglement, those who are free from attachment to the enjoyment of worldly pleasures and lustful pursuits, those who have devotion to Śiva with no ulterior motive, are the wise ones. They attain salvation.

## \|\| 3.8.3 \|\|

*viṣayānabhisaṃdhāya ye kurvaṃti śive ratim \|*  
*viṣayairnābhibhūyaṃte bhuṃjānāstatphalānyapi \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Those who direct their love towards Śiva even with the worldly pleasures in their mind, are not adversely affected by those worldly pursuits, even as they enjoy their benefits.

## \|\| 3.8.4 \|\|

*yena kenāpi bhāvena śivabhaktiyuto naraḥ \|*  
*na vinaśyati kālena sa yāti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. A man endowed with devotion to Śiva, irrespective of the motive thereof, does not perish. He attains the greatest goal in due course.

## \|\| 3.8.5 \|\|

*ārurukṣuḥ paraṃ sthānaṃ viṣayāsaktamānasaḥ \|*  
*pūjayetkarmaṇā śaṃbhuṃ bhogāṃte śivamāpnuyāt \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Desirous of ascending the highest region, a man attracted mentally to worldly pleasures, should worship Śaṃbhu along with regular activities. When the enjoyment of pleasures ends, he shall attain Śiva.

## \|\| 3.8.6 \|\|

*aśaktaḥ kaścidutsraṣṭuṃ prāyo viṣayavāsanām \|*  
*ataḥ karmamayī pūjā kāmadhenuḥ śarīriṇām \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Generally no one is capable of renouncing entirely the keenness to enjoy worldly pleasures. Hence, the adoration in happy combination with regular activities, acts as the very wish-yielding divine cow unto all embodied beings.

## \|\| 3.8.7 \|\|

*māyāmayepi saṃsāre ye vihṛtya ciraṃ sukham \|*  
*muktimicchanti dehāṃte teṣāṃ dharmoyamīritaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. This is the religious duty ordained for those who seek salvation at the end of the mortal body, after enjoying happiness for a long time, sporting about in the world, albeit, it is a creation of the illusive Māyā.

## \|\| 3.8.8 \|\|

*śivapūjā sadā loke hetuḥ svargāpavargayoḥ \|*  
*somavāre viśeṣeṇa pradoṣādiguṇānvite \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The worship of Śiva is always the cause of heavenly pleasures as well as absolute salvation, particularly when it is performed on Mondays associated with Praḍoṣa and such other auspicious occasions.

## \|\| 3.8.9 \|\|

*kevalenāpi ye kuryuḥ somavāre śivārcanam \|*  
*na teṣāṃ vidyate kiṃcidihāmutra ca durlabham \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Nothing is difficult of access here and hereafter to those who perform the adoration of Śiva even on ordinary Mondays.

## \|\| 3.8.10 \|\|

*upoṣitaḥ śucirbhūtvā somavāre jiteṃdriyaḥ \|*  
*vaidikairlaukikairvāpi vidhivatpūjayecchivam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The devotee should restrain all sense-organs, observe fast and be perfectly pure on Monday and duly worship Śiva by means of Vedic hymns or ordinary prayers.

## \|\| 3.8.11 \|\|

*brahmacārī gṛhastho vā kanyā vāpi sabharttṛkā \|*  
*vibhartṛkā vā saṃpūjya labhate varamīpsitam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. A religious student or a householder, a virgin or a married girl or even a widow obtains the desired boon by worshipping Śiva.

## \|\| 3.8.12 \|\|

*atrāhaṃ kathayiṣyāmi kathāṃ śrotṛmanoharām \|*  
*śrutvā muktiṃ prayāṃtyeva bhartirbhavati śāṃbhavī \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. In this context I shall narrate a story that delights all those who listen to (it). On hearing this attentively they will have devotion to Śaṃbhu engendered in them and will attain salvation.

## \|\| 3.8.13 \|\|

*āryāvarte nṛpaḥ kaścidāsīddharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ \|*  
*citravarmeti vikhyāto dharmarājo durātmanām \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. In Āryāvarta there was a certain king well-known as Citravarmā. He was the foremost among those who had pious pursuits. He was Dharmarāja (god of Death) unto all the wicked ones.

## \|\| 3.8.14 \|\|

*sa goptā dharmasetūnāṃ śāstā duṣpathagāminām \|*  
*yaṣṭā samastayajñānāṃ trātā śaraṇamicchatām \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. He was a protector of all religious institutions, chastiser of those who take to the evil path, performer of all types of Yajñas and saviour of those who seek refuge.

## \|\| 3.8.15 \|\|

*karttā sakalapuṇyānāṃ dātā sakalasaṃpadām \|*  
*jetā sapatnavṛṃdānāṃ bhaktaḥ śivamukundayoḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. He scrupulously and regularly performed all meritorious deeds; he gifted away all sorts of riches; he vanquished hosts of enemies; he was a devotee of Śiva and Mukunda (i.e. Viṣṇu).

## \|\| 3.8.16 \|\|

*sonukūlāsu patnīṣu labdhvā putrānmahaujasaḥ \|*  
*cireṇa prārthitāṃ lebhe kanyāmekāṃ varānanām \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. He begot powerfully brilliant sons of his wives faithful and favourably disposed towards him, and after a long time, a girl of excellent countenance, eagerly awaited for a long time.

## \|\| 3.8.17 \|\|

*sa labdhvā tanayāṃ diṣṭyā himavāniva pārvatīm \|*  
*ātmānaṃ devasadṛśaṃ mene pūrṇamanoratham \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. After luckily getting a daughter in the same way as Himavān got Pārvatī, he considered himself on a par with the Devas, one whose desires were fulfilled.

## \|\| 3.8.18 \|\|

*sa ekadā jātakalakṣaṇajñānāhūya sādhūndvijamukhyavṛṃdān \|*  
*kutūhalenābhiniviṣṭacetāḥ papraccha kanyājanane phalāni \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Once he invited a good many excellent Brāhmaṇas conversant with the (astrological) characteristics of the newly born and prompted by curiosity asked them about the (future) events associated with the nativity of his daughter.

## \|\| 3.8.19-22 \|\|

*atha tatrābravīdeko bahujño dvijasattamaḥ \|*  
*eṣā sīmaṃtinī nāmnā kanyā tava mahīpate \|\| 19 \|\|*

*umeva māṃgalyavatī damayaṃtīva rūpiṇī \|*  
*bhāratīva kalābhijñā lakṣmīriva mahāguṇā \|\| 20 \|\|*

*suprajā devamāteva jānakīva dhṛtavratā \|*  
*raviprabheva satkāṃtiścaṃdrikeva manoramā \|\| 21 \|\|*

*daśavarṣasahasrāṇi saha bhartrā pramodate \|*  
*prasūya tanayānaṣṭau paraṃ sukhamavāpsyati \|\| 22 \|\|*

19-22. An excellent Brāhmaṇa among them, deep in knowledge, spoke thus: “This daughter of yours, O king, Sīmantinī by name, shall have everything auspicious and splendid like Umā; she will be having the beauty of form like Damayantī; conversant with all fine arts like Goddess Sarasvatī and endowed with greatly auspicious qualities like Lakṣmī. Like the mother of Devas, she will have excellent progeny; be steadfast in vows and observances like the daughter of Janaka; brilliant with excellent lustre like solar splendour and charming like moonlight. She will rejoice in the company of her husband for ten thousand years. She will beget eight sons and attain great happiness.”

## \|\| 3.8.23 \|\|

*ityuktavaṃtaṃ nṛpatirdhanaiḥ saṃpūjya taṃ dvijam \|*  
*avāpa paramāṃ prītiṃ tadvāgamṛtasevayā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The king honoured with monetary gifts the Brāhmaṇa who spoke thus and had the greatest pleasure by imbibing the nectar of his sweet words.

## \|\| 3.8.24 \|\|

*athānyo'pi dvijaḥ prāha dhairyavānamitadyutiḥ \|*  
*eṣā caturdaśe varṣe vaidhavyaṃ pratipatsyati \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Another bold Brāhmaṇa of unmeasured splendour said: “In her fourteenth year she will be faced with widowhood.”

## \|\| 3.8.25 \|\|

*ityākarṇya vacastasya vajranirghātaniṣṭhuram \|*  
*muhūrtamabhavadrājā ciṃtāvyākulamānasaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. On hearing these words, cruel like a stroke of thunderbolt, the king became excessively agitated in his mind for a while.

## \|\| 3.8.26 \|\|

*atha sarvānsamutsṛjya brāhmaṇānbrahmavatsalaḥ \|*  
*sarvaṃ daivakṛtaṃ mattvā niściṃtaḥ pārthivo'bhavat \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. All the Brāhmaṇas were sent off by the king who was favourable and friendly to them. Considering that everything was the handiwork of adverse fate, the king became free from anxiety.

## \|\| 3.8.27 \|\|

*sāpi sīmaṃtinī bālā krameṇa gataśaiśavā \|*  
*vaidhavyamātmano bhāvi śuśrāvātmasakhīmukhāt \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The girl Sīmantinī passed the stage of childhood. From one of her friends she heard about her destined widowhood.

## \|\| 3.8.28 \|\|

*paraṃ nirvedamāpannā ciṃtayāmāsa bālikā \|*  
*yājñavalkyamuneḥ patnīṃ maitreyīṃ paryapṛcchata \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. She was extremely disappointed. She became anxious. She approached Maitreyī, the wife of Sage Yājñavalkya, and asked:

## \|\| 3.8.29 \|\|

*mātastvaccaraṇāṃbhojaṃ prapannāsmi bhayākulā \|*  
*saubhāgyavardhanaṃ karma mama śaṃsitumarhasi \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. “O mother, I am extremely frightened and have sought refuge in your lotus-like feet. It behoves you to suggest some rite that will enhance my Saubhāgya (conjugal felicity).”

## \|\| 3.8.30 \|\|

*iti prapannāṃ nṛpateḥ kanyāṃ prāha muneḥ satī \|*  
*śaraṇaṃ vraja tanvaṃgi pārvatīṃ śivasaṃyutām \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Thus, when the princess sought refuge in her, the chaste wife of the sage spoke to her: “O lady of tender limbs, seek refuge in Pārvath in the company of Śiva.

## \|\| 3.8.31-33 \|\|

*somavāre śivaṃ gaurīṃ pūjayasva samāhitā \|*  
*upoṣitā vā susnātā virajāmbaradhāriṇī \|\| 31 \|\|*

*yatavāṅniścalamanāḥ pūjāṃ kṛtvā yathocitām \|*  
*brāhmaṇānbhojayitvātha śivaṃ samyakprasādayat \|\| 32 \|\|*

*pāpakṣayo'bhiṣekeṇa sāmrājyaṃ pīṭhapūjanāt \|*  
*saubhāgyamakhilaṃ saukhyaṃ gaṃdhamālyākṣatārpaṇāt \|\| 33 \|\|*

31-33. With mental and bodily purity, worship Śiva and Gaurī on Mondays. Observe fast, after taking the holy ablution and wearing dust-free (clean) garments. With steady mind and restrained speech, perform the befitting adoration, feed Brāhmaṇas and propitiate Śiva ardently.

By bathing (the Śiva Liṅga) there will be destruction of sins; by worshipping the pedestal one can gain an empire; by offering sweet scents, garlands and raw rice, one shall get complete happiness and conjugal bliss.

## \|\| 3.8.34 \|\|

*dhūpadānena saugaṃdhyaṃ kāṃtirdīpapradānataḥ \|*  
*naivedyaiśca mahābhogo lakṣmīstāṃbūladānataḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. By offering incense one will get sweet odour; by offering lamps one will get brilliance; by offering foodstuffs one shall get enjoyment of pleasures; by offering betel leaves one will have prosperity.

## \|\| 3.8.35 \|\|

*dharmārthakāmamokṣāśca namaskārapradānataḥ \|*  
*aṣṭaiśvaryādisiddhīnāṃ japa eva hi kāraṇam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. By offering obeisance one gets religious merit, wealth, worldly pleasures and salvation. Japa alone is the cause of the achievement of the eight kinds of supernatural powers.

## \|\| 3.8.36 \|\|

*homena sarvakāmānāṃ samṛddhirupajāyate \|*  
*sarveṣāmeva devānāṃ tuṣṭirbrāhmaṇabhojanāt \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. By performing Homa one will have increased realization of all cherished desires. By feeding Brāhmaṇas all the Devas will be propitiated.

## \|\| 3.8.37 \|\|

*itthamārādhaya śivaṃ somavāre śivāmapi \|*  
*atyāpadamapi prāptā nistīrṇābhibhavā bhaveḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Thus on Mondays propitiate Śiva and Śivā also. Even if you were to face great adversity, you will be absolutely free.

## \|\| 3.8.38 \|\|

*ghorādghoraṃ prapannāpi mahākleśaṃ bhayānakam \|*  
*śivapūjāprabhāveṇa tariṣyasi mahadbhayam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Even if you find yourself involved in the most terrible distress, you will cross the great danger by the power of the adoration of Śiva.”

## \|\| 3.8.39 \|\|

*itthaṃ sīmaṃtinīṃ samyaganuśāsya punaḥ satī \|*  
*yayau sāpi varārohā rājaputrī tathā'karot \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. After adominishing\[?\] and instructing Sīmantī thus, the chaste (wife of the sage) went away. The princess of great beauty did so (as she was advised).

## \|\| 3.8.40 \|\|

*damayaṃtyāṃ nalasyāsīdiṃdrasenābhidhaḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*tasya caṃdrāṃgado nāma putrobhū ccaṃdrasannibhaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Nala begot of Damayantī a son named Indrasena. He had a son named Candrāṅgada and he resembled the moon.

## \|\| 3.8.41 \|\|

*citravarmā nṛpaśreṣṭhastamāhūya nṛpātmajam \|*  
*kanyāṃ sīmaṃtinīṃ tasmai prāyacchadgurvanujñayā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. At the instance of his preceptor, the excellent king Citravarmā invited that prince and gave his daughter Sīmantinī in marriage to him.

## \|\| 3.8.42 \|\|

*so'bhūnmahotsavastatra tasyā udvāhakarmaṇi \|*  
*yatra sarvamahīpānāṃ samavāyo mahānabhūt \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. There were great festivities at the time of the celebration of her marriage. There was a great gathering of all kings at the time.

## \|\| 3.8.43 \|\|

*tasyāḥ pāṇigrahaṃ kāle kṛtvā caṃdrāṃgadaḥ kṛtī \|*  
*uvāsa katicinmāsāṃstatraiva śvaśurālaye \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. After the marriage, the satisfied Candrāṅgada spent a few months in the abode of his father-in-law.

## \|\| 3.8.44 \|\|

*ekadā yamunāṃ tartuṃ sa rājatanayo balī \|*  
*āruroha tarīṃ kaiścidvayasyaiḥ saha līlayā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Once the prince wanted to cross Yamunā. The mighty prince sportingly got on to a boat along with some of his friends.

## \|\| 3.8.45 \|\|

*tasmiṃstarati kāliṃdīṃ rājaputre vidhervaśāt \|*  
*mamajja saha kaivatairāvarttābhihatā tarī \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. While the prince was crossing Kālindī (Yamunā), the boat got caught up into a whirlpool and it drowned along with the boatmen.

## \|\| 3.8.46 \|\|

*hā heti śabdaḥ sumahānāsīttasyāstaṭadvaye \|*  
*paśyatāṃ sarvasainyānāṃ pralāpo divama spṛśat \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. There was a loud cry of lamentation on both the banks. The wailing of the soldiers who were watching the accident rose up to the sky.

## \|\| 3.8.47 \|\|

*majjaṃto mamrire kecitkecidgrāhodaraṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*rājaputrādayaḥ kecinnādṛśyaṃta mahājale \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Some were drowned. Some were swallowed by crocodiles. The prince and some others disappeared in the great expanse of water.

## \|\| 3.8.48 \|\|

*tadupaśrutya rājāpi citravarmātivi hvalaḥ \|*  
*yamunāyāstaṭaṃ prāpya viceṣṭaḥ samajāyata \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. On hearing about it, King Citravarmā became bewildered and stunned. He came to the banks of Yamunā and became (unconscious and) motionless.

## \|\| 3.8.49 \|\|

*śrutvātha rājapatnyaśca vabhūburgatacetanāḥ \|*  
*sā ca sīmaṃtinī śrutvā papāpa ḍūvi mūrcchitā \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. On hearing about this, the wives of the king swooned and fell. Sīmantinī too fainted and fell down on the ground.

## \|\| 3.8.50 \|\|

*tathānye maṃtrimukhyāśca nāyakāḥ sapurohitāḥ \|*  
*vihvalāḥ śokasaṃtaptā vilepurmuktamūrdhajāḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Others too, the chief ministers, the ladies and the preceptors became worried and dismayed. With hairs dishevelled, they wailed and shouted.

## \|\| 3.8.51 \|\|

*iṃdrasenopi rājedraḥ putravārttāṃ suduḥkhitaḥ \|*  
*ākarṇya saha patnībhirnaṣṭasaṃjñaḥ papāta ha \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. On hearing it, the eminent king Indrasena became miserable for the accident that befell his son. He lost sense and fell down along with his queens.

## \|\| 3.8.52 \|\|

*tanmaṃtriṇaśca tatpaurāstathā taddeśavāsinaḥ \|*  
*ābālavṛddhavanitāścukruśuḥ śokavihvalāḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. His ministers, his citizens, the inhabitants of his realm including children, women and old men became grief-stricken and lamented.

## \|\| 3.8.53 \|\|

*śokātkeciduro jaghnuḥ śiro jaghnuśca kecana \|*  
*hā rājaputra hā tāta kvāsi kvāsīti babhramuḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Some beat their chests out of grief. Some hit their own heads. “Alas! O Prince! O dear one, where are you?” Saying thus, they wandered here and there.

## \|\| 3.8.54 \|\|

*evaṃ śokākulaṃ dīnamiṃdrasenamahīpateḥ \|*  
*nagaraṃ sahasā kṣubdhaṃ citravarmapuraṃ tathā \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Thus the city of King Indrasena and that of Citravarmā became agitated all of a sudden, involved as they were in the wretched state of grief.

## \|\| 3.8.55 \|\|

*atha vṛddhaiḥ samāśvastaścitravarmā mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*śanairnagaramāgatya sāntvayāmāsa cātmajām \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Consoled by elderly people, King Citravarmā slowly returned to the city and tried to console his daughter.

## \|\| 3.8.56 \|\|

*sa rājāṃbhasimagnasya jāmātustasya bāṃdhavaiḥ \|*  
*āgataiḥ kārayāmāsa sākalyādaurdhvadaihikam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. With the help of the kinsmen who had come, the king performed all the obsequies of his son-in-law who was drowned.

## \|\| 3.8.57 \|\|

*sā ca sīmaṃtinī sādhvī bhartṛlokamatiḥ satī \|*  
*pitrā niṣiddhā snehena vaidhavyaṃ pratyapadyata \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. The chaste lady Sīmantinī was at first thinking of going to the region where her husband had gone. But out of love, her father prevented her. Hence she resigned herself to the widowhood.

## \|\| 3.8.58 \|\|

*muneḥ patnyo'padiṣṭaṃ yatsomavāravrataṃ śubham \|*  
*na tatyāja śubhācārā vaidhavyaṃ prāptavatyapi \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Despite the fact that she had become a widow, the princess of splendid behaviour did not abandon the excellent Monday Vrata (holy observance) as instructed by the wife of the Sage.

## \|\| 3.8.59 \|\|

*evaṃ caturdaśe varṣe duḥkhaṃ prāpya sudāruṇam \|*  
*dhyāyantī śivapādābjaṃ vatsaratrayamatyagāt \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Thus she faced the terrible misery in her fourteenth year. Meditating on the lotus-like feet of Śiva, she passed three years.

## \|\| 3.8.60 \|\|

*putraśokādivonmattamiṃdrasenaṃ mahīpatim \|*  
*prasahya tasya dāyādāḥ saptāṃgaṃ jahrurojasā \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Already King Indrasena was more or less out of his senses due to the death of his son. Further his kinsmen forcibly occupied his realm consisting of the usual seven constituents.

## \|\| 3.8.61 \|\|

*hṛtasiṃhāsanaḥ śūrairdāyādaiḥ so'prajo nṛpaḥ \|*  
*nigṛhya kārābhavane sapatnīko niveśitaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. The king who had no other progeny was deprived of his throne by his powerful kinsmen. Moreover, he was confined in prison along with his wives.

## \|\| 3.8.62 \|\|

*caṃdrāgado'pi tatputro nimagno yamunājale \|*  
*adhodhomajjamāno'sau dadarśoragakāminīḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. His son Candrāṅgada who had drowned in the waters of Yamunā went deep into the river and saw serpent damsels.

## \|\| 3.8.63 \|\|

*jalakrīḍāsu saktāstā dṛṣṭvā rājakumāra kam \|*  
*vismitāstamatho ninyuḥ pātālaṃ pannagālayam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. They were engaged in aquatic sports. They were surprised on seeing the prince. They then took him to Pātāla, the abode of serpents.

## \|\| 3.8.64 \|\|

*sa nīyamānastarasā pannagībhirnṛpātmajaḥ \|*  
*takṣakasya puraṃ ramyaṃ viveśa paramādbhutam \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Hurriedly led by the serpent maidens, the prince entered the wonderfully beautiful city of Takṣaka.

## \|\| 3.8.65-72 \|\|

*so'paśyadrājatanayo maheṃdrabhavanopamam \|*  
*mahāratnaparibhrājanmayūkhaparidīpitam \|\| 65 \|\|*

*vajravaiḍūryapācādiprāsādaśatasaṃkulam \|*  
*māṇikya gopuradvāraṃ muktādāmabhirujjvalam \|\| 66 \|\|*

*caṃdrakāṃtasthalaṃ ramyaṃ hemadvārakapāṭakam \|*  
*anekaśatasāhasramaṇidīpavirājitam \|\| 67 \|\|*

*tatrāpaśyatsabhā madhye niṣaṇṇaṃ ratnaviṣṭare \|*  
*takṣakaṃ pannagādhīśaṃ phaṇānekaśatojjvalam \|\| 68 \|\|*

*divyāṃbaradharaṃ dīptaṃ ratnakuṇḍalarājitam \|*  
*nānāratnaparikṣiptamukuṭa dyutiraṃjitam \|\| 69 \|\|*

*phaṇāmaṇimayūkhāḍhyairasaṃkhyaiḥ pannagottamaiḥ \|*  
*upāsitaṃ prāṃjalibhiścitraratnavibhūṣitaiḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*rūpayauvanamādhuryavilāsagati śobhinā \|*  
*nāgakanyāsahasreṇa samaṃtātparivāritam \|\| 71 \|\|*

*divyābharaṇadīptāṃgaṃ divyacaṃdanacarcitam \|*  
*kālāgnimiva durdharṣaṃ tejasādityasannibham \|\| 72 \|\|*

65-72. The prince saw that city resembling the abode of Mahendra. It was illuminated by rays issuing from big jewels. There were hundreds of palaces made of diamonds, Lapis lazuli and crystals, with the main gateways made of rubies. They shone with pearl necklaces. The ground was paved with Candrakānta slabs and the doors were made of gold. The brightness was enhanced by thousands of gemset lamps.

There in the midst of his assembly he saw Takṣaka, the king of serpents, seated on a gemset throne. His hundreds of hoods shone brilliantly. He was clad in divine garments. He appeared brilliant with gemset ear-rings. Crowns set with many jewels added to his lustre.

Innumerable excellent serpents who radiated rays from the gems in their hoods and who were themselves adorned with gems, attended on him with palms joined in reverence. He was surrounded by a thousand Nāga maidens remarkably shining with beauty, youth, sweetness, seductive charms and amorous gaits. His limbs glittered with divine ornaments. His body was smeared with divine sandal-paste. He was formidably unassailable like the all-destroying fire at the end of the world. In ḥīs brilliance he vied with the sun.

## \|\| 3.8.73 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā rājasuto dhīraḥ praṇipatya sabhāsthale \|*  
*utthitaḥ prāṃjalistasya tejasākṣiptalocanaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. On seeing him the bold prince bowed down to him in the assembly hall itself. Then he got up and stood with palms joined in reverence. The brilliance (of Takṣaka) dazzled his eyes.

## \|\| 3.8.74 \|\|

*nāgarājopi taṃ dṛṣṭvā rājaputraṃ manoramam \|*  
*ko'yaṃ kasmādihāyāta iti papraccha pannagīḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. On seeing the charming prince, the king of serpents asked the serpent damsels, “Who is this? Where has he come from?”

## \|\| 3.8.75 \|\|

*tā ūcuryamunātoye dṛṣṭo'smābhiryadṛcchayā \|*  
*ajñātakulanāmāyamānītastava sannidhim \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. They said: “He was by chance seen by us in the waters of Yamunā. We do not know his name or family. He has been brought into your presence as he is.”

## \|\| 3.8.76 \|\|

*atha pṛṣṭo rājaputrastakṣakeṇa mahātmanā \|*  
*kasyāsi tanayaḥ kastvaṃ ko deśaḥ kathamāgataḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. The prince was then asked by the noble-souled Takṣaka: “Who are you? Whose son? What is your native land? How did you happen to come here?”

## \|\| 3.8.77 \|\|

*rājaputro vacaḥ śrutvā takṣakaṃ vākyamabravīt \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Hearing his words the prince said:

## \|\| 3.8.78-81 \|\|

*rājaputra uvāca \|*  
*asti bhūmaṃḍale kaściddeśo niṣadhasaṃjñakaḥ \|*  
*tasyādhipo'bhavadrājā nalo nāma mahā yaśāḥ \|*  
*sa puṇyakīrtiḥ kṣitipo damayantīpatiḥ śubhaḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

*tasmādapīṃdrasenākhyastasya putro mahābalaḥ \|*  
*caṃdrāṃgadosmi nāmnāhaṃ navoḍhaḥ śvaśurālaye \|*  
*viharanyamunātoye nimagno devacoditaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

*etābhiḥ pannagastrībhirānītosmi tavāṃtikam \|*  
*dṛṣṭvāhaṃ tava pādābjaṃ puṇyairjanmāṃtarārjitaiḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

*adya dhanyo'smi dhanyo'smi kṛtārtho pitarau mama \|*  
*yatprekṣito'haṃ kāruṇyāttvayā saṃbhāṣitopi ca \|\| 81 \|\|*

The Prince said:

78-81. There is on the earth a kingdom named Niṣadha. A famous king named Nala ruled it. That king of meritorious renown was the splendid husband of Damayantī. A son of great might was born of him named Indrasena. I am his son named Candrāṅgada. Soon after marriage, I was staying in my father-in-law’s abode. While sporting about in the water of Yamunā, I got drowned as was destined. I have now been brought near you by these serpent damsels, that I could see your lotus-like feet. I am blessed; I am blessed today. My parents also are blessed, because I was seen and talked to by you out of pity.

## \|\| 3.8.82 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ityudāramasaṃbhrāṃtaṃ vacaḥ śrutvātipeśalam \|*  
*takṣakaḥ punarautsukyādbabhāṣe rājanaṃdanam \|\| 82 \|\|*

Sūta said:

82\. On hearing these exquisite, unflurried, pleasing words, Takṣaka was prompted by curiosity and he asked the prince:

## \|\| 3.8.83 \|\|

*takṣaka uvāca \|*  
*bhobho nareṃdradāyāda mā bhaiṣīrdhīratāṃ vraja \|*  
*sarvadeveṣu ko devo yuṣmābhiḥ pūjyate sadā \|\| 83 \|\|*

Takṣaka said:

83\. O scion of the family of a king, do not be afraid. Be bold. Among all the Devas which Deva is always worshipped by you?

## \|\| 3.8.84 \|\|

*rājaputra uvāca \|*  
*yo devaḥ sarvedeveṣu mahādevaṃ iti smṛtaḥ \|*  
*pūjyate sa hi viśvātmā śivo'smābhirumāpatiḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

The prince said:

84\. The Lord who is remembered as Mahādeva among all the Devas, that cosmic-souled Śiva, the consort of Umā, is worshipped by us.

## \|\| 3.8.85 \|\|

*yasya tejoṃśaleśena rajasā ca prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*kṛtarūpo'sṛjadviśvaṃ sa naḥ pūjyo maheśvaraḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. That Maheśvara is worthy of our adoration, with whose modicum of brilliance, named Rajas, has been evolved the lord of subjects i.e. Brahmā and with the very same thing, he created this universe.

## \|\| 3.8.86 \|\|

*yasyāṃśātsāttvikaṃ divyaṃ bibhradviṣṇuḥ sanātanaḥ \|*  
*viśvaṃ bibhartti bhūtātmā śivo'smābhiḥ sa pūjyate \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. That Śiva from whose parts the eternal Viṣṇu possessed the divine quality of Sattva and is able to sustain the universe as the Bhūtātmā (‘Immanent soul of all living beings’), is worshipped by us.

## \|\| 3.8.87 \|\|

*yasyāṃśāttāmasājjāto rudraḥ kālāgnisannibhaḥ \|*  
*viśvametaddharatyaṃte sa pūjyo'smābhirīśvaraḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. That Īśvara from whose Tāmasa part was born Rudra who is like deadly fire and who annihilates this universe, is worthy of being worshipped.

## \|\| 3.8.88 \|\|

*yo vidhātā vidhātuśca kāraṇasyāpi kāraṇam \|*  
*tejasāṃ paramaṃ tejaḥ sa śivo naḥ parā gatiḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. The Śiva is our ultimate goal, who is the creator of Creator Brahmā, the cause of all causes and the greatest refulgence of all refulgent luminaries.

## \|\| 3.8.89 \|\|

*yoṃtikastho'pi dūrasthaḥ pāpopahṛtacetasām \|*  
*aparicchedya dhāmāsau śivo naḥ paramā gatiḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. That Śiva is our greatest goal who, though existing very near, appears to be far off unto those whose minds are affected by sins, and whose power is unlimited.

## \|\| 3.8.90 \|\|

*yo'gnau tiṣṭhati yo bhūmau yo vāyau salile ca yaḥ \|*  
*ya ākāśe ca viśvātmā sa pūjyo naḥ sadāśivaḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. That cosmic-souled Sadāśiva is worthy of being worshipped by us, who abides in the elements such as Fire, Earth, Wind, Water and Ether.

## \|\| 3.8.91 \|\|

*yaḥ sākṣī sarvabhūtānāṃ ya ātmastho niraṃjanaḥ \|*  
*yasyecchāvaśago lokaḥ so'smābhiḥ pūjyate śivaḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. That Śiva is being worshipped by us who is the eternal witness unto all living beings, is immanent in the soul as the unsullied one, and whose will controls the world.

## \|\| 3.8.92 \|\|

*yamekamādyaṃ puruṣaṃ purāṇaṃ vadaṃti bhinnaṃ guṇavaikṛtena \|*  
*kṣetrajñameketha turīyamanye kūṭasthamanye sa śivo gatirnaḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. That Śiva is our goal, whom they speak of as the (only) one, ancient, primordial Puruṣa, untouched by the aberrations of the Guṇas, whom some call Kṣetrajña (‘knower of the field i.e. body’), others call Turīya (‘the fourth one’) and still others Kūṭastha (‘the immovable, unchangeable Supreme Soul abiding in the heart’).

## \|\| 3.8.93 \|\|

*yaṃ nāspṛśaṃścaityamaciṃtyatattvaṃ duraṃtadhāmānamatatsvarūpam \|*  
*manovacovṛttaya ātmabhājāṃ sa eṣa pūjyaḥ paramaḥ śivo naḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. That Supreme Śiva is worthy of adoration to us, whom mental operations cannot touch, whose ultimate (real) truth is incomprehensible, whose brilliance is beyond any limitation, whose real form is of the nature of ‘not that’ (expressed in words ‘neti neti’), (who is beyond the reach of) the activities of the mind and speech of individual souls.

## \|\| 3.8.94 \|\|

*yasya prasādaṃ pratilabhya saṃto vāṃchaṃti naiṃdraṃ padamujjvalaṃ vā \|*  
*nistīrṇakarmārgalakālacakrāścaraṃtyabhītāḥ sa śivo gatirnaḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. That Śiva is our goal, after getting whose favour good men never desire even the glamorous post of Indra and they move about fearlessly after transcending the wheel of time and warding off the fastening bolt of mundane activities.

## \|\| 3.8.95 \|\|

*yasya smṛtiḥ sakalapāparujāṃ vighātaṃ sadyaḥ karotyapi cu pulkasajanmabhājām \|*  
*yasya svarūpamakhilaṃ śrutibhirvimṛgyaṃ tasmai śivāya satataṃ karavāma pūjām \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. We perform the adoration of that Śiva always, whose (mere) remembrance immediately eradicates all the ailments resulting from sins in their entirety, of even those who are born as Pulkasas, and whose real form is worthy of being sought by the Śruti.

## \|\| 3.8.96 \|\|

*yanmūrdhni labdhanilayā suralokasiṃdhuryasyāṃgagāṃ bhagavatī jagadaṃbikā ca \|*  
*yatkuṃḍale tvahaha takṣakavāsukī dvau so'smākameva gatirardhaśaśāṃkamauliḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. That Lord with the crescent moon for his crest-jewel is our ultimate goal, on whose head the celestial river has found a niche, whose body is shared by the Goddess, the Mother of the universe, and whose ear-rings are constituted by Takṣaka and Vāsuki.

## \|\| 3.8.97 \|\|

*jayati nigamacūḍāgreṣu yasyāṃghripadmaṃ jayati ca hṛdi nityaṃ yogināṃ yasya mūrtiḥ \|*  
*jayati sakalatattvodbhāsanaṃ yasya mūrtiḥ sa vijitaguṇasargaḥ pūjyate'smābhirīśaḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. That Īśa who has conquered the creations of the Guṇas, whose lotus-like feet reign gloriously on the top of the sacred scriptures, whose form is ever present in the hearts of Yogins and whose divine features illuminate all the principles, is being worshipped by us.

## \|\| 3.8.98 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacastasya takṣakaḥ prītamānasaḥ \|*  
*jātabhaktirmahādeve rājaputramabhāṣata \|\| 98 \|\|*

Sūta said:

98\. On hearing his words, Takṣaka became delighted in his mind. With his devotion to Mahādeva kindled, he spoke to the prince:

## \|\| 3.8.99 \|\|

*takṣaka uvāca \|*  
*parituṣṭo'smi bhadraṃ stāttava rājedranaṃdana \|*  
*bālopi yatparaṃ tattvaṃ vetsi śaivaṃ parātparam \|\| 99 \|\|*

Takṣaka said:

99\. O son of an eminent king, welfare unto thee. I am pleased with you, because though yet a boy, you know the highest truth of Śiva that is greater than the greatest.

## \|\| 3.8.100 \|\|

*eṣa ratnamayo loka etāścārudṛśo'balāḥ \|*  
*ete kalpadrumāḥ sarve vāpyomṛtarasāṃbhasaḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. Here the world is full of jewels. These girls have charming eyes. These are all wish-yielding Kalpa trees. These wells have nectarine juice for their water.

## \|\| 3.8.101 \|\|

*nātra mṛtyubhayaṃ ghoraṃ na jarārogapīḍanam \|*  
*yatheṣṭaṃ viharātraiva bhuṃkṣva bhogānyathocitān \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. Here there is no fear from the terrible death; there is no afflication due to old age and ailments. Sport about here as you please. Enjoy all the pleasures as you deem fit.

## \|\| 3.8.102 \|\|

*ityukto nāgarājena sa rājeṃdrakumārakaḥ \|*  
*pratyuvāca paraṃ prītyā kṛtāṃjalirudāradhīḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. On being told thus by the king of serpents, that prince of large-hearted nature, stood with palms joined in reverence and spoke with delight:

## \|\| 3.8.103 \|\|

*kṛtadāro'smyahaṃ kāle suvratā gṛhiṇī mama \|*  
*śiva pūjāparā nityaṃ pitarāvekaputrakau \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. “I was married with a wife at the proper time. My wife observes religious vows and restrictions regularly. She is always devoted to the worship of Śiva. I am the only son of my parents.

## \|\| 3.8.104 \|\|

*te tvadya māṃ mṛtaṃ mattvā śokena mahatāvṛtāḥ \|*  
*prāyaḥ prāṇairviyujyaṃte daivātprāṇānvahaṃti vā \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. They are, to be sure, overwhelmed with great grief considering me to be dead. Most probably, they too are dead or luckily they might have somehow managed to be alive.

## \|\| 3.8.105 \|\|

*ato mayā bahutithaṃ nātra stheyaṃ kathaṃcana \|*  
*tameva lokaṃ kṛpayā māṃ prāpayitumarhasi \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. Hence, I must not prolong my stay here. Kindly take me back to that world.”

## \|\| 3.8.106-107 \|\|

*ityuktavaṃtaṃ naradevaputraṃ divyairvarānnaiḥ surapādapotthaiḥ \|*  
*āpyāyayitvā varagaṃdhavāsaḥ sragratnadivyābharaṇairvicitraiḥ \|\| 106 \|\|*

*saṃtoṣayitvā vividhaiśca bhogaiḥ punarbabhāṣe bhujagādhirājaḥ \|*  
*yadāyadā tvaṃ smarasi tvadagre tadā tadāviṣkriyate mayeti \|\| 107 \|\|*

106-107. When the prince spoke thus, the king of serpents fed him with excellent divine food offered by the wish-yielding celestial trees. He made him happy further by means of excellent scents, garments, garlands and divine gemset ornaments of divine characteristics. He pleased him with all types of enjoyments and spoke, “Whenever you remember me, I shall gladly reveal myself to you.”

## \|\| 3.8.108-110 \|\|

*punaśca rājaputrāya takṣakośvaṃ ca kāmagam \|*  
*nānādvīpasamudreṣu lokeṣu ca nirargalam \|\| 108 \|\|*

*dattavānratnābharaṇa divyābharaṇavāsasām \|*  
*vāhanāya dadāvekaṃ rākṣasaṃ pannageśvaraḥ \|\| 109 \|\|*

*tatsahāyārthamekaṃ ca pannageṃdrakumārakam \|*  
*niyujya takṣakaḥ prītyā gaccheti visasarja tam \|\| 110 \|\|*

108-110. Takṣaka gave the prince a horse that could go wherever one wished it to go, and which went unhindered over different continents, oceans and worlds. He gave him jewel-set ornaments and fabrics of divine and superhuman origin. The serpent king presented him with a Rākṣasa who would carry (his luggage). There was a serpent boy to assist him. After offering all these, Takṣaka sent him off with great delight.

## \|\| 3.8.111 \|\|

*iti caṃdrāṃgadaḥ so'tha saṃgṛhya vividhaṃ dhanam \|*  
*aśvaṃ kāmagamāruhya tābhyāṃ saha viniryayau \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. Thus Candrāṅgada took with him all those rich presents. Seated on that horse able to move as he pleased, he set off accompanied by those two attendants.

## \|\| 3.8.112 \|\|

*sa mūhūrtādivonmajjya tasmā deva sarijjalāt \|*  
*vijahāra taṭe ramye divyamāruhya vājinam \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. In a short while he rose up from the waters of the rivers, and could sport about on the beautiful banks seated on the divine horse.

## \|\| 3.8.113 \|\|

*athāsminsamaye tanvī sā ca sīmaṃtinī satī \|*  
*snātuṃ samāyayau tatra sakhī bhiḥ parivāritā \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. At the same time his slender, chaste wife Sīmantinī came there to bathe, surrounded by her female companions.

## \|\| 3.8.114 \|\|

*sā dadarśa nadītīre viharaṃtaṃ nṛpātmajam \|*  
*rakṣasā nararūpeṇa nāgaputreṇa cānvitam \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. On the banks of the river, she saw the prince sporting about accompanied by the Rākṣasa who had assumed a human form and the son of a Nāga.

## \|\| 3.8.115 \|\|

*divyaratnasamākīrṇaṃ divya mālyāvataṃsakam \|*  
*dehena divyagaṃdhena vyākṣiptadaśayojanam \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. He was adorned with divine jewels, divine garlands and ornaments. The divine fragrance of his body spread over ten Yojanas.

## \|\| 3.8.116 \|\|

*tamapūrvākṛtiṃ vīkṣya divyāśvamadhisaṃsthitam \|*  
*jaḍonmatteva bhīteva tasthau tannyastalocanā \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. On seeing that (prince) of unusual form and features riding a divine horse, she stood frightened as though stunned and rendered out of senses with her eyes fixed on him.

## \|\| 3.8.117-119 \|\|

*tāṃ ca rājeṃdraputro'sau dṛṣṭapūrvāmiti smaran \|*  
*nirmuktakaṃṭhābharaṇāṃ kaṃṭhasūtravivarjitām \|\| 117 \|\|*

*asaṃyojitadhammillāmaṃgarāgavivarjitām \|*  
*tyaktanīlāṃjanāpāṃgīṃ kṛśāṃgīṃ śokadūṣitām \|\| 118 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā'vatīrya turagādupaviṣṭaḥ sarittaṭe \|*  
*tāmāhūya varārohāmupaveśyedama bravīt \|\| 119 \|\|*

117-119. On seeing her, the prince seemed to remember her as one seen before, though she was now devoid of all ornaments round her neck, without even the auspicious (marital) thread (Maṅgalasūtra). Her tresses were dishevelled and uncombed. She had no unguents on her body. There was no blue collyrium in her eyes. She was lean and distressed with grief.

On seeing her, he got down from the horse and sat down on the banks. He invited her to him and spoke to her as she was seated:

## \|\| 3.8.120 \|\|

*kā tvaṃ kasya kalatraṃ vā kasyāsi tanayā satī \|*  
*kimidaṃ teṃgane bālye duḥsahaṃ śokalakṣaṇam \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. “Who are you, O chaste lady? Whose wife are you? And whose daughter? Why are you so much distressed with unbearable grief at this early age (not yet out of teens)?”

## \|\| 3.8.121 \|\|

*iti snehena saṃpṛṣṭā sā vadhūraśrulocanā \|*  
*lajjitā svayamākhyātuṃ tatsakhī sarvamabravīt \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. On being asked so lovingly, the lady stood bashfully shedding tears. As she was unable to speak, her female companion spoke everything.

## \|\| 3.8.122-123 \|\|

*iyaṃ sīmaṃtinī nāmnā snuṣā niṣadhabhūpateḥ \|*  
*caṃdrāṃgadasya mahiṣī tanayā citravarmaṇaḥ \|\| 122 \|\|*

*asyāḥ patirdaivayogānnimagno'sminmahājale \|*  
*teneyaṃ prāptavaidhavyā bālā duḥkhena śoṣitā \|\| 123 \|\|*

122-123. “This is the daughter-in-law of the king of Niṣadha, Sīmantinī by name. She is the crowned queen of Candrāṅgada and daughter of Citravarmā. As fate would have it, her husband drowned in the waters of this great river. Hence the girl obviously widowed, has become emaciated due to grief.

## \|\| 3.8.124 \|\|

*evaṃ varṣatrayaṃ nītaṃ śokenātibalīyasā \|*  
*adyeṃduvāre saṃprāpte snātumatra samāgatā \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. Thus she has spent three years bearing the excessive grief. Today being Monday, she has come here for her bath.

## \|\| 3.8.125 \|\|

*śvaśuro'syāśca rājeṃdro hṛtarājyaśca śatru bhiḥ \|*  
*balādgṛhīto baddhaśca sabhāryastadvaśe sthitaḥ \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. Her father-in-law, the great king, has been deprived of his kingdom by his enemies. He has been imprisoned along with his wife and kept under their control.

## \|\| 3.8.126 \|\|

*tathāpyeṣā śubhācārā somavāre maheśvaram \|*  
*sāṃbikaṃ parayā bhaktyā pūjayatyamalāśayā \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. Still she continues to observe her splendid religious vows. The lady of pure heart worships Maheśvara in the company of Aṃbikā with great devotion.”

## \|\| 3.8.127 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*itthaṃ sakhīmukhenaiva sarvamāvedya suvratā \|*  
*tataḥ sīmaṃtinī prāha svayameva nṛpātmajam \|\| 127 \|\|*

Sūta said:

127\. After thus intimating everything to him through her companion, Sīmantinī of great pious observances addressed the prince herself.

## \|\| 3.8.128-130 \|\|

*kastvaṃ kaṃdarpasaṃkāśaḥ kāvimau tava pārśvagau \|*  
*devo nareṃdraḥ siddho vā gaṃdharvo vātha kinnaraḥ \|\| 128 \|\|*

*kimarthaṃ mama vṛttāṃtaṃ snehavāniva pṛcchasi \|*  
*kiṃ māṃ vetsi mahābāho dṛṣṭavānkimu kutracit \|\| 129 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭapūrva ivābhāsi mayā ca svajano yathā \|*  
*sarvaṃ kathaya tattvena satyasārā hi sādhavaḥ \|\| 130 \|\|*

128-130. “Who are you? A Deva? A king? A Sidḍha? A Gandharva? Or a Kinnara? You are verily like Kandarpa (god of Love). Who are these two attendants of yours? What prompts you to enquire about me so lovingly? O mighty one, do you happen to know me? Have you seen me anywhere? You appear to be one seen before as though a near kinsman. Kindly narrate everything truthfully. Indeed good people give weightage to truth.”

## \|\| 3.8.131 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*etāvaduktvā naradevaputrī sabāṣpakaṃṭhaṃ suciraṃ ruroda \|*  
*mumoha bhūmau patitā sakhībhirvṛtā na kiṃcitkathituṃ śaśāka \|\| 131 \|\|*

Sūta said:

131\. After saying this much, the princess cried for a long time with her throat choked with tears. She fainted and fell down on the ground. Her female companions crowded round her. She could not utter anything further.

## \|\| 3.8.132 \|\|

*śrutvā caṃdrāṃgadaḥ sarvaṃ priyāyāḥ śokakāraṇam \|*  
*muhūrttamabhavatūṣṇīṃ svayaṃ śokasamākulaḥ \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. On hearing everything that caused grief to his beloved, Candrāṅgada kept silent for a short while, himself undergoing excessive grief.

## \|\| 3.8.133 \|\|

*athāśvāsya priyāṃ tanvīṃ vividhairvākyanaipuṇaiḥ \|*  
*siddhā nāma vayaṃ devāḥ kāmagā iti so'bravīt \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. He consoled his beloved wife by means of different words cleverly expressed. “Indeed we are Siddhas and Devas with ability to move about as we please”, he said.

## \|\| 3.8.134 \|\|

*tato balādivākṛṣya pāṇigrahaṇaśaṃkitām \|*  
*pulakāṃcitasarvāṃgīṃ tāṃ karṇe tvidamabravīt \|\| 134 \|\|*

134\. Then he dragged her to him with force while she hesitated when he caught hold of her hand. Hairs stood on their ends all over her body. He spoke thus into her ear.

## \|\| 3.8.135-137 \|\|

*kvāpi loke mayā dṛṣṭastava bharttā varānane \|*  
*tvadvratācaraṇātprītaḥ sadya evāgamiṣyati \|\| 135 \|\|*

*apaneṣyati te śokaṃ dvitraireva dinairdhruvam \|*  
*etacchaṃsitumāyātastava bharttuḥ sakhā'smyaham \|\| 136 \|\|*

*atra kāryo na saṃdehaḥ śapāmi śivapādayoḥ \|*  
*tāvattvaddhṛdaye stheyaṃ na prakāśyaṃ ca kutracit \|\| 137 \|\|*

135-137. “O lady of excellent countenance, somewhere in this world your husband has been seen by me. He is delighted with your observances of vows. He will come quickly. Within two or three days he will surely remove your grief. I am a friend of your husband and have come here to tell this. In this respect no doubt need be entertained. I promise by the feet of Śiva. But let this be a secret well kept in your heart. It should not be revealed to anyone.”

## \|\| 3.8.138 \|\|

*sā tu tadvacanaṃ śrutvā sudhādhārāśatādhikam \|*  
*saṃbhramodbhrāṃtanayanā tameva muhuraikṣata \|\| 138 \|\|*

138\. On hearing his words flowing like nectar in hundreds of torrents, she looked at him frequently with dismay and excitement.

## \|\| 3.8.139-140 \|\|

*premabaṃdhānuguṇitaṃ vākyaṃ cāha rasāyanam \|*  
*vibhramodārasahitaṃ madhurāpāṃgavīkṣaṇam \|\| 139 \|\|*

*svapāṇisparśanodbhinnapulakāṃcitavigraham \|*  
*pūrva dṛṣṭāni cāṃgeṣu lakṣaṇāni svarādiṣu \|*  
*vayaḥpramāṇaṃ varṇaṃ ca parīkṣyainamatarkayat \|\| 140 \|\|*

139-140. She carefully noted his loving words sweet like honey. Noting carefully his sweet side-glances and graceful charm, his body which was thrilled (with hair standing on their ends) at the touch of her hand, the characteristics of his person, tone, age and complexion, she suspected and thought:

## \|\| 3.8.141-146 \|\|

*eṣa eva patirme syāddhruvaṃ nānyo bhaviṣyati \|*  
*asminneva prasaktaṃ me hṛdayaṃ premakātaram \|\| 141 \|\|*

*paralokādihāyātaḥ kathamevaṃ svarūpadhṛk \|*  
*durbhāgyāyāḥ kathaṃ me syādbharturnaṣṭasya darśanam \|\| 142 \|\|*

*svapnoyaṃ kimu na svapno bhramo'yaṃ kiṃ tu na bhramaḥ \|*  
*eṣa dhūrto'thavā kaścidyakṣo gaṃdharva eva vā \|\| 143 \|\|*

*munipalyā yaduktaṃ me paramāpadgatāpi ca \|*  
*vratametatkuruṣveti tasya vā phalameva vā \|\| 144 \|\|*

*yo varṣāyuta saubhāgyaṃ mametyāha dvijottamaḥ \|*  
*nūnaṃ tasya vacaḥ satyaṃ ko vidyādīśvaraṃ vinā \|\| 145 \|\|*

*nimittāni ca dṛśyaṃte maṃgalāni dinedine \|*  
*prasanne pārvatīnāthe kimasādhyaṃ śarīriṇām \|\| 146 \|\|*

141-146. ‘Surely this is my husband. It cannot be anyone else. My heart is agitated with love and is attached to him. How has he come here from the other world? How could he assume such a form as this? Unfortunate that I am, am I destined to see my lost husband? Is this a dream? No, no, this is no illusion. Is he a rogue? Is he a Yakṣa or a Gandharva? The wife of the sage had advised me to continue this pious observance even when I am in great adversity. Is this the fruit of that observance? An excellent Brāhmaṇa had predicted my conjugal bliss for ten thousand years. Indeed, have his words come true? Excepting Īśvara who will know these things? Everyday good omens forebode auspicious future. If the Consort of Pārvatī is pleased, what is impossible to be achieved by embodied beings?’

## \|\| 3.8.147 \|\|

*itthaṃ vimṛśya bahudhā tāṃ punarmuktasaṃśayām \|*  
*lajjānamramukhīṃ karṇe śaśaṃsātmaprayojanam \|\| 147 \|\|*

147\. After pondering thus for a while, she became free from all doubts. While she stood with the face down due to bashfulness, he disclosed into her ear what he intended.

## \|\| 3.8.148 \|\|

*imaṃ vṛttāṃtamākhyātuṃ tatpitroḥ śokataptayoḥ \|*  
*gacchāmaḥ svasti te bhadre sadyaḥ patimavāpsyasi \|\| 148 \|\|*

148\. “Let us go near my parents who are grief-stricken to communicate this news. O fair lady, hail unto you! You shall get your husband soon.”

## \|\| 3.8.149 \|\|

*ityuktvāśvaṃ samāruhya jagāma nṛpanaṃdanaḥ \|*  
*tābhyāṃ saha nijaṃ rāṣṭraṃ pratyapadyata tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 149 \|\|*

149\. After saying thus, the prince mounted his horse and accompanied by both of them reached his kingdom in a trice.

## \|\| 3.8.150 \|\|

*sa puropavanābhyāśe sthitvā taṃ phaṇi putrakam \|*  
*visasarjātmadāyādānnṛpāsanagatānprati \|\| 150 \|\|*

150\. He stood near the garden at the outskirts of the city and sent the son of Nāga to his kinsmen who had usurped the royal throne.

## \|\| 3.8.151-153 \|\|

*sa gatvovāca tāñchīghramiṃdraseno vimucyatām \|*  
*caṃdrāṃgadastasya sutaḥ prāpto'yaṃ pannagāla yāt \|\| 151 \|\|*

*nṛpāsanaṃ vimuṃcaṃtu bhavaṃto na vicāryatām \|*  
*no ceccaṃdrāgadasyāśu bāṇāḥ prāṇānharaṃti vaḥ \|\| 152 \|\|*

*sa magno yamunātoye gatvā takṣakamaṃdiram \|*  
*labdhvā ca tasya sāhāyyaṃ punarlokādihāgataḥ \|\| 153 \|\|*

151-153. He went and informed them: “Let Indrasena be released quickly. Candrāṅgada, his son, has come from the world of serpents. You may soon abdicate the throne with no further hesitation. If not, the arrows of Candrāṅgada will take away your vital breaths. Diving into the waters of Yamunā, he went to the palace of Takṣaka. After getting his assistance, he has come here from that world.”

## \|\| 3.8.154 \|\|

*ityākhyātamaśeṣeṇa tadvṛttāṃtaṃ niśamya te \|*  
*sādhusādhviti saṃbhrāṃtāḥ śaśaṃsuḥ paripaṃthinaḥ \|\| 154 \|\|*

154\. On hearing these words intimating the details, the enemies became agitated and said, “Very good!”

## \|\| 3.8.155 \|\|

*atheṃdrasenāya nivedya satvaraṃ naṣṭasya putrasya punaḥ samāgamam \|*  
*prasādya taṃ prāptanareśvarāsanaṃ dāyādamukhyāstu bhayaṃ prapedire \|\| 155 \|\|*

155\. Everything was conveyed to Indrasena such as the return of the lost son and other things. They congratulated him on his regaining the throne. The kinsmen, as expected, became frightened inordinately.

## \|\| 3.8.156 \|\|

*atha paurajanāḥ sarve purodyāne nṛpātmajam \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā rājñe drutaṃ procurlebhire ca mahādhanam \|\| 156 \|\|*

156\. All the citizens met the prince at the garden and conveyed the news to the king. They were sumptuously rewarded.

## \|\| 3.8.157 \|\|

*ākarṇya putramāyāṃtaṃ rājānaṃdajalāplutaḥ \|*  
*na vyajānādimaṃ lokaṃ rājñī ca parayā mudā \|\| 157 \|\|*

157\. On hearing that the prince was approaching, the king’s eyes welled with tears of joy. Due to great joy, the queen too did not see properly things (in front in the) world.

## \|\| 3.8.158 \|\|

*atha nāgarikāḥ sarve maṃtrivṛddhāḥ purodhasaḥ \|*  
*pratyudgamya pariṣvajya tamāninyurnṛpāṃti kam \|\| 158 \|\|*

158\. All the citizens, the elderly ministers, the priests received him, embraced him and took him to the king.

## \|\| 3.8.159 \|\|

*athotsavena mahatā praviśya nijamaṃdiram \|*  
*rājaputraḥ svapitarau vavaṃde bāṣpamutsṛjan \|\| 159 \|\|*

159\. With great festivity and pomp, the prince entered the palace, bowed down to his parents and shed tears of joy.

## \|\| 3.8.160 \|\|

*taṃ pādamūle patitaṃ svaputraṃ viveda nāsau pṛthivīpatiḥ kṣaṇam \|*  
*prabodhito'mātyajanaiḥ kathaṃcidutthāya klinnena hṛdāliliṃga \|\| 160 \|\|*

160\. For a moment, the king could not recognize his son who fell at his feet. Reminded by his ministers, he somehow raised him up and embraced him with a melting heart.

## \|\| 3.8.161 \|\|

*krameṇa mātṝrabhivaṃdya tābhiḥ pravardhitāśīḥ praṇayāku lābhiḥ \|*  
*āliṃgitaḥ paurajanānaśeṣānsaṃbhāvayāmāsa sa rājasūnuḥ \|\| 161 \|\|*

161\. The prince bowed down to his mothers in due order. With increased affection, they offered their blessings to him and embraced him. He then duly honoured all the citizens.

## \|\| 3.8.162-163 \|\|
