*teṣāṃ madhye samāsīnaḥ svavṛttāṃtamaśeṣataḥ \|*  
*pitre nivedayāmāsa takṣakasya ca mitratām \|\| 162 \|\|*

*dattaṃ bhujaṃgarājena ratnādidhanasaṃcayam \|*  
*divyaṃ tadrākṣasānītaṃ pitre sarvaṃ nyavedayat \|\| 163 \|\|*

162-163. Seated amidst them, he reported everything that happened to him, to his father, such as the friendship of Takṣaka, the jewel and other rich presents given by the king of serpents, all those divine things brought by that Ṛākṣasa and similar things.

## \|\| 3.8.164 \|\|

*rājaputrasya caritaṃ dṛṣṭvā śrutvā ca vihvalaḥ \|\| \|*  
*mene snuṣāyāḥ saubhāgyaṃ maheśārādhanārjitam \|\| 164 \|\|*

164\. On seeing and hearing the incidents in the life of his son, the king became thrilled. He thought that the conjugal bliss of his daughter-in-law was a thing acquired by propitiating Maheśvara.

## \|\| 3.8.165 \|\|

*saumāṃgalyamayīṃ vārtāmimāṃ niṣadhabhūpatiḥ \|*  
*cārairnivedayāmāsa citravarmamahīpateḥ \|\| 165 \|\|*

165\. The king of Niṣadha conveyed this good news of great auspiciousness to King Citravarmā through his spies and errand boys.

## \|\| 3.8.166 \|\|

*śrutvā'mṛtamayīṃ vārttāṃ sa samutthāya saṃbhramāt \|*  
*tebhyo dattvā dhanaṃ bhūri nanartānaṃdavihvalaḥ \|\| 166 \|\|*

166\. On hearing the delightful news soothing like ambrosia, he got up with excitement. Rewarding them with adequate monetary gifts, he began to dance with joy.

## \|\| 3.8.167 \|\|

*athāhūya svatanayāṃ pariṣvajyāśrulocanaḥ \|*  
*bhūṣaṇairbhūṣayāmāsa tyaktavaidhavyalakṣaṇām \|\| 167 \|\|*

167\. With eyes brimming with tears of joy he called his daughter to him and adorned her with ornaments removing the signs of widowhood.

## \|\| 3.8.168 \|\|

*athotsavo mahānāsīdrāṣṭragrāmapurādiṣu \|*  
*sīmaṃtinyāḥ śubhācāraṃ śaśaṃsuḥ sarvato janāḥ \|\| 168 \|\|*

168\. There was a great celebration and rejoicing in the cities and villages of the country. Everywhere the people praised the pious conduct of Sīmantinī.

## \|\| 3.8.169 \|\|

*citravarmātha nṛpatiḥ samāhūyeṃdrasenajam \|*  
*punarvivāhavidhinā sutāṃ tasmai nyavedayat \|\| 169 \|\|*

169\. King Citravarmā invited Indrasena’s son and offered his daughter to him going through the rites of marriage all over again.

## \|\| 3.8.170 \|\|

*candrāṃgado'pi ratnādyairānītaistakṣakālayāt \|*  
*svāṃ patnīṃ bhūṣayāṃ cakre martyānāmatidurlabhaiḥ \|\| 170 \|\|*

170\. With the jewels and other valuable things brought from the abode of Takṣaka, which were rare and inaccessible to human beings, Candrāṅgada adorned his wife.

## \|\| 3.8.171 \|\|

*aṃgarāgeṇa divyena taptakāṃcanaśobhinā \|*  
*śuśubhe sā sugaṃdhena daśayojanagāminā \|\| 171 \|\|*

171\. With the divine unguent shining like molten gold and sweet scent spreading its fragrance ten Yojanas all round, she looked splendid.

## \|\| 3.8.172 \|\|

*amlānamālayā śaśvatpadmakiṃjalkavarṇayā \|*  
*kalpadrumotthayā bālā bhūṣitā śuśubhe satī \|\| 172 \|\|*

172\. Decorated with a never-fading garland having the colour and filaments of lotus coming from the wish-yielding Kalpa tree, the chaste lady shone all the more.

## \|\| 3.8.173 \|\|

*evaṃ caṃdrāṃgadaḥ patnīmavāpya samaye śubhe \|*  
*yayau svanagarīṃ bhūyaḥ śvaśureṇānumoditaḥ \|\| 173 \|\|*

173\. Having been reunited with his wife on an auspicious occasion, Candrāṅgada went back to his city blessed and congratulated by his father-in-law.

## \|\| 3.8.174 \|\|

*indraseno'pi rājeṃdro rājye sthāpya nijātmajam \|*  
*tapasā śivamārādhya lebhe saṃyamināṃ gatim \|\| 174 \|\|*

174\. The eminent King Indrasena installed his son in his kingdom, propitiated Śiva by means of penance and attained the goal of those who practice self-control.

## \|\| 3.8.175 \|\|

*daśavarṣa sahasrāṇi sīmaṃtinyā svabhāryayā \|*  
*sārdhaṃ candrāṃgado rājā bubhuje viṣayānbahūn \|\| 175 \|\|*

175\. For ten thousand years King Candrāṅgada enjoyed various worldly pleasures along with his wife Sīmantinī.

## \|\| 3.8.176 \|\|

*prāsūta tanayānaṣṭau kanyāmekāṃ varānanām \|*  
*reme sīmaṃtinī bhartrā pūjayatī maheśvaram \|*  
*dinedine ca saubhāgyaṃ prāptaṃ caivenduvāsarāt \|\| 176 \|\|*

176\. She gave birth to eight sons and a beautiful daughter. Worshipping Maheśvara, Sīmantinī sported about with her husband. Day by day the conjugal bliss got augmented due to the Monday observance (worship of Śiva).

## \|\| 3.8.177 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*vicitramidamākhyānaṃ mayā samanuvarṇitam \|*  
*bhūyo'pi vakṣye māhātmyaṃ somavāravratoditam \|\| 177 \|\|*

Sūta said:

177\. This wonderful narrative has been told by me. I shall further recount the greatness of the pious Monday observance.

## Chapter 9 - The (Spiritual) Power of Simantinī

## \|\| 3.9.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*sādhusādhu mahābhāga tvayā kathitamuttamam \|*  
*ākhyānaṃ punaranyatra vicitraṃ vaktumarhasi \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: The chapter further describes how due to this Vrata, the spiritual power of Sīmantinī became so great that a male Brāhmaṇa who tried to cheat her by posing as a woman was permanently transformed into a woman.

The Sages said:

1\. Well! Well! O blessed one, what has been narrated by you is excellent. It behoves you to relate another tale equally wonderful.

## \|\| 3.9.2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*vidarbhaviṣaye pūrvamāsīdeko dvijottamaḥ \|*  
*vedamitra iti khyāto veda śāstrārthavitsudhīḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sūta said:

2\. In the land of Vidarbha, formerly, there was an excellent Brāhmaṇa well-known as Vedamitra. He was intelligent and a knower of the meanings of Vedic and scriptural texts.

## \|\| 3.9.3 \|\|

*tasyāsīdaparo vipraḥ sakhā sārasvatāhvayaḥ \|*  
*tāvubhau paramasnigdhāvekadeśanivāsinau \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. He had another Brāhmaṇa friend named Sārasvata. Both of them hailing from the same place were very friendly to each other.

## \|\| 3.9.4 \|\|

*vedamitrasya putro'bhūtsumedhā nāma suvrataḥ \|*  
*sārasvatasya tanayaḥ somavāniti viśrutaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Vedamitra’s son was a virtuous boy named Sumedhā. The son of Sārasvata was well-known as Somavān.

## \|\| 3.9.5 \|\|

*ubhau savayasau bālau samaveṣau samasthitī \|*  
*samaṃ ca kṛtasaṃskārau sama vidyau babhūvatuḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Both the boys were of the same age. Their status was equal and they dressed alike. They were consecrated simultaneously and their level of learning was the same.

## \|\| 3.9.6-7 \|\|

*sāṃgānadhītya tau vedāṃstarkavyākaraṇāni ca \|*  
*itihāsapurāṇāni dharmaśāstrāṇi kṛtsnaśaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*sarvavidyākuśalinau bālya eva manīṣiṇau \|*  
*praharṣamatulaṃ pitrordadatuḥ sakalairguṇaiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. They learned all the Vedas along with their Aṅgas (ancillaries), Tarka, Vyākaraṇa, Itihāsas, Purāṇas and all the Dharma Śāstras completely and became adepts in all arts and sciences. They became great scholars just in their childhood. With their good qualities they satisfied their parents.

## \|\| 3.9.8 \|\|

*tāvekadā svatanayau tāvubhau brāhmaṇottamau \|*  
*āhūyāvocatāṃ prītyā ṣoḍa śābdau śubhākṛtī \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Once those two excellent Brāhmaṇas called their sons when they had completed their sixteenth year and had grown into handsome youths and said thus with pleasure:

## \|\| 3.9.9-10 \|\|

*he putrakau yuvāṃ bālye kṛtavidyau suvarcasau \|*  
*vaivāhikoyaṃ samayo vartate yuvayoḥ samam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*imaṃ prasādya rājānaṃ vidarbheśaṃ svavidyayā \|*  
*tataḥ prāpya dhanaṃ bhūri kṛtodvāhau bhaviṣyathaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. “O sons, you have learned everything early in your childhood. You have become very brilliant. Now is the proper time for the marriage. You must please the king of Vidarbha with your learning. Get ample sums of money from him and celebrate your marriage.”

## \|\| 3.9.11 \|\|

*evamuktau sutau tābhyāṃ tāvubhau dvijanaṃdanau \|*  
*vidarbharājamāsādya samatoṣayatāṃ guṇaiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. On being told thus by them, the two Brāhmaṇa boys went to the king of Vidarbha and pleased him with their good qualities.

## \|\| 3.9.12 \|\|

*vidyayā parituṣṭāya tasmai dvijakumārakau \|*  
*vivāhārthaṃ kṛtodyogau dhanahīnāvaśaṃsatām \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. When the king was satisfied with their academic achievement, the Brāhmaṇa boys revealed to him that being devoid of money, they had done this (presentation of their academic achievement) for the sake of marriage.

## \|\| 3.9.13 \|\|

*tayorapi mataṃ jñātvā sa vidarbhamahīpatiḥ \|*  
*prahasya kiṃcitprovāca lokatattvavivitsayā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. After coming to know of their intention, the king laughingly told them something with a desire to know some facts concerning common people.

## \|\| 3.9.14-17 \|\|

*āste niṣadharājasya rājñī sīmaṃtinī satī \|*  
*somavāre mahādevaṃ pūjayatyaṃbikāyutam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*tasmindine sapatnīkāndvijāgryānvedavittamān \|*  
*saṃpūjya parayā bhaktyā dhanaṃ bhūri dadāti ca \|\| 15 \|\|*

*ato'tra yuvayoraiko nārīvibhramaveṣadhṛk \|*  
*ekastasyā patirbhūtvā jāyetāṃ vipradaṃpatī \|\| 16 \|\|*

*yuvāṃ vadhūvarau bhūtvā prāpya sīmaṃtinīgṛham \|*  
*bhuktvā bhūri dhanaṃ labdhvā punaryātaṃ mamāṃmatikam \|\| 17 \|\|*

14-17. “There is a queen of Niṣadha, Sīmantinī, a chaste lady. She worships Mahādeva along with Aṃbikā on Mondays. On that day, with great devotion, she honours great Brāhmaṇas well-versed in the Vedas, along with their wives, and offers them plenty of wealth. So one of you shall go there in the graceful guise of a woman and the other shall be her husband. You will thus become a Brāhmaṇa couple. Thus like a bride and a bridegroom you go to Sīmantinī’s abode. Take food there and after getting sufficient amount of money, come to me.”

## \|\| 3.9.18-23 \|\|

*iti rājñā samādiṣṭau bhītau dvijakumārakau \|*  
*pratyūcaturidaṃ karma kartuṃ nau jāyate bhayam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*devatāsu gurau pitrostathā rājakuleṣu ca \|*  
*kauṭilyamācaranmohātsadyo naśyati sānvayaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*kathamaṃtargṛhaṃ rājñāṃ chadmanā praviśetpumān \|*  
*gopyamānamapicchadma kadācitkhyātimeṣyati \|\| 20 \|\|*

*ye guṇāḥ sādhitāḥ pūrvaṃ śīlācāraśrutādibhiḥ \|*  
*sadyaste nāśamāyāṃti kauṭilya pathagāminaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*pāpaṃ niṃdā bhayaṃ vairaṃ catvāryetāni dehinām \|*  
*chadmamārgaprapannānāṃ tiṣṭhaṃtyeva hi sarvadā \|\| 22 \|\|*

*ata āvāṃ śubhācārau jātau ca śucināṃ kule \|*  
*vṛttaṃ dhūrtajanaślāghyaṃ nāśrayāvaḥ kadācana \|\| 23 \|\|*

18-23. On being ordered thus by the king, the Brāhmaṇa boys became frightened. They replied: “We are afraid to do an act like this. One who acts fraudulently in respect to deities, elders, parents and royal households under a false idea perishes along with his family. How can a man enter deceitfully the inner apartments of kings? Even well-concealed deception becomes exposed (sooner of later). Good qualities acquired earlier by means of good education, decent habits and regulated activities are lost at once if the person concerned takes to a crooked path.

Sin, censure, fear and enmity—these four always belong to persons adopting deceitful means. Therefore, we, born in sinless families, of a good conduct, will never resort to acts praised by rogues.”

## \|\| 3.9.24 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*daivatānāṃ gurūṇāṃ ca pitrośca pṛthivīpateḥ \|*  
*śāsanasyāpyalaṃghyatvātpratyādeśo na karhicit \|\| 24 \|\|*

The king said:

24\. The word of command of deities, elders, parents and king should not be disobeyed. One should never think of going against it.

## \|\| 3.9.25 \|\|

*etairyadyatsamādiṣṭaṃ śubhaṃ vā yadi vā'śubham \|*  
*kartavyaṃ niyataṃ bhītairapramattairbubhūṣubhiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Whatever has been ordered by these, good or bad, should immediately be carried into practice by those who wish to be free from error, even if they are afraid.

## \|\| 3.9.26 \|\|

*aho vayaṃ hi rājānaḥ prajā yūyaṃ hi saṃmatāḥ \|*  
*rājājñayā pravṛttānāṃ śreyaḥ syādanyathā bhayam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Don’t you know, we are kings. You are accepted as subjects. Prosperity comes to those people who act according to the behests of kings; otherwise there is fear of danger.

## \|\| 3.9.27 \|\|

*ato macchāsanaṃ kāryaṃ bhava dbhyāmavilaṃbitam \|*  
*ityuktau naradevena tau tathetyūcaturbhayāt \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Hence, do as I have commanded you to do without delay.

On being told thus by the king, they consented to it out of fright.

## \|\| 3.9.28 \|\|

*sārasvatasya tanayaṃ sāmavantaṃ narādhipaḥ \|*  
*strīrūpadhāriṇaṃ cakre vastrākalpāṃ janādibhiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The king made Somavān, the son of Sārasvata, to disguise as a female with (appropriate) garments, ornaments, collyrium and other things.

## \|\| 3.9.29 \|\|

*sa kṛtrimodbhūtakalatrabhāvaḥ prayuktakarṇābharaṇāṃgarāgaḥ \|*  
*snigdhāñjanākṣaḥ spṛhaṇīyarūpo babhūva sadyaḥ pramadottamābhaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. With an artificial role of a woman imposed on him by the use of unguents, ear-rings and other ornaments, with his eyes made smooth and shining by means of collyrium, he immediately became one shining like an excellent maiden of comely form and features.

## \|\| 3.9.30 \|\|

*tāvubhau daṃpatī bhūtvā dvijaputrau nṛpājñayā \|*  
*jagmaturnaiṣadhaṃ deśaṃ yadvā tadvā bhavatviti \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. At the bidding of the king the Brāhmaṇa boys became a Brāhmaṇa couple and went to the land of Niṣadha thinking, ‘Let come what may.’

## \|\| 3.9.31 \|\|

*upetya rājasadanaṃ somavāre dvijottamaiḥ \|*  
*sapatnīkaiḥ kṛtātithyau dhautapādau babhūvatuḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Along with other excellent Brāhmaṇas with their wives, they went to the royal palace on Monday. They were received with hospitality and their feet were washed.

## \|\| 3.9.32 \|\|

*sā rājñī brāhmaṇānsarvānupaviṣṭānvarāsane \|*  
*pratyekamarcayāṃcakre sapatnīkāndvijottamān \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The queen honoured the excellent Brāhmaṇas and their wives individually after making them sit on excellent seats.

## \|\| 3.9.33 \|\|

*tau ca viprasutau dṛṣṭvā prāptau kṛtakadaṃpatī \|*  
*jñātvā kiṃcidvihasyātha mene gaurīmaheśvarau \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. On seeing the Brāhmaṇa boys who approached her, she recognised that they were a couple in disguise. She smiled within herself. But she considered them as Gaurī and Maheśvara.

## \|\| 3.9.34 \|\|

*āvāhya dvijamukhyeṣu devadevaṃ sadāśivam \|*  
*patnīṣvāvāhayāmāsa sā devīṃ jagadaṃbikām \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. She invoked Sadāśiva, the Lord of Devas, in those Brāhmaṇas, and goddess, the mother of the universe, in their wives.

## \|\| 3.9.35 \|\|

*gandhairmālyaiḥ surabhibhirdhūpairnīrājanairapi \|*  
*arcayitvā dvijaśreṣṭhānnamaścakre samāhitā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. With mental and bodily purity, she adored the excellent Brāhmaṇas with sweet scents, garlands, fragrant incense and waved lights and then made obeisance to them.

## \|\| 3.9.36-39 \|\|

*hiraṇmayeṣu pātreṣu pāyasaṃ ghṛtasaṃyutam \|*  
*śarkarāmadhusaṃyuktaṃ śākairjuṣṭaṃ manoramaiḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*gaṃdhaśālyodanairhṛdyairmodakāpūparāśibhiḥ \|*  
*śaṣkrulībhiśca saṃyāvaiḥ kṛsarairmāṣapakvakaiḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*tathānyairapyasaṃkhyātairbhakṣyairbhojyairmanoramaiḥ \|*  
*sugandhaiḥ svādubhiḥ sūpaiḥ pānīyairapi śītalaiḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*klṛptamannaṃ dvijāgryebhyaḥ sā bhaktyā paryaveṣayat \|*  
*dadhyodanaṃ nirupamaṃ nivedya samatoṣayat \|\| 39 \|\|*

36-39. She offered them nice dishes to eat. There was milk pudding with adequate sugar and honey soaked in ghee in gold pots. There were pleasing vegetable dishes, cooked rice of sweetsmelling flavour, sweetmeats and heaps of baked pies, Śaṣkulīs (fried coiled snacks), Saṃyāvas (Halwas), Kṛśaras cooked with black gram pulses and numerous other delicacies. The soups were delicious and sweet-smelling. The water was very cool. She served all these foodstuffs to those excellent Brāhmaṇas with great devotion. After offering them cooked rice with excellent curds, she delighted them immensely.

## \|\| 3.9.40-41 \|\|

*bhuktavatsu dvijāgryeṣu svācāṃteṣu nṛpāṃganā \|*  
*praṇamya dattvā tāṃbūlaṃ dakṣiṇāṃ ca yathārhataḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*dhenūrhiraṇyavāsāṃsi ratnasragbhūṣaṇāni ca \|*  
*dattvā bhūyo namaskṛtya visasarja dvijottamān \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. After the excellent Brāhmaṇas had taken their food and rinsed their mouths, the queen bowed to them and offered betel leaves and monetary gifts in a befitting manner. She gave cows, gold pieces, garments, jewels, gemset ornaments and necklaces. Again she bowed to them and sent away the excellent Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 3.9.42 \|\|

*tayordvayorbhūsuravaryaputrayorekasttayā haimavatīdhiyārcitaḥ \|*  
*eko mahādevadhiyābhipūjitaḥ kṛtapraṇāmau yayatustadājñayā \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Of those two Brāhmaṇa boys, one was worshipped by her after identifying her with the Daughter of Himavān. The other one was adored with the thought that he was Mahādeva. Both of them went off after taking leave of her after the customary obeisance had been made.

## \|\| 3.9.43 \|\|

*sā tu vismṛtapuṃbhāvā tasminneva dvijottame \|*  
*jātaspṛhā madotsiktā kandarpavivaśābravīt \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. (The Brāhmaṇa boy disguised as a woman) forgot her real nature as a man. She became enamoured of the other excellent Brāhmaṇa boy. She was overcome with passion and was love-lorn, being tormented by Kandarpa (god of Love).

## \|\| 3.9.44-45 \|\|

*aṃyi nātha viśālākṣa sarvāvayavasundara \|*  
*tiṣṭhatiṣṭha kva vā yāsi māṃ na paśyasi te priyām \|\| 44 \|\|*

*idamagre vanaṃ ramyaṃ supuṣpitamahādrumam \|*  
*asminvihartumicchāmi tvayā saha yathāsukham \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. “O my lord of large lovely eyes, handsome in every limb! Stop, stop. Where are you going? Don’t you see me, your beloved?

Here (we are approaching) this beautiful forest teeming with great trees in full bloom. I wish to sport in dalliance with you in this forest as I please.”

## \|\| 3.9.46 \|\|

*itthaṃ tayoktamākarṇya puro'gacchaddvijātmajaḥ \|*  
*viciṃtya parihāsoktiṃ gacchati sma yathā purā \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. On hearing these words uttered by her, the other Brāhmaṇa boy thought that his friend was joking and continued his walk ahead as before.

## \|\| 3.9.47-48 \|\|

*punarapyāha sā bālā tiṣṭhatiṣṭha kva yāsyasi \|*  
*durutsahasmarāveśāṃ paribhoktumupetya mām \|\| 47 \|\|*

*pariṣvajasva māṃ kāṃtāṃ pāyayasva tavādharam \|*  
*nāhaṃ gaṃtuṃ samarthāsmi smarabāṇaprapīḍitā \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. Again the girl said: “Stop, stop. Where do you intend to go? Come and embrace me and enjoy me tormented inordinately by Smara (god of Love). I am your beloved. Let me kiss your lips and drink (the honey) thereof. I have been afflicted by the arrows of Smara. I am incapable of going ahead.”

## \|\| 3.9.49 \|\|

*itthamaśrutapūrvāṃ tāṃ niśamya pariśaṃkitaḥ \|*  
*āyāṃtīṃ pṛṣṭhato vīkṣya sahasā vismayaṃ gataḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. On hearing these words not heard before, he became suspicious. He looked behind and saw her proceeding towards him. He was immediately astonished.

## \|\| 3.9.50-51 \|\|

*kaiṣā padmapalāśākṣī pīnonnatapayodharā \|*  
*kṛśodarī bṛhacchroṇī navapallavakomalā \|\| 50 \|\|*

*sa eva me sakhā kinnu jāta eva varāṃganā \|*  
*pṛcchāmyenamataḥ sarvamiti saṃcintya so'bravīt \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51. ‘Who is this beautiful woman with eyes like petals of lotus, heavy protruding breasts, slender belly and bulging hips? She is as tender as sprouts. Is it possible that my friend has been changed into an excellent female? I shall ask him,’ Thinking thus he said:

## \|\| 3.9.52-53 \|\|

*kimapūrva ivābhāṣi sakhe rūpaguṇādibhiḥ \|*  
*apūrvaṃ bhāṣase vākyaṃ kāminīva samākulā \|\| 52 \|\|*

*yastvaṃ vedapurāṇajño brahmacārī jiteṃdriyaḥ \|*  
*sārasvatātmajaḥ śāṃtaḥ kathamevaṃ prabhāṣase \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. “O friend, you appear strange and unusual in form, features and qualities. You speak strange words like an excited lustful woman. You are a celibate religious student, conversant with Vedas and Purāṇas, son of Sārasvata, quiescent, with sense-organs controlled. Why do you speak like this?”

## \|\| 3.9.54-55 \|\|

*ityuktā sā punaḥ prāha nāhamasmi pumānprabho \|*  
*nāmnā sāmavatī bālā tavāsmi ratidāyinī \|\| 54 \|\|*

*yadi te saṃśayaḥ kāṃta mamāṃgāni vilokaya \|*  
*ityuktaḥ sahasā mārge rahasyenāṃ vyalokayat \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55a. On being addressed thus, she said: “O lord, I am not a man. I am a girl Sāmavatī by name. I am here to give you sexual pleasure. If, O my lover, you have any doubt, see my limbs.”

55b. On being told thus, the other boy secretly examined her.

## \|\| 3.9.56 \|\|

*tāmakṛtrimadhammillāṃ javanastanaśobhinīm \|*  
*surūpāṃ vīkṣya kāmena kiṃcidvyākulatāmagāt \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. On seeing her with natural luxuriant tresses of hair, beautiful with hips and breasts and comely in form, he become slightly agitated with love.

## \|\| 3.9.57 \|\|

*punaḥ saṃstabhya yatnena cetaso vikṛtiṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*muhūrtaṃ vismayāviṣṭo na kiṃcitpratyabhāṣata \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Soon the learned boy controlled himself with great effort, and subdued the straying mind. For a short while he was wonderstruck and did not say anything.

## \|\| 3.9.58 \|\|

*sāmavatyuvāca \|*  
*gataste saṃśayaḥ kaścittarhyāgaccha bhajasva mām \|*  
*paśyedaṃ vipinaṃ kāṃta parastrīsuratocitam \|\| 58 \|\|*

Sāmavatī said:

58\. I hope your doubt is set at rest. Then come on, enjoy me. See this forest, O dear lover, ideally suited for sexual dalliance with an excellent girl.

## \|\| 3.9.59 \|\|

*sumedhā uvāca \|*  
*maivaṃ kathaya maryādāṃ mā hiṃsīrmadamattavat \|*  
*āvāṃ vijñātaśāstrārthau tvamevaṃ bhāṣase katham \|\| 59 \|\|*

Sumedhā said:

59\. Do not speak like this. Do not violate the bounds of decency like an intoxicated one. Both of us have understood the scriptural texts fully. Why do you speak thus?

## \|\| 3.9.60 \|\|

*adhītasya ca śāstrasya vivekasya kulasya ca \|*  
*kimeṣa sadṛśo dharmo jāradharmaniṣevaṇam \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Is this adoption of the way of an (adulterous) paramour worthy of you who have studied scriptures, have power of discrimination, belong to a noble family?

## \|\| 3.9.61 \|\|

*na tvaṃ strī puruṣo vidvāñjānīhyātmānamātmanā \|*  
*ayaṃ svayaṃkṛto'nartha āvābhyāṃ yadviceṣṭitam \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. You are not a woman. You are a learned Brāhmaṇa. Know your own self through your own soul. Or is this a calamity invited by ourselves, because we did commit the blunder of deceiving the queen?

## \|\| 3.9.62 \|\|

*vaṃcayitvātmapitarau dhūrttarājānuśāsanāt \|*  
*kṛtvā cānucitaṃ karma tasyaitadbhujyate phalam \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. At the bidding of a roguish king, we have deceived our own parents. We have been guilty of impropriety of conduct, the fruit (result) of which is now reaped by us.

## \|\| 3.9.63 \|\|

*sarvaṃ tvanucitaṃ karma nṛṇāṃ śreyovināśanam \|*  
*yastvaṃ viprātmajo vidvāngataḥ strītvaṃ vigarhitam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. All improper acts are detrimental to the good of man. You who are born as the son of a Brāhmaṇa, a scholar, have undergone the despicable state of being a woman.

## \|\| 3.9.64 \|\|

*mārgaṃ tyaktvā gato'raṇyaṃ naro vidhyeta kaṇṭakaiḥ \|*  
*balārddhisyeta vā hiṃsrairyadā tyaktasamā gamaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. One who leaves off the beaten track and strays into a forest, is sure to be pricked with thorns. One who has abandoned the company of his own people, is sure to be injured by beasts of prey.

## \|\| 3.9.65 \|\|

*evaṃ vivekamāśritya tūṣṇīmehi svayaṃ gṛham \|*  
*devadvijaprasādena strītvaṃ tava vilīyate \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Hence be sensible and follow me to the house quietly. Perhaps, by the grace of gods and Brāhmaṇas, your womanhood will disappear.

## \|\| 3.9.66 \|\|

*athavā daivayogena strītvameva bhavettava \|*  
*pitrā dattā mayā sākaṃ raṃsyase varavarṇini \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Or, if ordained by fate, this womanhood clings to you, O lady of excellent complexion, you can have sexual dalliance with me after being given to me in marriage by your father.

## \|\| 3.9.67 \|\|

*aho citramaho duḥkhamaho pāpabalaṃ mahat \|*  
*aho rājñaḥ prabhāvoyaṃ śivārādhanasaṃbhṛtaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Alas! This is indeed a miracle! A misery! The disastrous effect of sinful behaviour! Or is it the power of the king, acquired by him as a result of the propitiation of Śiva?

## \|\| 3.9.68 \|\|

*ityuktāpyasakṛttena sā vadhūrativihvalā \|*  
*balena taṃ samāliṃgya cucuṃbādharapallavam \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Although admonished thus by him many times, that girl, in her agitated state, embraced him forcibly and kissed his sproutlike lips.

## \|\| 3.9.69 \|\|

*dharṣitopi tayā dhīraḥ sumedhā nūtanastriyam \|*  
*yatnādānīya sadanaṃ kṛtsnaṃ tatra nyavedayat \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Though molested thus by her, the bold Sumedhā somehow brought the newly transformed woman to their house and reported everything then.

## \|\| 3.9.70 \|\|

*tadākarṇyātha tau viprau kupitau śokavihvalau \|*  
*tābhyāṃ saha kumārābhyāṃ vaidarbhāṃtikamīyatuḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. On hearing this, the Brāhmaṇas became infuriated, besides being grief-stricken. Accompanied by those two boys, they came to the king of Vidarbha.

## \|\| 3.9.71-76 \|\|

*tataḥ sārasvataḥ prāha rājānaṃ dhūrtaceṣṭitam \|*  
*rājanmamātmajaṃ paśya tava śāsanayaṃtritam \|\| 71 \|\|*

*etau tavājñāvaśagau cakratuḥ karma garhitam \|*  
*matputrastatphalaṃ bhuṃkte strītvaṃ prāpya jugupsitam \|\| 72 \|\|*

*adya me saṃtatirnaṣṭā nirāśāḥ pitaro mama \|*  
*nāputrasya hi lokosti luptapiṃḍādisaṃskṛteḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

*śikhopavītamajinaṃ maujīṃ daṃḍaṃ kamaṃḍalum \|*  
*brahmacaryocitaṃ cihnaṃ vihāyemāṃ daśāṃ gataḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

*brahmasūtraṃ ca sāvitrīṃ snānaṃ saṃdhyāṃ japārcanam \|*  
*visṛjya strītvamāptosya kā gatirvada pārthiva \|\| 75 \|\|*

*tvayā me saṃtatirnaṣṭā naṣṭo vedapathaśca me \|*  
*ekātmajasya me rājankā gatirvada śāśvatī \|\| 76 \|\|*

71-76. Then Sārasvata said to the king who had perpetrated the roguish act:

“O king, see my son who obeyed your command. Acting at your bidding, these two perpetrated a despicable thing. It is my son who experiences the bitter fruit by turning into a woman that is hateful.

My family line is broken today. My ancestors have become disappointed. To one devoid of a son, no (heavenly) world is within reach, as the offering of balls of rice and other consecratory rites come to an end.

He has to forgo the lock of hair on the crown, the sacred thread, deerskin, girdle of Muñja grass, staff and water-pot which are all signs of a celibate religious student and to fall into this miserable plight.

The Brāhmaṇical cord, the Sāvitrī Mantra, the daily ablution, the performance of Sandhyā prayers, the Japa and the adoration—all these have been discarded, as he is transformed into a woman. O king, tell me, where has he to go for salvation?

On account of you, my family line is broken, the Vedic path has been lost. O king, tell me, can there be any permanent salvation for me, who have an only son?”

## \|\| 3.9.77 \|\|

*iti sārasvatenoktaṃ vākyamākarṇya bhūpatiḥ \|*  
*sīmaṃtinyāḥ prabhāveṇa vismayaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. On hearing the words spoken by Sārasvata the king was wonderstruck at the power of Sīmantinī.

## \|\| 3.9.78 \|\|

*atha sarvānsamāhūya maharṣīnamitadyutīn \|*  
*prasādya prārthayāmāsa tasya puṃstvaṃ mahīpatiḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Calling together all great sages of unmeasured lustre, the king propitiated them and requested them for the return of manhood to the boy.

## \|\| 3.9.79 \|\|

*te'buvannatha pārvatyāḥ śivasya ca samīhitam \|*  
*tadbhaktānāṃ ca māhātmyaṃ konyathā kartumīśvaraḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. They said: “Who can change the will of Pārvatī and Śiva and the greatness of their devotees?”

## \|\| 3.9.80-81 \|\|

*atha rājā bharadvājamādāya munipuṃgavam \|*  
*tābhyāṃ saha dvijāgryābhyāṃ tatsutābhyāṃ samanvitaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

*aṃbikābhavanaṃ prāpya bharadvājopadeśataḥ \|*  
*tāṃ devīṃ niyamaistīvrairupāste sma mahāniśi \|\| 81 \|\|*

80-81. Then the king took the great sage Bhāradvāja and at the instance of Bhāradvāja went to the temple of Aṃbikā accompanied by those two excellent Brāhmaṇas and their sons.

As per advice of Bhāradvāja, he served and worshipped the goddess with severe vows and observances.

## \|\| 3.9.82 \|\|

*evaṃ trirātraṃ suvisṛṣṭabhojanaḥ sa pārvatīdhyāna rato mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*samyakpraṇāmairvividhaiśca saṃstavairgaurīṃ prapannārtiharāmatoṣayat \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Thus, for three nights, the king eschewed completely his meals and remained engrossed in meditating upon Pārvatī. By obeisances and different kinds of prayers and hymns he propitiated Gaurī who removes the distress of those who seek refuge in her.

## \|\| 3.9.83 \|\|

*tataḥ prasannā sā devī bhaktasya pṛthivīpateḥ \|*  
*svarūpaṃ darśayāmāsa caṃdrakoṭisamaprabham \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. The goddess became pleased with the devout king, and to him revealed her form having the lustre of ten million moons.

## \|\| 3.9.84 \|\|

*athāha gaurī rājānaṃ kiṃ te brūhi samīhitam \|*  
*so'pyāha puṃstvametasya kṛpayā dīyatāmiti \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Then Gaurī asked the king: “Tell me, what do you wish?” He said: “The manhood of this boy may be restored.”

## \|\| 3.9.85 \|\|

*bhūyopyāha mahādevī madbhaktaiḥ karma yatkṛtam \|*  
*śakyate nānyathā kartuṃ varṣāyutaśatairapi \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. The great goddess said again: “What has been done by my devotees cannot be altered even in tens and hundreds of thousands of years.”

## \|\| 3.9.86 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*ekātmajo hi viproyaṃ karmaṇā naṣṭasaṃtatiḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ sukhaṃ prapadyeta vinā putreṇa tādṛśaḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

The king said:

86\. This Brāhmaṇa has an only son. Now his line has been broken on account of this event. How can such a man as this attain happiness without a son?

## \|\| 3.9.87 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*tasyānyo matprasādena bhaviṣyati sutottamaḥ \|*  
*vidyā vinayasaṃpanno dīrghāyuramalāśayaḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

The goddess said:

87\. With my favour he will have another excellent son endowed with learning and modesty. He will live long. He will be pure-hearted.

## \|\| 3.9.88 \|\|

*eṣā sāmavatī nāma sutā tasya dvijanmanaḥ \|*  
*bhūtvā sumedhasaḥ patnī kāmabhogena yujyatām \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. Let this daughter of that Brāhmaṇa, named Sāmavatī, be united in wedlock with Sumedhā and let her enjoy all pleasures of love.

## \|\| 3.9.89 \|\|

*ityuktvāṃtarhitā devī te ca rājapurogamāḥ \|*  
*gatāḥ svaṃsvaṃ gṛhaṃ sarve cakrustacchāsane sthitim \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. After saying this the goddess vanished. Those persons with the king at their head, went to their respective places, abiding by his order.

## \|\| 3.9.90 \|\|

*sopi sārasvato vipraḥ putraṃ pūrvasuto ttamam \|*  
*lebhe devyāḥ prasādena hyacirādeva kālataḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. The Brāhmaṇa Sārasvata ere-long obtained a son better than the previous one with the favour of the goddess.

## \|\| 3.9.91 \|\|

*tāṃ ca sāmavatīṃ kanyāṃ dadau tasmai sumedhase \|*  
*tau daṃpatī ciraṃ kālaṃ bubhujāte paraṃ sukham \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. He gave his daughter Sāmavatī to Sumedhā in marriage. For a long time the couple enjoyed happiness.

## \|\| 3.9.92 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ityeṣa śivabhaktāyāḥ sīmaṃtinyā nṛpastriyāḥ \|*  
*prabhāvaḥ kathitaḥ śaṃbhormāhātmyamapi varṇitam \|\| 92 \|\|*

Sūta said:

92\. Thus the power of Queen Sīmantinī, a great devotee of Śiva, has been narrated and the greatness of Śaṃbhu too described.

## \|\| 3.9.93 \|\|

*bhūyopi śivabhaktānāṃ prabhāvaṃ vismayāvaham \|*  
*samāsādvarṇayiṣyāmi śrotṝṇāṃ maṃgalāyanam \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. Further too I shall describe the power of Śiva’s devotees, striking one with wonder. I shall state it succinctly. To those who listen, it is a source of all auspiciousness.

## Chapter 10 - Bhadrāyu Resuscitated

## \|\| 3.10.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*vicitraṃ śivanirmāṇaṃ vicitra śivaceṣṭitam \|*  
*vicitraṃ śivamāhātmyaṃ vicitraṃ śivabhāṣitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: The aim of this chapter is to describe the efficacy of Bhasma (sacred ash). As usual the motif of rebirth is used as an explanation of the suffering of Bhadrāyu and his mother. Śivayogin who was served by them in the last birth resuscitates and cures Bhadrāyu and his mother

Sūta said:

1\. Astonishing is the constructive ability of Śiva. Miraculous is the activity of Śiva. Wonderful is the greatness of Śiva; wonderful is the utterance of Śiva.

## \|\| 3.10.2 \|\|

*vicitraṃ śivabhaktānāṃ caritaṃ pāpanāśanam \|*  
*svargāpavargayoḥ satyaṃ sādhanaṃ tadbravīmyaham \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Strange is the conduct of the devotees of Śiva; it is destructive of sins; verily it is the means of heavenly pleasures and salvation. I shall describe it.

## \|\| 3.10.3 \|\|

*avaṃtīviṣaye kaścidbrāhmaṇo maṃdarāhvayaḥ \|*  
*babhūva viṣayārāmaḥ strījito dhanasaṃgrahī \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. In the land of Avantī, there was a certain Brāhmaṇa named Mandra. He was of easy-going temperament in worldly affairs, one ruled by women and eager to amass wealth.

## \|\| 3.10.4 \|\|

*saṃdhyāsnāparityakto gaṃdhamālyāṃbarapriyaḥ \|*  
*kustrīsaktaḥ kumārgastho yathā pūrvamajāmilaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He had entirely abandoned Sandhyā prayers and regular ablutions. He was very fond of sweet scents, garlands and garments, attached to women of immoral ways, straying often into crooked paths like Ajāmila of yore.

## \|\| 3.10.5 \|\|

*sa veśyāṃ piṃgalāṃ nāma ramamāṇo divāniśam \|*  
*tasyā eva gṛhe nityamāsīdavijiteṃdriyaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. He hovered round a prostitute named Piṅgalā, sporting about with her day and night. Of uncontrolled passion, he constantly remained in her house itself.

## \|\| 3.10.6 \|\|

*kadācitsadane tasyāstasminnivasati dvije \|*  
*ṛṣabho nāma dharmātmā śivayogī samāyayau \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Once, while the Brāhmaṇa was staying in her house, a pious-souled Śivayogin named Ṛṣabha came there.

## \|\| 3.10.7 \|\|

*tamāgatamabhiprekṣya matvā svaṃ puṇyamūrjitam \|*  
*sā veśyā sa ca vipraśca paryapūjayatāmubhau \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Having seen him arrived and considering (his arrival) the result of their powerful merit, that harlot and the Brāhmaṇa, both of them worshipped him.

## \|\| 3.10.8 \|\|

*tamāropya mahāpīṭhe kaṃbalāṃbarasaṃbhṛte \|*  
*prakṣālya caraṇau bhaktyā tajjalaṃ dadhatuḥ śiraḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. They made him sit on a big pedestal covered with a shawl and a cloth. Devoutly they washed his feet and applied (sprinkled) the water over their head.

## \|\| 3.10.9 \|\|

*svāgatārghyanamaskārairgaṃdhapuṣpākṣatādibhiḥ \|*  
*upacāraiḥ samabhyarcya bhojayāmāsaturmudā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. They honoured him with various services by offering cordial welcome, Arghya, obeisance, sweet scents, flowers, raw rice grains etc. and joyously gave him a meal.

## \|\| 3.10.10 \|\|

*taṃ bhuktavaṃtamācāṃtaṃ paryaṃke sukhasaṃstare \|*  
*upaveśya mudā yuktau tāṃbūlaṃ pratyayacchatām \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. After he had taken his food and rinsed his mouth, they made him sit on a bedstead covered with a good bedsheet and offered him betel leaves.

## \|\| 3.10.11 \|\|

*pādasaṃvāhanaṃ bhaktyā kurvaṃtau daivaco ditau \|*  
*kalpayitvā tu śuśrūṣāṃ prīṇayāmāsatuściram \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Urged by an auspicious fate, they devoutly massaged his feet. By various acts of attendance and service, they entertained him for a long time.

## \|\| 3.10.12 \|\|

*evaṃ samarcitastābhyāṃ śivayogī mahādyutiḥ \|*  
*ativāhya niśāmekāṃ yayau prātastadādṛtaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Thus honoured by both of them, the Śivayogin of great splendour spent a night there and went away in the morning duly respected by them.

## \|\| 3.10.13 \|\|

*evaṃ kāle gataprāye sa vipro nidhanaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*sā ca veśyā mṛtā kāle yayau karmārjitāṃ gatim \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. As time went on thus, the Brāhmaṇa passed away and the harlot too died when the time came and attained a state deserved by her acts.

## \|\| 3.10.14 \|\|

*sa vipraḥ karmaṇā nīto daśārṇadharaṇīpateḥ \|*  
*vajrabāhukuṭuṃbinyāḥ sumatyā garbhamāsthitaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Carried by his own actions the Brāhmaṇa entered the womb of Sumati, wife of Vajrabāhu, king of Daśārṇa (Western Malwa, M.P.).

## \|\| 3.10.15 \|\|

*tāṃ jyeṣṭhapatnīṃ nṛpatergarbhasaṃpadamāśritām \|*  
*avekṣya tasyai garalaṃ sapatnyaśchadmanā daduḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. On seeing that senior queen blessed with pregnancy, the other queens, the cowives administered poison to her fraudulently.

## \|\| 3.10.16 \|\|

*sā bhuktvā garalaṃ ghoraṃ na mṛtā daivayogataḥ \|*  
*kleśameva paraṃ prāpa maraṇādatiduḥsaham \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Even after consuming that terrible poison, the queen did not die, as fate had ordained it. She had to undergo sufferings more unbearable than death.

## \|\| 3.10.17 \|\|

*atha kāle samāyāte putrame kamajījanat \|*  
*kleśena mahatā sādhvī pīḍitā varavarṇinī \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The chaste lady of excellent complexion was afflicted with great pain. At the proper time, she gave birth to a son.

## \|\| 3.10.18 \|\|

*sa nirdaśo rājaputraḥ spṛṣṭapūrvo gareṇa yat \|*  
*tenāvāpa mahākleśaṃ kraṃdamāno divāniśam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Barely more than ten days old, the prince who had already been affected by the poison, suffered the most acute pain and went on crying day and night.

## \|\| 3.10.19 \|\|

*tasya bālasya mātā ca sarvāṃgavraṇapīḍitā \|*  
*babhūvaturatikliṣṭau garayogaprabhāvataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The mother of the child was also afflicted with wounds all over the body. Thus both of them suffered acute pain as a result of the poison.

## \|\| 3.10.20 \|\|

*tau rājñā ca samānītau vaidyaiśca kṛtabheṣajau \|*  
*na svāsthyamāpaturyatnairanekairyojitairapi \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. They were taken to physicians and treatment was given. Despite a number of efforts they did not regain normal health.

## \|\| 3.10.21 \|\|

*na rātrau labhate nidrāṃ sā rājñī vipulavyathā \|*  
*svaputrasya ca duḥkhena duḥkhitā nitarāṃ kṛśā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The queen afflicted with severe pain never had sleep at night. She became further emaciated by being miserable due to the affliction of her son.

## \|\| 3.10.22 \|\|

*nītvaivaṃ katicinmāsānsa rājā mātṛputrakau \|*  
*jīvaṃtau ca mṛtaprāyau vilokyātmanyaciṃtayat \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. A few months passed by like this. On seeing the mother and the child alive but no better than dead, the king thought thus within himself.

## \|\| 3.10.23-24 \|\|

*etau me gṛhiṇīputrau nirayādāgatāviha \|*  
*aśrāṃtarogau kraṃdaṃtau nidrābhaṃgavidhāyinau \|\| 23 \|\|*

*atropāyaṃ kariṣyāmi pāpayordhruvametayoḥ \|*  
*martuṃ vā jīvituṃ vāpi na kṣamau pāpabhoginau \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. ‘These, my wife and son, have come here from the veritable hell. Crying out due to their incurable illness, they cause sleeplessness (to everyone). I shall have recourse to some means certainly in regard to these two sinners who cannot die or live. Let them suffer from their own sins.’

## \|\| 3.10.25 \|\|

*itthaṃ viniścitya ca bhūmipālaḥ saktaḥ sapatnīṣu tadātmajeṣu \|*  
*āhūya sūtaṃ nijadāraputrau nirvāpayāmāsa rathena dūram \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The king was enamoured of the other queens and their sons. Having decided thus, he called his charioteer and made him take them far away in the chariot.

## \|\| 3.10.26 \|\|

*tau sūtena parityaktau kutracidvijane vane \|*  
*avāpatuḥ parāṃ pīḍāṃ kṣuttṛḍbhyāṃ bhṛśavihvalau \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. They were abandoned somewhere in a lonely spot in the forest by the charioteer. Distressed very much by hunger and thirst, they suffered acute pain.

## \|\| 3.10.27 \|\|

*sodvahaṃtī nijaṃ bālaṃ nipataṃtī pade pade \|*  
*niḥśvasaṃtī nijaṃ karma niṃdaṃtī cakitā bhṛśam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Carrying the boy, she faltered at every step and gasped for breath; she trembled apprehensively and cursed her own previous actions (and fate).

## \|\| 3.10.28 \|\|

*kvacitkaṃṭakabhinnāṃgī muktakeśī bhayāturā \|*  
*kvacidvyāghrasvanairbhītā kvacidvyālairanudrutā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Now her limbs were pricked and bruised by thorns. Her hair was dishevelled. Now she took fright at the roaring sound of tigers. Now she was chased by pythons.

## \|\| 3.10.29 \|\|

*bhartsyamānā piśācaiśca vetālairbrahmarākṣasaiḥ \|*  
*mahāgulmeṣu dhāvaṃtī bhinnapādā kṣurāśmabhiḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. She was ridiculed and rebuked by ghosts, vampires and Brahmarākṣasas. Rushing through hedges, the soles of her feet were cut by razor-like sharp stones.

## \|\| 3.10.30 \|\|

*saivaṃ ghore mahāraṇye bhramaṃtī nṛpage hinī \|*  
*daivātprāptā vaṇiṅmārgaṃ govājinarasevitam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Wandering thus in the thick forest, the queen luckily reached the path of merchants frequented by cows, horses and men.

## \|\| 3.10.31 \|\|

*gacchaṃtī tena mārgeṇa sudūramatiyatnataḥ \|*  
*dadarśa vaiśyanagaraṃ vahustrīnarasevitam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Proceeding along that path a very long distance with stress and strain, she saw the city of Vaiśyas abounding in men and women.

## \|\| 3.10.32 \|\|

*tasya goptā mahāvaiśyo nagarasya mahājanaḥ \|*  
*asti padmākaro nāma rājarāja ivāparaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. There was a great Vaiśya named Padmākara who was an eminent merchant and leader of that city. He was as though another Kubera.

## \|\| 3.10.33 \|\|

*tasya vaiśyapateḥ kācidgṛhadāsī nṛpāṃganām \|*  
*āyāṃtī dūrato dṛṣṭvā tadaṃtikamupāyayau \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The domestic slave of that lord of Vaiśyas saw the queen coming from far. She approached her.

## \|\| 3.10.34 \|\|

*sā dāsī nṛpateḥ kāṃtāṃ saputrāṃ bhṛśapīḍitām \|*  
*svayaṃ viditavṛttāṃtā svāmine pratyadarśayat \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. After learning the full details herself, she introduced the suffering queen and her son to her lord and master.

## \|\| 3.10.35 \|\|

*sa tāṃ dṛṣṭvā viśāṃ nātho rujārttāṃ kliṣṭaputrakām \|*  
*nītvā rahasi suvyaktaṃ tadvṛttāṃtamapṛcchata \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. On seeing her excessively ill, herself burdened with a child that also was suffering much, he took them aside and himself asked the details specifically.

## \|\| 3.10.36 \|\|

*tayā niveditāśeṣavṛttāṃtaḥ sa vaṇikpatiḥ \|*  
*ahokaṣṭamiti jñātvā niśaśvāsa muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. She told him all the details. Realizing their pitiable plight, the leader of the Vaiśyas sighed repeatedly.

## \|\| 3.10.37 \|\|

*tāmaṃtike svagehasya saṃniveśya rahogṛhe \|*  
*vāsonnapānaśayanairmātṛsāmyamapūjayat \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Treating her like his own mother, he accommodated her in a secret apartment very near his house and honoured her with everything essential such as food, drink, clothes and bedding.

## \|\| 3.10.38 \|\|

*tasmingṛhe nṛpavadhūrnivasaṃtī surakṣitā \|*  
*vraṇayakṣmādirogāṇāṃ na śāṃtiṃ pratyapadyata \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Though the queen went on staying in that house well guarded and looked after, she did not find any relief from wounds, pulmonary consumption and other ailments.

## \|\| 3.10.39 \|\|

*tato dinaiḥ katipayaiḥ sa bālo vraṇapīḍitaḥ \|*  
*vilaṃghitabhiṣaksattvo mamāra ca vidhervaśāt \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Then, after a few days, as fate had destined it, the boy, afflicted with wounds died, setting at nought the efficacious treatment of all the physicians.

## \|\| 3.10.40 \|\|

*mṛte svatanaye rājñī śokena mahatāvṛtā \|*  
*mūrcchitā cāpatadbhūmau gajabhagneva vallarī \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. When her son died, the queen was excessively grieved. She fell into a swoon like a creeper dashed to the ground by an elephant.

## \|\| 3.10.41 \|\|

*daivātsaṃjñāmavāpyātha vāṣpaklinnapayodharā \|*  
*sāṃtvitā'pi vaṇikstrībhirvilalāpa suduḥkhitā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Luckily, she regained consciousness, but shed tears profusely drenching her breasts. Though the Vaiśya ladies nearby tried to console her, she lamented much in the excess of her sorrow.

## \|\| 3.10.42-43 \|\|

*hā tātatāta hā putra hā mama prāṇarakṣaka \|*  
*hā rājakulapūrṇendo hā mamānaṃdavardhana \|\| 42 \|\|*

*imāmanāthāṃ kṛpaṇāṃ tvatprāṇāṃ tyaktavabāṃdhavām \|*  
*mātaraṃ te parityajya kva yāto'si nṛpātmaja \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. “Oh dear one, dear one, Oh my son, Oh saviour of my life, a full moon unto the royal household and the delighter of my own self! But, Oh prince, where have you gone leaving me, your mother, helpless and miserable, already abandoned by all the kinsmen? Verily my vital breaths depend upon you.”

## \|\| 3.10.44 \|\|

*ityebhiruditairvākyaiḥ śokaciṃtāvivardhakaiḥ \|*  
*vilapaṃtīṃ mṛtāpatyāṃ ko nu sāṃtvayituṃ kṣamaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Who could have consoled that poor lady with a dead child? She continued to lament uttering words like these that increased the worries and sorrow (of others as well).

## \|\| 3.10.45 \|\|

*etasminsamaye tasyā duḥkhaśokacikitsakaḥ \|*  
*ṛṣabhaḥ pūrvamākhyātaḥ śivayogī samāyayau \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. In the mean time, Ṛṣabha, the Śivayogin, mentioned before, came there as the sole physician for her misery and sorrow.

## \|\| 3.10.46 \|\|

*sa yogī vaiśyanāthena sārghahastena pūjitaḥ \|*  
*tasyāḥ sakāśamagamacchocantyā idamabravīt \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. That Yogin was duly honoured by the leader of the Vaiśyas with the Arghya ready in his hands. He then went near her as she continued to lament and spoke thus:

## \|\| 3.10.47 \|\|

*ṛṣabha uvāca \|*  
*akasmātkimaho vatse roravīṣi vimūḍhadhīḥ \|*  
*ko jātaḥ katamo loke ko mṛto vada sāṃpratam \|\| 47 \|\|*

Ṛṣabha said:

47\. Oh dear child, why do you cry for no reason at all, with your intellect confounded and deluded? Who among many is born in the world? Who is dead? Tell me now.

## \|\| 3.10.48 \|\|

*amī dehādayo bhāvāstoyaphenasadharmakāḥ \|*  
*kvacidbhrāṃtiḥ kvacicchāṃtiḥ sthitirbhavati vā punaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. This body and other objects like it have characteristics similar to the bubbles of water. There is agitation and excitement in some place. There is peace elsewhere. There is restful state again.

## \|\| 3.10.49 \|\|

*ato'sminphenasadṛśe dehe pañcatvamāgate \|*  
*śokasyānavakāśatvānna śocaṃti vipaścitaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Hence when the bubble-like body vanishes in death, learned men do not feel sorry, because there is no scope or reason for that sorrow.

## \|\| 3.10.50 \|\|

*guṇairbhūtāni sṛjyaṃte bhrāmyaṃte nijakarmabhiḥ \|*  
*kālenātha vikṛṣyaṃte vāsanāyāṃ ca śerate \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Living beings are evolved by Guṇas (Sattva etc.). They wander about in accordance with their own Karmas. They are being dragged by Time (Death). They are involved in the Vāsanās (impressions left behind by Karmas).

## \|\| 3.10.51 \|\|

*māyayotpattimāyāṃti guṇāḥ sattvādayastrayaḥ \|*  
*taireva dehā jāyaṃte jātāstallakṣaṇāśrayāḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The three Guṇas including Sattva etc., take their origin from Māyā (delusion). The bodies are born due to them. Once born, they have the characteristics similar to those (of Māyā).

## \|\| 3.10.52 \|\|

*devatvaṃ yāni sattvena rajasā ca manuṣyatām \|*  
*tiryaktvaṃ tamasā jaṃturvāsanānugatovaśaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Helpless by itself, a creature chased by Vāsanā, attains godhood through Sattva; human form through Rajas and brute-hood through Tamas Guṇa.

## \|\| 3.10.53 \|\|

*saṃsāre vartamānesmiñjaṃtuḥ karmānubandhanāt \|*  
*durvibhāvyāṃ gatiṃ yāti sukhaduḥkhamayīṃ muhuḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The soul undergoes repeatedly states not easily foreseen, involving happiness and sorrow as consequences of the Karmas in the present worldly existence.

## \|\| 3.10.54 \|\|

*api kalpāyuṣāṃ teṣāṃ devānāṃ tu viparyayaḥ \|*  
*anekāmayabaddhānāṃ kā kathā naradehinām \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. There are ups and downs even in the case of Devas whose life span is of a duration of a Kalpa. In the case of human beings subject to innumerable ailments they are even more.

## \|\| 3.10.55 \|\|

*kecidvadaṃti dehasya kālameva hi kāraṇam \|*  
*karma kecidguṇānkeciddehaḥ sādhāraṇo hyayam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Some say that the cause of the body is Kāla (Time); some say that it is Karma; some say the Gaṇas bring about the body. But the body is common (to all).

## \|\| 3.10.56 \|\|

*kālakarmaguṇādhānaṃ pañcātmakamidaṃ vapuḥ \|*  
*jātaṃ dṛṣṭvā na hṛṣyaṃti na śocaṃti mṛtaṃ budhāḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. (On the whole) this body with five constituents (the elements) is a product of Kāl\[?\]. Karma and/or Guṇas. Learned men are not delighted on seeing one born nor are they worried on seeing it dead.

## \|\| 3.10.57 \|\|

*avyakte jāyate jaṃturavyakte ca pralīyate \|*  
*madhye vyaktavadābhāti jalabudbudasannibhaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. The creature is born in the unmanifest; it gets dissolved in the unmanifest; only in the middle does it appear to be visible (though transitory) like water bubbles.

## \|\| 3.10.58 \|\|

*yadā garbhagato dehī vināśaḥ kalpitastadā \|*  
*daivājjīvati vā jāto mriyate sahasaiva vā \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. The destruction of an embodied being is already decided the moment it enters the womb. As ordained by fate, after being born, it may continue to live or die all of a sudden.

## \|\| 3.10.59 \|\|

*garbhasthā eva naśyaṃti jātamātrāstathā pare \|*  
*kvacidyuvāno naśyaṃti mriyaṃte kepi vārdhake \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Some die within the womb; some are stillborn; others die immediately after birth; in some places young men die and in some when they attain old age.

## \|\| 3.10.60 \|\|

*yādṛśaṃ prāktanaṃ karma tādṛśaṃ viṃdate vapuḥ \|*  
*bhuṃkte tadanurūpāṇi sukhaduḥkhāni vai hyasau \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. The soul gets its body in accordance with its previous Karma; it experiences happiness and misery also in accordance with it (Karma).

## \|\| 3.10.61 \|\|

*māyānubhāveritayoḥ pitroḥ suratasaṃbhramāt \|*  
*deha utpadyate kopi puṃyoṣitklībalakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Some body takes shape when, urged by Māyā and its efficient energy, the parents indulge in a sexual act. This body (so born) may be male, female or eunuch.

## \|\| 3.10.62 \|\|

*āyuḥ sukhaṃ ca duḥkha ca puṇyaṃ pāpaṃ śrutaṃ dhanam \|*  
*lalāṭe likhitaṃ dhātrā vahañjaṃtuḥ prajāyate \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. A creature is born bearing the writing on his forehead by the Creator, specifying his span of life, and extent of happiness, misery, merit, sin, learning and assets.

## \|\| 3.10.63 \|\|

*karmaṇāmavilaṃghyatvātkālasyāpyanatikramāt \|*  
*anityatvācca bhāvānāṃ na śokaṃ kartumarhasi \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. It does not behove you to grieve over anything as the (eff ects or fruits of) Karmas cannot be evaded, Kāla (god of Death) cannot be dodged and no object is permanent.

## \|\| 3.10.64 \|\|

*kva svapne niyataṃ sthairyamiṃdrajāle kva satyatā \|*  
*kva nityatā śaranmeghe kva śaśvattvaṃ kalevare \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Where is fixity and stability in a dream? Where is truth and permanence in a magic feat? Where is the continuity in autumnal clouds? Where is perpetuity in the physical body?

## \|\| 3.10.65 \|\|

*tava janmānyatītāni śatakoṭyayutāni ca \|*  
*ajānaṃtyāḥ paraṃ tattvaṃ saṃprāpto'yaṃ mahāśramaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Your previous lives are hundreds, thousands and millions. Since you do not know the ultimate truth, you have thus great misapprehension and delusion.

## \|\| 3.10.66 \|\|

*kasyakasyāsi tanayā jananī kasyakasya vā \|*  
*kasyakasyāsi gṛhiṇī bhavakoṭiṣu varttinī \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. (You do not know) to whom you have been a daughter? To whom have you been a mother? To whom you had been a wife in your transmigration through millions of births?

## \|\| 3.10.67 \|\|

*pañcabhūtātmako dehastvagasṛṅmāṃsabandhanaḥ \|*  
*medomajjāsthinicito viṇmūtraśleṣmabhājanam \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. The body is constituted of the five elements. The skin, the blood and the flesh make it stay together. It is filled and overspread by suets, marrow and bones. It is the receptacle of urine, faeces and phlegm.

## \|\| 3.10.68 \|\|

*śarīrāṃtaramapyetannijadehodbhavaṃ malam \|*  
*mattvā svatanayaṃ mūḍhe mā śokaṃ kartumarhasi \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. O deluded woman! It does not behove you to feel sorry if you consider your son as another body—a waste product of your own body.

## \|\| 3.10.69 \|\|

*yadi nāma janaḥ kaścinmṛtyuṃ tarati yatnataḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ tarhi vipadyeransarve pūrve vipaścitaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. If anyone can surmount death by means of efforts, how do you account for the death and disaster of all those learned men of yore?

## \|\| 3.10.70 \|\|

*tapasā vidyayā buddhyā mantrauṣadhirasāyanaiḥ \|*  
*atiyāti paraṃ mṛtyuṃ na kaścidapi paṃḍitaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. No learned man can avoid ultimate death by means of penance, learning, intelligence, spells, herbs and elixirs.

## \|\| 3.10.71 \|\|

*ekasyādya mṛtirjaṃtoḥ śvaścānyasya varānane \|*  
*tasmādanityāvayave na tvaṃ śocitumarhasi \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. One creature faces death today; another tomorrow, O lady of excellent countenance. Hence, as to the death or destruction of the body, of perishable organs, you do not deserve to feel sorry.

## \|\| 3.10.72 \|\|

*nityaṃ sannihito mṛtyuḥ kiṃ sukhaṃ vada dehinām \|*  
*vyāghre puraḥ sthite grāsaḥ paśūnāṃ kiṃ nu rocate \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Death is ever present at hand. Tell me where is (can be) the happiness of embodied beings. When a tiger stands before them, do beasts relish their mouthfuls of fodder?

## \|\| 3.10.73 \|\|

*ato janmajarāṃ jetuṃ yadīcchasi varānane \|*  
*śaraṇaṃ vraja sarveśaṃ mṛtyuṃjayamumāpatim \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Hence, O lady of excellent countenance, if you wish to conquer birth and old age, seek refuge in Umā’s Consort, the Lord of all, the conqueror of Death.

## \|\| 3.10.74 \|\|

*tāvanmṛtyubhayaṃ ghoraṃ tāvajjanmajarābhayam \|*  
*yāvanno yāti śaraṇaṃ dehī śivapadāṃbujam \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. As long as an embodied being does not seek shelter in the lotus-like feet of Śiva, so long will he face the terrible fear of death, the fear from birth and old age.

## \|\| 3.10.75 \|\|

*anubhūyeha duḥkhāni saṃsāre bhṛśadāruṇe \|*  
*mano yadā viyujyeta tadā dhyeyo maheśvaraḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. When the mind becomes detached and devoid of cravings, after experiencing miseries in the extremely terrible world, Maheśvara should be meditated upon.

## \|\| 3.10.76 \|\|

*manasā pibataḥ puṃsaḥ śivadhyānarasāmṛtam \|*  
*bhūyastṛṣṇā na jāyeta saṃsāraviṣayāsave \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. To a person mentally imbibing the juicy elixir of meditation of Śiva, there cannot be any lurking thirst for the liquor of mundane affairs.

## \|\| 3.10.77 \|\|

*vimuktaṃ sarvasaṃgaiśca mano vairāgyayaṃtritam \|*  
*yadā śivapade magnaṃ tadā nāsti punarbhavaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. When the mind is rid of all entanglements and is restrained by absence of desire and when it is turned towards the feet of Śiva, a being has no further birth.

## \|\| 3.10.78 \|\|

*tasmādidaṃ mano bhadre śivadhyānaikasādhanam \|*  
*śokamohasamāviṣṭaṃ mā kuruṣva śivaṃ bhaja \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Hence, O fair lady, do not make your mind affected with grief and delusion. It is the sole means for you to meditate on Śiva. Worship Śiva.

## \|\| 3.10.79 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*itthaṃ sānunayaṃ rājñī bodhitā śivayoginā \|*  
*pratyācaṣṭa gurostasya praṇamya caraṇāṃ bujam \|\| 79 \|\|*

Sūta said:

79\. Thus enlightened by the Śivayogin with consoling words, the queen bowed down to the lotus-like feet of the preceptor and replied.

## \|\| 3.10.80 \|\|

*rājñyuvāca \|*  
*bhagavanmṛtaputrāyāstyaktāyāḥ priyabandhubhiḥ \|*  
*mahārogāturāyā me kā gatirmaraṇaṃ vinā \|\| 80 \|\|*

The queen said:

80\. What other goal can I have except death, O holy Sir? My son is dead. I have been forsaken by all my kinsmen. Further, I am distressed by a fell disease.

## \|\| 3.10.81 \|\|

*ato'haṃ martumicchāmi sahaiva śiśunā'munā \|*  
*kṛtārthāhaṃ yadadya tvāmapaśyaṃ maraṇonmukhī \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Hence I wish to die following this child. I am contented and have achieved my object inasmuch as I have seen you today at the moment of my death.

## \|\| 3.10.82 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*iti tasyā vacaḥ śrutvā śivayogī dayānidhiḥ \|*  
*pūrvopakāraṃ saṃsmṛtya mṛtasyāṃtikamāyayau \|\| 82 \|\|*

Sūta said:

82\. On hearing her words, the Śivayogin, a storehouse of mercy, remembered the previous service and approached the dead body.

## \|\| 3.10.83 \|\|

*sa tadā bhasma saṃgṛhya śivamantrābhimaṃtritam \|*  
*vidīrṇe tanmukhe kṣiptvā mṛtaṃ prāṇairayojayat \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. He took some ash previously charged with Śiva’s Mantras, and scattered it into his open mouth. He united the dead body with vital breaths.

## \|\| 3.10.84 \|\|

*sa bālaḥ saṃgataḥ prāṇaiḥ śanairunmīlya locane \|*  
*prāptapūrvendriyabalo ruroda stanyakāṃkṣayā \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. That boy regaining the vital breaths opened his eyes slowly. Having got back the strength of his sense-organs as before, he cried out with a desire for breast-milk.

## \|\| 3.10.85 \|\|

*mṛtasya punarutthānaṃ vīkṣya bālasya vismitāḥ \|*  
*janā mumudire sarve nagareṣu purogamāḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. On seeing the resuscitation of the dead boy, all the people were struck with wonder. The leading citizens became glad.

## \|\| 3.10.86 \|\|

*athānaṃdabharā rājñī vihvalonmattalocanā \|*  
*jagrāha tanayaṃ śīghraṃ bāṣpavyākulalocanā \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. The queen was filled with delight. Her eyes became excited as though she was intoxicated. With eyes welling with tears, she quickly caught hold of her son.

## \|\| 3.10.87 \|\|

*upaguhya tadā tanvī paramānaṃdanirvṛtā \|*  
*na vedātmānamanyaṃ vā suṣupteva pariśramāt \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Embracing him, she reached the highest point of bliss. Like one in sound sleep after a laborious work, she did not know herself or others.

## \|\| 3.10.88 \|\|

*punaśca ṛṣabho yogī tayormātṛkumārayoḥ \|*  
*viṣavraṇayutaṃ dehaṃ bhasmanaiva parāmṛśat \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. Further, Ṛṣabha, the Yogin, applied the ash on the body of the mother as well as on that of the son, which were covered with poisonous wounds.

## \|\| 3.10.89 \|\|

*tau ca tadbhasmanā spṛṣṭau prāptadivyakalevarau \|*  
*devānāṃ sadṛśaṃ rūpaṃ dadhatuḥ kāṃtibhūṣitam \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. When the ash was thus applied, the bodies became transformed into divine ones. Their forms became lustrous like those of Devas.

## \|\| 3.10.90 \|\|

*saṃprāpte tridivaiśvarye yatsukhaṃ puṇyakarmaṇām \|*  
*tasmācchataguṇaṃ prāpa sā rājñī sukhamuttamam \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. The excellent pleasure of the queen was hundred times more than the happiness of the people of meritorious deeds when heavenly pleasures and prosperity are bestowed on them.

## \|\| 3.10.91 \|\|

*tāṃ pādayornipatitāmṛṣabhaḥ premavihvalaḥ \|*  
*utthāpyāśvāsayāmāsa duḥkhairmuktāmuvāca ha \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. When she fell at his feet, the affectionate Yogin Ṛṣabha lifted her up and consoled her. When she was fully free from misery he said:

## \|\| 3.10.92-94 \|\|

*ayi vatse mahārājñi jīvatvaṃ śāśvatīḥ samāḥ \|*  
*yāvajjīvasi lokesminna tāvatprāpsyase jarām \|\| 92 \|\|*

*eṣa te tanayaḥ sādhvi bhadrāyuriti nāmataḥ \|*  
*khyātiṃ yāsyati lokeṣu nijaṃ rājyamavāpsyati \|\| 93 \|\|*

*asya vaiśyasya sadane tāvattiṣṭha śucismite \|*  
*yāvadeṣa kumāraste prāptavidyo bhaviṣyati \|\| 94 \|\|*

92-94.“O child! O great queen! Live for endless years. As long as you are alive, you will never meet with old age. O chaste lady, this son of yours will become renowned by the name Bhadrāyu. He will regain his (lost) kingdom. O lady of pure smiles, continue to stay in the apartment of the Vaiśya till your son completes his study.”

## \|\| 3.10.95 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|\| \|*  
*iti tāmṛṣabho yogī taṃ ca rājakumārakam \|*  
*saṃjīvya bhasmavīryeṇa yayau deśānyathepsitān \|\| 95 \|\|*

Sūta said:

95\. Thus reviving the prince by the efficacy of the ash, the Yogin, Ṛṣabha, went away to the land of his choice.

## Chapter 11 - Ṛṣabha’s Advice to Bhadrāyu

## \|\| 3.11.1-2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*piṃgalā nāma yā veśyā mayā pūrvamudāhṛtā \|*  
*śivabhaktārcanātpuṇyāttyaktvā pūrvakalevaram \|\| 1 \|\|*

*candrāṃgadasya sā bhūyaḥ sīmaṃtinyāmajāyata \|*  
*rūpaudāryaguṇopetā nāmnā vai kīrtimālinī \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1-2. I have already spoken to you about the harlot named Piṅgalā. Due to the merit of the worship of Śiva, after leaving off the old body, she was reborn as daughter of Sīmantinī, wife of Candrāṅgada. She was endowed with physical beauty and liberal-mindedness. She was known by the name Kīrtimālinī.

## \|\| 3.11.3 \|\|

*bhadrāyurapi tatraiva rājaputro vaṇikpateḥ \|*  
*vavṛdhe sadane bhānuḥ śucāviva mahātapāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. In the apartment of the prominent Vaiśya, Prince Bhadrāyu grew up endowed with excessive refulgence like the sun in summer.

## \|\| 3.11.4 \|\|

*tasyāpi vaiśyanāthasya kumārastveka uttamaḥ \|*  
*sa nāmnā sunayaḥ prokto rājasūnoḥ sakhā'bhavat \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The prominent Vaiśya had an excellent son named Sunaya. He became companion of the prince.

## \|\| 3.11.5 \|\|

*tāvubhau paramasnigdhau rājavaiśyakumārakau \|*  
*citrakrīḍāvudārāṃgau ratnābharaṇamaṃḍitau \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The prince and the Vaiśya boy were intimate friends. Lovely in limbs and bedecked in gemset ornaments, they used to play about in diverse ways.

## \|\| 3.11.6 \|\|

*tasya rājakumārasya brāhmaṇaiḥ sa vaṇikpatiḥ \|*  
*saṃskārānkārayāmāsa svaputrasyāpi vistarāt \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The prominent Vaiśya got all the consecratory rites of the prince as well as his own son performed through Brāhmaṇas on an elaborate scale.

## \|\| 3.11.7 \|\|

*kāle kṛtopanayanau guruśuśrūṣaṇe ratau \|*  
*cakratuḥ sarvavidyānāṃ saṃgrahaṃ vinayānvitau \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Their sacred thread ceremony was celebrated at the proper age. Engrossed in attending upon their preceptor in all humility, they mastered various branches of learning one by one.

## \|\| 3.11.8 \|\|

*atha rājakumārasya prāpte ṣoḍaśahāyane \|*  
*sa eva ṛṣabho yogī tasya veśmanyupāyayau \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. When the prince completed his sixteenth year, the same Yogin, Ṛṣabha, came to his abode.

## \|\| 3.11.9 \|\|

*sā rājñī sa kumāraśca śivayoginamāgatam \|*  
*muhurmuhuḥ praṇamyobhau pūjayāmāsaturmudā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The queen and the prince repeatedly bowed down to the Śivayogin and gladly adored him.

## \|\| 3.11.10 \|\|

*tābhyāṃ ca pūjitaḥ so'tha yogīśo hṛṣṭamānasaḥ \|*  
*taṃ rājaputramuddiśya babhāṣe karuṇārdradhīḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Duly honoured by both of them, the eminent Yogin became pleased in his mind. With a compassionate heart, he spoke addressing the prince:

## \|\| 3.11.11 \|\|

*śivayogyuvāca \|*  
*kaccitte kuśalaṃ tāta tvanmātuścāpyanāmayam \|*  
*kaccittvaṃ sarvavidyānāmakārṣīśca pratigraham \|\| 11 \|\|*

Śivayogin said:

11\. O dear boy, I hope you are hail and hearty. I hope your mother is free from illness. I have no doubt that you have learnt all arts and sciences.

## \|\| 3.11.12 \|\|

*kaccidgurūṇāṃ satataṃ śuśrūṣātatparo bhavān \|*  
*kaccitsmarasi māṃ tāta tava prāṇapradaṃ gurum \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. I believe you are always eager to serve your preceptors. Don’t you remember me, your preceptor who brought you back to life?

## \|\| 3.11.13 \|\|

*evaṃ vadati yogīśe rājñī sā vinayānvitā \|*  
*svaputraṃ pādayostasya nipātyainamabhāṣata \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. When the chief of Yogins said thus, the queen in all humility made her son fall at his feet and spoke thus:

## \|\| 3.11.14-15 \|\|

*eṣa putrastava guro tvamasya prāṇadaḥ pitā \|*  
*eṣa śiṣyastu saṃgrāhyo bhavatā karuṇātmanā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*ato bandhubhirutsṛṣṭamanāthaṃ paripālaya \|*  
*asmai samyaksatāṃ mārgamupadeṣṭuṃ tvamarhasi \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. “O preceptor, this is your son. You are his father as you resuscitated him. He may please be accepted by you sympathetically as your disciple. Hence extend your protection to him who is helpless, being virtually abandoned by his kinsmen. It behoves you to instruct him duly in the path of the good.”

## \|\| 3.11.16 \|\|

*iti prasādito rājñyā śivayogī mahāmatiḥ \|*  
*tasmai rājakumārāya sanmārgamupadiṣṭavān \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Thus propitiated by the queen, the highly intelligent Śivayogin instructed the prince in the noble way of living.

## \|\| 3.11.17 \|\|

*ṛṣabha uvāca \|*  
*śrutismṛtipurāṇeṣu prokto dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ \|*  
*varṇāśramānurūpeṇa niṣevyaḥ sarvadā janaiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

Ṛṣabha said:

\[Note: VV. 17 ff give the prevalent concepts of Sadācāra for a prince.\]

17\. The eternal Dharma (righteous conduct) has been laid down in Śrutis, Smṛtis and Purāṇas. It has to be always resorted to by people in a manner according to one’s specific caste and stage of life.

## \|\| 3.11.18 \|\|

*bhaja vatsa satāṃ mārgaṃ sadeva caritaṃ cara \|*  
*na devājñāṃ vilaṃghethā mā kārṣīrdevahelanam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Resort to the path of the good, dear boy. Follow the conduct of life of good people. Do not disobey the command of Devas. Do not slight Devas contemptuously.

## \|\| 3.11.19 \|\|

*godevaguruvipreṣu bhaktimānbhava sarvadā \|*  
*cāṃḍālamapi saṃprāptaṃ sadā saṃbhāvayātithim \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Always entertain devotion to cows, Devas, preceptors and Brāhmaṇas. Even if a Cāṇḍāla comes as a guest, honour him suitably on all occasions.

## \|\| 3.11.20 \|\|

*satyaṃ na tyaja sarvatra prāpte'pi prāṇasaṃkaṭe \|*  
*gobrāhmaṇānāṃ rakṣārthamasatyaṃ tvaṃ vada kvacit \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Do not abandon truth on any occasion even when your very life is endangered. But on occasions do not hesitate to utter a lie for the sake of preserving the lives of cows and Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 3.11.21 \|\|

*parasveṣu parastrīṣu devabrāhmaṇa vastuṣu \|*  
*tṛṣṇāṃ tyaja mahābāho durlabheṣvapi vastuṣu \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O mighty one, give up greed and covetousness in respect to other men’s assets and wives, the properties of gods and Brāhmaṇas and rare objects.

## \|\| 3.11.22 \|\|

*satkathāyāṃ sadācāre sadvrate ca sadāgame \|*  
*dharmādisaṃgrahe nityaṃ tṛṣṇāṃ kuru mahāmate \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O highly intelligent one, show earnestness and eagerness in respect to stories of saintly persons, conduct of gods, vows and observances of the good, scriptures of the good and practice of pious rituals.

## \|\| 3.11.23 \|\|

*snāne jape ca home ca svādhyāye pitṛtarpaṇe \|*  
*godevātithipūjāsu nirālasyo bhavānagha \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. O sinless one, be free from slothfulness in respect to the daily bath, Japa, Homa, study of the Vedas, libations to the ancestors and the worship of cows, gods and guests.

## \|\| 3.11.24 \|\|

*krodhaṃ dveṣaṃ bhayaṃ śāṭhyaṃ paiśunya masadāgraham \|*  
*kauṭilyaṃ daṃbhamudvegaṃ yatnena parivarjaya \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Scrupulously avoid anger, hatred, fear, stubbornness, backbiting, persistence in evil, crookedness, arrogance and agitated excitement.

## \|\| 3.11.25 \|\|

*kṣātradharmarato'pi tvaṃ vṛthā hiṃsāṃ parityaja \|*  
*śuṣkavairaṃ vṛthālāpaṃ paranidāṃ ca varjaya \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. You may very well follow the duties of a Kṣatriya, but avoid unnecessary and purposeless injury to others. Eschew futile enmity, useless talk and slandering others.

## \|\| 3.11.26-28 \|\|

*mṛgayā dyūtapāneṣu strīṣu strīvijiteṣu ca \|*  
*atyāhāramatikrodhamatinidrāmatiśramam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*atyālāpamatikrīḍāṃ sarvadā parivarjaya \|\| 27 \|\|*

*atividyāmatiśraddhāmatipuṇyamatismṛtim \|*  
*atyutsāhamatikhyātimatidhairyaṃ ca sādhaya \|\| 28 \|\|*

26-28. Always try to avoid hunting, game of dice, drinking bouts, women and cuckolds. Always refrain from too much of eating, too much of talk and too much of play. Try to achieve the maximum of learning, utmost faith, highest merit, keenness in memory, earnestness, extensive popularity and unflinching courage.

## \|\| 3.11.29 \|\|

*sakāmo nijadāreṣu sakrodho nija śatruṣu \|*  
*salobhaḥ puṇyanicaye sābhyasūyo hyadharmiṣu \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Be steadfast in the love of your own wife; be wrathful towards your enemies; be covetous of gathering merit; and cultivate intolerance towards the unrighteous.

## \|\| 3.11.30 \|\|

*sadveṣo bhava pākhaṇḍe sarāgaḥ sajjaneṣu ca \|*  
*durbodho bhava durmaṃtre badhiraḥ piśunoktiṣu \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Be hostile to heresy; be friendly to the good; don’t be led away by evil counsels; and be deaf to the words of a backbiter.

## \|\| 3.11.31 \|\|

*dhūrttaṃ caṃḍaṃ śaṭhaṃ krūraṃ kitavaṃ capalaṃ khalam \|*  
*patitaṃ nāstikaṃ jihmaṃ dūrataḥ parivarjaya \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Shun from a great distance, a rogue, the wrathful, the perfidious, the ruthless, the deceitful, the fickle and the wicked, so also the fallen, an atheist and the crooked.

## \|\| 3.11.32 \|\|

*ātmapraśaṃsā mā kārṣīḥ parijñāteṃgito bhava \|*  
*dhane sarvakuṭuṃbe ca nātyāsaktaḥ sadā bhava \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Do not boast about yourself; understand the implications of hints and gestures; do not be very much attached to wealth and the entire family.

## \|\| 3.11.33 \|\|

*patnyāḥ pativratāyāśca jananyāḥ śvaśurasya ca \|*  
*satāṃ gurośca vacane viśvāsaṃ kuru sarvadā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Always have faith in the words of your chaste wife, mother, father-in-law, good people, and preceptor.

## \|\| 3.11.34 \|\|

*ātmarakṣāparo nityamapramatto dṛḍhavrataḥ \|*  
*viśvāsaṃ naiva kurvīthāḥ svabhṛtyeṣvapi kutra cit \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Be alert in guarding yourself; be unerring, steadfast in your observances; do not place too much of faith even in your servants at any cost.

## \|\| 3.11.35 \|\|

*viśvastaṃ mā vadhīḥ kaṃcidapi coraṃ mahāmate \|*  
*apāpeṣu na śaṃkethāḥ satyānna calito bhava \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. O highly intelligent one, do not kill one who has trusted you, even if he happens to be a thief; do not be suspicious of sinless ones; do not swerve from the path of truth.

## \|\| 3.11.36 \|\|

*anāthaṃ kṛpaṇaṃ vṛddhaṃ striyaṃ bālaṃ nirāgasam \|*  
*parirakṣa dhanaiḥ prāṇairbuddhyā śaktyā balena ca \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. With money, life, intellect, power and strength protect the helpless, the miserable, the old, women, children and the innocent.

## \|\| 3.11.37-38 \|\|

*api śatruṃ vadhasyārhaṃ mā vadhīḥ śaraṇāgatam \|*  
*apyapātraṃ supātraṃ vā nīco vāpi mahattamaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*yo vā ko vāpi yāceta tasmai dehi śiropi ca \|*  
*api yatnena mahatā kīrtimeva sadārjaya \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. Do not kill even an enemy worthy of being killed, if he seeks refuge in you; give up even your head if anyone earnestly begs for it, be he one deserving it or not deserving it, mean or noble. Exerting with great effort always earn fame.

## \|\| 3.11.39 \|\|

*rājñāṃ ca viduṣāṃ caiva kīrtireva hi bhūṣaṇam \|*  
*satkīrtiprabhavā lakṣmīḥ puṇyaṃ satkīrtisaṃbhavam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Fame alone is the ornament of kings and learned men. Prosperity comes out of good fame. Merit results from good fame.

## \|\| 3.11.40-42 \|\|

*satkīrtyā rājate lokaścaṃdraścaṃdrikayā nyathā \|*  
*gajāśvahemanicayaṃ ratnarāśiṃ nagopamam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*akīrtyopahataṃ sarvaṃ tṛṇavanmuṃca satvaram \|*  
*mātuḥ kopaṃ pituḥ kopaṃ guroḥ kopaṃ dhanavya yam \|\| 41 \|\|*

*putrāṇāmaparādhaṃ ca brāhmaṇānāṃ kṣamasva bhoḥ \|*  
*yathā dvijaprasādaḥ syāttathā teṣāṃ hitaṃ cara \|\| 42 \|\|*

40-42. The world shines with good reputation like the moon with the moonlight. Give up like an insignificant blade of grass, collections of elephants, horses and gold as well as mountain-like heaps of jewels, if they are defiled by ignominy.

Oh, forgive the anger of the mother, the fury of the father, the wrath of the preceptor, wastage of wealth by sons, and the guilt of Brāhmaṇas. Do what is beneficial to them in such a way that the favour of Brāhmaṇas is ensured.

## \|\| 3.11.43-45 \|\|

*rājānaṃ saṃkaṭe magnamuddhareyurdvijottamā \|*  
*āyuryaśo balaṃ saukhyaṃ dhanaṃ puṇyaṃ prajonnatiḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*karmaṇā yena jāyeta tatsevyaṃ bhavatā sadā \|*  
*deśaṃ kālaṃ ca śaktiṃ ca kāryaṃ cā kāryameva ca \|\| 44 \|\|*

*samyagvicārya yatnena kuru kāryaṃ ca sarvadā \|*  
*na kuryāḥ kasyacidbādhāṃ parabādhāṃ nivāraya \|\| 45 \|\|*

43-45. Excellent Brāhmaṇas should extricate the king entangled in difficulties. You must always resort to that activity whereby longevity, fame, power, happiness, wealth, merit and progress of the subjects can be ensured.

Consider carefully the place, the time, the power, what should be done and what should not be done and ardently do that always which should be done. Do not offend anyone. Avoid harassment of others.

## \|\| 3.11.46-48 \|\|

*corānduṣṭāṃśca bādhethāḥ sunītyā śaktimattayā \|*  
*snāne jape ca home ca daive pitrye ca karmaṇi \|\| 46 \|\|*

*atvaro bhava nidrāyāṃ bhojane bhava satvaraḥ \|*  
*dākṣiṇyayuktamaśaṭhaṃ satyaṃ janamanoharam \|\| 47 \|\|*

*alpākṣaramanaṃtārthaṃ vākyaṃ brūhi mahāmate \|*  
*abhīto bhava sarvatra vipakṣeṣu vipatsu ca \|\| 48 \|\|*

46-48. Attack thieves and the wicked by means of good policy and enforcement of power (at the proper time and place).

Do not be in a hurry with respect to daily ablution, Japa, Homa, and the rites pertaining to Devas and ancestors. But do not make haste to go to sleep and be quick in finishing (your) meal.

O highly intelligent one, always utter words full of civility and politeness, but not befitting a rogue, truthful, pleasing to the minds of the people and few but meaningful. Be fearless everywhere—in regard to enemies and adversities.

## \|\| 3.11.49-59 \|\|

*bhīto bhava brahmakule na pāpe guruśāsane \|*  
*jñātibaṃdhuṣu vipreṣu bhāryāsu tanayeṣu ca \|\| 49 \|\|*

*samabhāvena vartethāstathā bhojanapaṃktiṣu \|*  
*satāṃ hitopadeśeṣu tathā puṇya kathāsu ca \|\| 50 \|\|*

*vidyāgoṣṭhīṣu dharmyāsu kvacinmā bhūḥ parāṅmukhaḥ \|*  
*śucau puṇyajalasyāṃte prakhyāte brahmasaṃkule \|\| 51 \|\|*

*mahādeśe śivamaye vastavyaṃ bhavatā sadā \|*  
*kulaṭā gaṇikā yatra yatra tiṣṭhati kāmukaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*durdeśe nīcasaṃbādhe kadācidapi mā vasa \|*  
*ekamevāśritopi tvaṃ śivaṃ tribhuvaneśvaram \|\| 53 \|\|*

*sarvāndevānupāsīthāstaddināni ca mānayan \|*  
*sadā śuciḥ sadā dakṣaḥ sadā śāṃtaḥ sadā sthiraḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*sadā vijita ṣaḍvargaḥ sadaikāṃto bhavānagha \|*  
*viprānvedavidaḥ śāṃtānyatīṃśca niyatojvalān \|\| 55 \|\|*

*yugmam \|*  
*puṇyavṛkṣānpuṇyanadīḥ puṇyatīrthaṃ mahatsaraḥ \|*  
*dhenuṃ ca vṛṣabhaṃ ratnaṃ yuvatīṃ ca pativratām \|\| 56 \|\|*

*ātmano gṛhadevāṃśca sahasaiva namaskuru \|*  
*utthāya samaye brāhme svācamya vimalāśayaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*namaskṛtyātmaguruve dhyātvā devamumāpatim \|*  
*nārāyaṇaṃ ca lakṣmīśaṃ brahmāṇaṃ ca vināyakam \|\| 58 \|\|*

*skandaṃ kātyāyanīṃ devīṃ mahālakṣmīṃ sarasvatīm \|*  
*indrādīnatha lokeśānpuṇyaślokānṛṣīnapi \|\| 59 \|\|*

49-53a. Be afraid of the Brāhmaṇa community but do not be so in stern administration (in dispensing justice).

You must treat equally kinsmen, relatives, Brāhmaṇas, wives and sons (not partial to one against another of the same type). So also treat alike all the persons sitting for food in a row.

Do not be averse to good advices of excellent persons, to meritorious stories, to learned discussions of a virtuous nature.

You must always stay in places of purity and near spots of sacred waters, near sacred Tīrthas, in famous places, in places abounding in Brāhmaṇas and in a great country of auspicious features.

Never live in a place where there is a whore, where there is a lecherous libertine and in a bad place crowded by mean people.

53b-57a. Though you solely depend upon Śiva, the lord of the three worlds, do adore all the Devas, honouring their respective (festival) days.

Be always pure, always efficient, always calm, always steady, always subduing the six enemies (anger etc.). Stay alone, O sinless one.

Promptly offer obeisance to Brāhmaṇas conversant with the Vedas, calm and brilliant ascetics, sacred trees, sacred rivers, meritorious holy spots, great lakes, cows, bulls, gems, chaste young women, and domestic deities.

57b-59. Get up early in the Brāhma Muhūrta, wash the mouth with pure heart, bow down to your own preceptor, meditate on the Lord, Consort of Umā, think of Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of Lakṣmī, Brahmā, Vināyaka, Skanda, Kātyāyanī, Goddess Mahālakṣmī, Sarasvatī, the Guardians of Quarters including Indra and sages of pure fame. After meditating on all these, bow down to the rising sun.

## \|\| 3.11.60-62 \|\|

*ciṃtayitvātha mārttaṃḍamudyaṃtaṃ praṇametsadā \|*  
*gaṃdhaṃ puṣpaṃ ca tāṃbūlaṃ śākaṃ pakvaphalādikam \|\| 60 \|\|*

*śivāya dattvopabhuṃkṣva bhakṣyaṃ bhojyaṃ priyaṃ navam \|*  
*yaddattaṃ yatkṛtaṃ japtaṃ yatsnātaṃ yaddhutaṃ smṛtam \|\| 61 \|\|*

*yacca taptaṃ tapaḥ sarvaṃ tacchivāya nivedaya \|*  
*bhuṃjānaśca paṭhanvāpi śayāno viharannapi \|*  
*paśyañchṛṇnvavadangṛhṇañchivamevānuciṃtaya \|\| 62 \|\|*

60-62. Use scents, flowers, betel leaves, vegetables, ripe fruits etc. after first offering them to Śiva.

Whatever is offered, whether edible, pleasing or fresh, whatever is done, whatever Japa is performed, ablution taken and Homa, penance performed—dedicate all these to Śiva.

While taking food, reading or reciting, lying down, sporting about, seeing, hearing, speaking or taking anything think of Śiva alone.

## \|\| 3.11.63 \|\|

*rudrākṣakaṃkaṇalasatkaradaṃḍayugmo mālāṃtarāladhṛtabhasma sitatripuṃḍūḥ \|*  
*paṃcākṣaraṃ paripaṭhanparamaṃtrarājaṃ dhyāyansadā paśupateścaraṇaṃ ramethāḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Your pair of strong hands must have Rudrākṣa as the shining bracelets. You must have the three parallel lines of white ash on the forehead. You must repeat the five-syllabled king of Mantras (i.e. namaḥ śivāya) and you must always meditate on the feet of Paśupati. Thus you must enjoy yourself.

## \|\| 3.11.64 \|\|

*iti saṃkṣepato vatsa kathito dharmasaṃgrahaḥ \|*  
*anyeṣu ca purāṇeṣu vistareṇa prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Thus, O dear one, the compendium of Dharma (virtuous conduct) has been succinctly revealed. It has been explained more elaborately in other Purāṇas.

## \|\| 3.11.65 \|\|

*athāparaṃ sarvapurāṇaguhyaṃ niḥśeṣapāpaughaharaṃ pavitram \|*  
*jayapradaṃ sarvavipadvimocanaṃ vakṣyāmi śaivaṃ kavacaṃ hitāya te \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Now for your benefit I shall explain another thing—the Śiva Kavaca (‘Amulet of Śiva’). It is a secret, esoteric doctrine of all the Purāṇas; it is pure and sacred, destructive of all sins; it bestows victory and rids one of all calamities.

## Chapter 12 - Description of Śivakavaca

## \|\| 3.12.1 \|\|

*ṛṣabha uvāca \|*  
*namaskṛtya mahādevaṃ viśvavyāpinamīśvaram \|*  
*vakṣye śivamayaṃ varma sarvarakṣākaraṃ nṛṇām \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: ‘Kavaca’ means an armour. The different aspects of the deity are believed to protect different parts of a man’s body by touching it while uttering that particular portion of the incantation.—The procedure of Śiva-Kavaca is given in this chapter.

Ṛṣabha said:

1\. After bowing down to Mahādeva, the Lord who pervades the entire universe, I shall describe the (mystic) amulet of Śiva (that which is auspicious) which protects men in every respect.

## \|\| 3.12.2 \|\|

*śucau deśe samāsīno yathāvatkalpitāsanaḥ \|*  
*jiteṃdriyo jitaprāṇaściṃtayecchivamavyayam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. One should be seated in a clean place in a suitable posture. He should curb his sense-organs, control his vital breaths and meditate upon the immutable Śiva.

## \|\| 3.12.3 \|\|

*hṛtpuṃḍarīkāṃtarasanniviṣṭaṃ svatejasā vyāptanabhovakāśam \|*  
*atīṃdriyaṃ sūkṣmamanaṃtamādyaṃ dhyāyetparānaṃdamayaṃ maheśam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. He should meditate on Maheśa, the embodiment of supreme bliss, stationed within the lotus of the heart, who has pervaded the entire ethereal space by means of his own brilliance, who is the primordial being, subtle and infinite, and who is beyond the ken of the sense-organs.

## \|\| 3.12.4 \|\|

*dhyānāvadhūtākhilakarmabaṃdhaściraṃ cidānaṃdanimagnacetāḥ \|*  
*ṣaḍakṣaranyāsasamāhitātmā śaivena kuryā tkavacena rakṣām \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The devotee should protect (himself) by means of Śivakavaca, shaking off all the bindings (i.e. effects) of Karmas through meditation, with his mind immersed for a long time in the bliss of consciousness and with his self composed by means of the Nyāsa (ritualistic touch of the limbs) of the six syllables.

## \|\| 3.12.5 \|\|

*māṃ pātu devo'khiladevatātmā saṃsārakūpe patitaṃ gabhīre \|*  
*tannāma divyaṃ varamaṃtramūlaṃ dhunotu me sarvamaghaṃ hṛdistham \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. “May the Lord, the soul of all deities, protect me fallen into the deep well of worldly existence. Let his divine name, the Mula Mantra (original mantra) of great excellence, shake off all my sins accumulated in the heart.

## \|\| 3.12.6 \|\|

*sarvatra māṃ rakṣatu viśvamūrttirjyotirmayānaṃdaghanaścidātmā \|*  
*aṇoraṇīyānuruśaktirekaḥ sa īśvaraḥ pātu bhayādaśeṣāt \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. May the Cidātmā (‘soul having consciousness as its essence’) of cosmic form, consisting of refulgence and bliss, protect me everywhere. May that Īśvara who is minuter than the minutest, who is single with extraordinary power, protect (me) from every type of fear.

## \|\| 3.12.7 \|\|

*yo bhūsvarūpeṇa bibharti viśvaṃ pāyātsa bhūmergiriśo'ṣṭamūrtiḥ \|*  
*yo'pāṃ svarūpeṇa nṛṇāṃ karoti saṃjīnaṃ so'vatu māṃ jalebhyaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*
