31\. Then the great goddess spoke to the girl eagerly: “O dear girl of great fortune, listen to my final remark:

## \|\| 3.19.32-37 \|\|

*yadā kadāpi bharttāraṃ kvāpi deśe purātanam \|*  
*drakṣyasi svapnadṛṣṭaṃ prākjñāsyase tvaṃ vicakṣaṇā \|\| 32 \|\|*

*tvāṃ drakṣyati sa vipropi sunayāṃ svapnalakṣaṇām \|*  
*tadā parasparālāpo yuvayoḥ saṃbhaviṣyati \|\| 33 \|\|*

*tadā svatanayaṃ bhadre tasmai dehi bahuśrutam \|*  
*phalamasya vratasyāgryaṃ tasya haste samarpaya \|\| 34 \|\|*

*tataḥ prabhṛti tasyaiva vaśe tiṣṭha sumadhyame \|*  
*yuvayodaihikaḥ saṃgo mābhūtsvapnaratādṛte \|\| 35 \|\|*

*kālātpaṃcatvamāpanne tasminbrāhmaṇasattame \|*  
*agniṃ praviśya tenaiva saha yāsyasi matpadam \|\| 36 \|\|*

*putraste bhavitā subhru sarvalokamanoramaḥ \|*  
*saṃpadaśca bhaviṣyaṃti prāpsyate paramaṃ padam \|\| 37 \|\|*

32-37. Whenever and wherever you happen to see your earlier husband, the one seen in dreams, you will be clever enough to recognize him. That Brāhmaṇa too will recognize you, the lady of good behaviour, by the features seen in the dream. Then both of you will talk over the matter. Then, O fair lady, hand over your learned son to him. Place in his hands the greatest fruit of this Vrata. Thereafter, O lady of excellent waistline, stay under his control. But let there be no physical contact between you two, apart from the dalliance in the course of dreams. In due course, when that excellent Brāhmaṇa passes away, you should enter his funeral pyre and attain my region. O lady of excellent eyebrows, your son will be the delighter of the minds of the entire public. He will have riches too. He will also attain the highest region.”

## \|\| 3.19.38 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā trijaganmātā dattvā tasyai manoratham \|*  
*tayoḥ saṃpaśyatoreva kṣaṇenādarśanaṃ gatā \|\| 38 \|\|*

Sūta said:

38\. After saying this and granting her wish, the Mother of the three worlds quickly vanished even as both of them were watching.

## \|\| 3.19.39 \|\|

*sāpi bālā varaṃ labdhvā pārvatyāḥ karuṇānidheḥ \|*  
*avāpa paramānaṃdaṃ pūjayāmāsa taṃ gurum \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. After receiving the boon from Pārvatī, the storehouse of mercy, the girl derived great pleasure. She worshipped the preceptor.

## \|\| 3.19.40 \|\|

*tasyāṃ rātryāṃ vyatītāyāṃ sa munirlabdhalocanaḥ \|*  
*tasyāḥ pitrośca tatsarvaṃ rahasyācaṣṭa dharmavit \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. When the night passed off, the sage who had regained his eyes and who was conversant with Dharma, secretly informed her parents about everything.

## \|\| 3.19.41 \|\|

*atha sarvānupāmaṃtrya śāradāṃ ca yaśasvinīm \|*  
*vidhāyānugrahaṃ teṣāṃ yayau svairagatirmuniḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. After taking leave of Śāradā, the glorious girl, and of all the others, offering them all blessings, the sage went away as he pleased.

## \|\| 3.19.42 \|\|

*evaṃ dineṣu gacchatsu sā bālā ca pratikṣaṇam \|*  
*bhartuḥ samāgamaṃ lebhe svapne sukha vivardhanam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. As days passed on, the girl did have the contact with her husband in dreams, increasing her pleasure every moment.

## \|\| 3.19.43 \|\|

*gauryā varapradānena śāradā viśadavratā \|*  
*dadhāra garbhaṃ svapnepi bhartuḥ saṃgānubhāvataḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Due to the boon bestowed by Gaurī, Śāradā, the performer of spotless holy vows, conceived as a result of the dream-dalliance with her husband.

## \|\| 3.19.44 \|\|

*tāṃ śrutvā bhartṛrahitāṃ śāradāṃ garbhiṇī satīm \|*  
*sarve dhigiti procustāṃ jāriṇīti jagurjanāḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. On hearing that Śāradā had conceived even as she continued to be a widow, all of them said, “Fie upon you!” The people proclaimed her an adulteress.

## \|\| 3.19.45 \|\|

*saṃparetasya tadbharturye jātikulavabāṃdhavāḥ \|*  
*tāṃ vārtāṃ duḥsahāṃ śrutvā yayustatpitṛmaṃdiram \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The kinsmen and the family friends of her dead husband got the news and hastened to her parent’s house.

## \|\| 3.19.46 \|\|

*atha sarve samāyātā grāmavṛddhāśca paṃḍitāḥ \|*  
*samājaṃ cakrire tatra kulavṛddhaiḥ samanvitam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Then all the elderly persons of the village and the learned men came there and held an assembly including the old men of the family.

## \|\| 3.19.47 \|\|

*antarvatnīṃ samāhūya śāradāṃ vinatānanām \|*  
*atarjayansusaṃkruddhāḥ kecidāsanparāṅmukhāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. They summoned Śāradā, the pregnant girl. (As she sat) with face bowed down, they furiously threatened and rebuked her. Some of them turned their faces away from her.

## \|\| 3.19.48 \|\|

*ayi jāriṇi durbuddhe kimetatte viceṣṭitam \|*  
*asmatkule suduṣkīrttiṃ kṛtavatyasi bāliśe \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. “O adulteress, O evil-minded one, what have you done? You have brought about dishonour and infamy to our family in your childish waywardness.”

## \|\| 3.19.49 \|\|

*iti saṃtarjayaṃtaste grāmavṛddhā manīṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*sarve saṃmaṃtrayāmāsuḥ kiṃ kurma iti bhāṣiṇaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. After rebuking her thus, the learned old men of the village consulted together asking, “What shall we do?”

## \|\| 3.19.50-51 \|\|

*tatrocuḥ ke ca vṛddhāstāṃ bālāṃ prati vinirdayāḥ \|*  
*eṣā pāpamatirbālā kuladvayavināśinī \|\| 50 \|\|*

*kṛtvāsyāḥ keśavapanaṃ chittvā karṇau ca nāsikām \|*  
*nirvāsyatāṃ bahirgrāmātparityajya svagotrataḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51. There some old men spoke to the girl mercilessly: “This girl of evil intentions has destroyed both the families. Her hairs should be closely shaved. Her ears and nose should be cut off. Let her be driven out of the family and banished from the village.”

## \|\| 3.19.52 \|\|

*iti sarve samālocya tāṃ tathā kartumudyatāḥ \|*  
*athāṃtarikṣe saṃbhūtā śuśruve vāgagocarā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. After thinking thus, they were about to do so. Thereupon, an ethereal voice was heard:

## \|\| 3.19.53-54 \|\|

*anayā na kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ na caiva kuladūṣaṇam \|*  
*vratabhaṃgo na caitasyāssucaritreyamaṃganā \|\| 53 \|\|*

*itaḥ paramiyaṃ nārī jāriṇīti vadaṃti ye \|*  
*teṣāṃ doṣavimūḍhānāṃ sadyo jihvā vidīryate \|\| 54 \|\|*

53-54. “No sin has been committed by this girl, nor has this family been disgraced. She has not broken any of her vows. This woman is decent in her behaviour. Henceforth, if any one dares to call her an adulteress, he deluded by his own fault will get his tongue split and torn in a trice.”

## \|\| 3.19.55 \|\|

*ityaṃtarikṣe janitāṃ vāṇīṃ śrutvā'śarīriṇīm \|*  
*sarve prajahṛṣustasyā jananījanakādayaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. On hearing these unembodied words arising from the firmament, her mother, father and all the others became delighted.

## \|\| 3.19.56 \|\|

*tataḥ sasaṃbhramāḥ sarve grāmavṛddhāḥ sabhājanāḥ \|*  
*muhūrttaṃ maunamālaṃbya bhītāstasthuradhomukhāḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Then all those elders of the villages and members of the assembly became bewildered. They sat silent for a short while, extremely frightened with heads hanging down.

## \|\| 3.19.57 \|\|

*tatra kecidaviśvastā mithyāvāṇītyavādiṣuḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ jihvā dvidhā bhinnā vavamuste kṛmīnkṣaṇāt \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Some among them were not credulous enough. They said that the ethereal voice was not genuine at all. Their tongues became split into two and they soon vomited worms.

## \|\| 3.19.58 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃpūjayāmāsustāṃ bālāṃ jñātibāṃdhavāḥ \|*  
*bāṃdhavāśca striyo vṛddhāḥ śaśaṃsuḥ sādhusādhviti \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Then the kinsmen and the relatives adored that girl. The elderly female and male relatives praised, “Excellent! Excellent!”

## \|\| 3.19.59 \|\|

*mumucuḥ kecidānaṃdabāṣpabiṃdūnkulottamāḥ \|*  
*kulastriyaḥ pramuditāstāmuddiśya samāśvasan \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Some of the excellent ones among them shed tears of joy. The ladies of the family consoled themselves regarding her. They were happy (without any regret).

## \|\| 3.19.60 \|\|

*atha tatrāpare procurdevo vadati nānṛtam \|*  
*kathameṣāṃ dadhau garbhaṃ śīlānna calitā dhruvam \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Then the others said, “The god does not utter any lie. But how did she conceive without swerving from the path of virtue and modesty?”

## \|\| 3.19.61 \|\|

*iti sarvānsabhyajanā nsaṃśayāviṣṭacetasaḥ \|*  
*vilokya vṛddhastatraiko sarvajño lokatattvavit \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. When some of the persons assembled there were seen doubting, an all-knowing old man well conversant with the truth about the world, said:

## \|\| 3.19.62 \|\|

*māyāmayamidaṃ viśvaṃ dṛśyate śrūyate ca yat \|*  
*kiṃ bhāvyaṃ kimabhāvyaṃ vā saṃsāre'sminkṣaṇātmake \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. “This whole universe which is seen and heard is a product of Māyā. What is it that should happen or should not happen in this transient world?

## \|\| 3.19.63 \|\|

*anirūpyamabhūtārthaṃ māyayā jāyate sphuṭam \|*  
*īśvarasya vaśe māyā tasya ko veda ceṣṭitam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. An unprecedented and indescribable thing is clearly born of Māyā. The Māyā is under the control of Īśa. Who can know his activities?

## \|\| 3.19.64 \|\|

*yūpaketośca rājarṣeḥ śukraṃ nipatitaṃ jale \|*  
*saśukraṃ tajjalaṃ pītvā veśyā garbhaṃ dadhau kila \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. The semen virile of the royal sage Yūpaketu fell into water. It is said that a harlot drank that water together with the semen and became pregnant.

## \|\| 3.19.65 \|\|

*munervibhāṃḍakasyāpi śukraṃ pītvā sahāṃbhasā \|*  
*hariṇī garbhiṇī bhūtvā ṛṣyaśṛṃgamasūyata \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. After drinking the semen of Sage Vibhāṇḍaka together with water, a female deer became pregnant and gave birth to Ṛṣyaśṛṅga.

## \|\| 3.19.66 \|\|

*surāṣṭrasya tathā rājñaḥ karaṃ spṛṣṭvā mṛgāṃganā \|*  
*tatkṣaṇādgarbhiṇī bhūtvā muniṃ prāsūta tāpasam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. A female deer touched the hand of the king of Surāṣṭra, became pregnant instantly and gave birth to an ascetic.

## \|\| 3.19.67 \|\|

*tathā satyavatī nārī śapharīgarbhasaṃbhavā \|*  
*tathaiva mahiṣīgarbho jātaśca mahiṣāsuraḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Similarly, the woman Satyavatī was born of the womb of the glittering fish called Śapharī. The demon Mahiṣa was born of the womb of a buffalo.

## \|\| 3.19.68 \|\|

*tathā saṃti purā nāryaḥ kāruṇyādgarbhasaṃbhavāḥ \|*  
*tathā hi vasudevena rohiṇyā stanayo'bhavat \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Similarly there have been women who were made pregnant out of pity. For example a son was born of Rohiṇī through Vasudeva.

## \|\| 3.19.69 \|\|

*devatānāṃ maharṣīṇāṃ śāpena ca vareṇa ca \|*  
*ayuktamapi yatkarma yujyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. By the boons of deities or curses of great sages, even improper things become proper undoubtedly.

## \|\| 3.19.70 \|\|

*sāṃbasya jaṭharājjātaṃ musalaṃ muniśāpataḥ \|*  
*yuvanāśvasya garbho'bhūnmunīnāṃ maṃtragauravāt \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. A pestle came out of the belly of Sāṃba by the curse of a sage. By the power of the Mantras of the sages Yuvanāśva became pregnant.

## \|\| 3.19.71 \|\|

*nūnameṣāpi kalyāṇī maharṣeḥ pādasevanāt \|*  
*mahāvratānubhāvācca dhatte garbhamaniṃ ditā \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Certainly this auspicious girl became pregnant, because she had been serving the sage’s feet and had observed great Vratas of excessive efficacy.

## \|\| 3.19.72 \|\|

*asminnarthe rahasyenāṃ satyaṃ pṛcchaṃtu yoṣitaḥ \|*  
*tato nivṛttasaṃdeho bhaviṣyati mahājanaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. In this connection, let the women secretly ask her and get at the real truth. Then the public will be free from suspicions.”

## \|\| 3.19.73 \|\|

*tatastadvacanādeva tāmapṛcchanstriyo mithaḥ \|*  
*tābhyaḥ śaśaṃsa tatsarvaṃ sā svavṛttaṃ mahādbhutam \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Accordingly the women asked her secretly and she narrated the miraculous incident that happened to her in its entirety.

## \|\| 3.19.74 \|\|

*vijānaṃtastataḥ sarve mānayitvā ca tāṃ satīm \|*  
*modamānāḥ praśaṃsaṃtaḥ prayayuḥ svaṃ svamālayam \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Comprehending everything, they accepted her as a chaste lady. Joyously praising her, they went to their respective abodes.

## \|\| 3.19.75 \|\|

*atha kāle śubhe prāpte śāradā vimalāśayā \|*  
*asūta tanayaṃ bālā bālārkasamatejasam \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. At an auspicious hour Śāradā of pure heart gave birth to a son having the lustre of the rising sun.

## \|\| 3.19.76 \|\|

*sa kumāro mahodāralakṣaṇaḥ kamalekṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*avāpya mahatīṃ vidyāṃ bālya eva mahāmatiḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. The lotus-eyed boy of beautiful features acquired great learning even in childhood and became highly intelligent.

## \|\| 3.19.77 \|\|

*athopanīto guruṇā kāle lokamanoramaḥ \|*  
*sa śāradeya eveti loke khyāti mavāpa ha \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. He was invested with the sacred thread by the preceptor at the proper time. He earned the reputation of being a Śāradeya (‘child of Śāradā’ or ‘one pertaining to Goddess Sarasvatī i.e. highly learned’). He delighted the minds of the people.

## \|\| 3.19.78 \|\|

*ṛgvedamaṣṭame varṣe navame yajuṣāṃ gaṇam \|*  
*daśame sāmavedaṃ ca līlayādhyagamatsudhīḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. The intelligent boy easily learned Ṛgveda in his eighth year, all the Yajur Mantras in the ninth year, and Sāma Veda in the tenth year.

## \|\| 3.19.79-81 \|\|

*atha trilokamahite saṃprāpte śivaparvaṇi \|*  
*gokarṇaṃ prayayuḥ sarve janāḥ sarvanivāsinaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

*śāradāpi svaputreṇa gokarṇaṃ prayayau satī \|\| 80 \|\|*

*tatrāpaśyatsamāyātaṃ sadā svapneṣu lakṣitam \|*  
*pūrvajanmani bharttāraṃ dvijabaṃdhujanāvṛtam \|\| 81 \|\|*

79-81. All the residents (of that village) went to Gokarṇa when the great festival of Śiva, devoutly celebrated in all the three worlds, approached. The chaste lady Śāradā too went to Gokarṇa along with her son. There she saw the husband of the previous birth coming (towards her) in the same form as was seen in the dreams. He was surrounded by his Brāhmaṇa relatives.

## \|\| 3.19.82 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā premanirviṇṇā pulakāṃkitavigrahā \|*  
*niruddhabāṣpaprasarā tasthau tannyastalocanā \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. On seeing him, she became overwhelmed with love. Hairs stood on their ends all over the body. With great difficulty she could control the profuse shedding of tears. She stood there with her eyes fixed on him.

## \|\| 3.19.83-84 \|\|

*sa ca vipro'pi tāṃ dṛṣṭvā rūpalakṣaṇalakṣitām \|*  
*svapne sadā bhujyamānāmātmano ratidāyinīm \|\| 83 \|\|*

*taṃ kumāramapi svapne dṛṣṭvā cātma śarīrajam \|*  
*vilokya vismayāviṣṭastadaṃtikamupāyayau \|\| 84 \|\|*

83-84. On seeing that woman recognized by beauty of form and other features, who had been enjoyed by him in dreams and who gave him much of sexual pleasure and also the boy born of his own body as seen in the dream, the Brāhmaṇa was struck with wonder and approached her.

## \|\| 3.19.85 \|\|

*bhadre tvāṃ praṣṭumicchāmi yatkiṃcinmanasi sthitam \|*  
*iti prathamamābhāṣya rahaḥ sthānaṃ nināya tām \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. “O fair lady, I wish to ask you something that is in my mind”. After saying this he took her to a secret place.

## \|\| 3.19.86 \|\|

*kā tvaṃ kathaya vāmoru kasya bhāryāsi suvrate \|*  
*ko deśaḥ kasya vā putrī kinnāmetyabravīcca tām \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. “O lady of beautiful thighs, tell me who you are. O lady of excellent Vratas, whose wife are you? What is your native place? Whose daughter? What is your name?” He further asked.

## \|\| 3.19.87 \|\|

*iti tena samāpṛṣṭā sā nārī bāṣpalocanā \|*  
*vyājahārātmanovṛttaṃ bālye vaidhavyakāraṇam \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. On being asked by him, the woman with eyes brimming with tears, narrated everything concerning her, including her child-widowhood.

## \|\| 3.19.88 \|\|

*punaḥ papraccha tāṃ bālāṃ putraḥ kasyāyamuttamaḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ dhṛto vā jaṭhare bālo'yaṃ caṃdrasannibhaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. Then he asked that girl, “Whose excellent son is this? How was this boy as beautiful as the moon conceived in your womb?”

## \|\| 3.19.89 \|\|

*\|śāradovāca \|*  
*eṣa me tanayaḥ svāminsarvavidyāviśāradaḥ \|*  
*śāradeya iti prokto mama nāmnaiva kalpitaḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

Śāradā said:

89\. O my lord, this is my son. He is a master of all learnings. He is called Śāradeya after my own name.

## \|\| 3.19.90-91 \|\|

*iti tasyā vacaḥ śrutvā vihasya brāhmaṇottamaḥ \|*  
*provāca kaṣṭātkaṣṭaṃ hi caritaṃ tava bhāmini \|\| 90 \|\|*

*pāṇigrahaṇamātraṃ te kṛtvā bharttā mṛtaḥ kila \|*  
*kathaṃ cāyaṃ suto jātastasya kāraṇamucyatām \|\| 91 \|\|*

90-91. On hearing her words the excellent Brāhmaṇa laughed and said: “O beautiful lady, your life story is extremely painful. Immediately after holding your hand, your husband was dead. How is this boy born? Let his source be disclosed.”

## \|\| 3.19.92 \|\|

*iti tenoditāṃ vāṇīmākarṇyātīva lajjitā \|*  
*kṣaṇaṃ cāśrumukhī bhūtvā dhairyāditthamabhāṣata \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. On hearing these words uttered by him she became ashamed. Her face was covered with tears for a short while. Immediately she regained courage and spoke thus:

## \|\| 3.19.93 \|\|

*śāradovāca \|*  
*tadalaṃ parihāsoktyā tvaṃ māṃ vetsi mahāmate \|*  
*tvāmahaṃ vedmi cārthe'sminpramāṇaṃ mana āvayoḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

Śāradā said:

93\. Enough of jocular utterances! O highly intelligent one, you know me. I too know you. In this matter, our mind is the ultimate authority.

## \|\| 3.19.94 \|\|

*ityuktvā sarvamāvedya devyā dattaṃ varādikam \|*  
*vratasyārdhaṃ kumāraṃ taṃ dadau tasmai dhṛtavratam \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. After saying this and narrating the details of the boon granted by the Goddess, she gave him the boy, the partial fruit of her Vrata, who himself was in the habit of observing Vratas.

## \|\| 3.19.95 \|\|

*so'pi pramudito vipraḥ kumāraṃ pratigṛhya tam \|*  
*pitroranumatenaiva tāṃ nināya nijālayam \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. The delighted Brāhmaṇa accepted the boy and with the permission of his parents took her to his abode.

## \|\| 3.19.96 \|\|

*sāpi sthitvā bahūnmāsāṃstasya viprasya maṃdire \|*  
*tasminkālavaśaṃ prāpte praviśyāgniṃ tamanvagāt \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. She stayed in that Brāhmaṇa’s abode for many months. When he passed away she too jumped into the funeral pyre and followed him.

## \|\| 3.19.97 \|\|

*tatastau daṃpatī bhūtvā vimānaṃ divyamāsthitau \|*  
*divyabhogasamāyuktau jagmatuḥ śivamaṃdiram \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. They rode on a divine chariot in the form of a couple. They enjoyed all divine pleasures and went to Śiva’s place.

## \|\| 3.19.98 \|\|

*ityetatatpuṇyamākhyānaṃ mayā samanuvarṇitam \|*  
*paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ samyagbhuktimuktiphalapradam \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. Thus the meritorious narrative has been recounted by me. To those who read this or hear this, it yields the benefit of worldly pleasures and salvation.

## \|\| 3.19.99 \|\|

*āyurārogyasaṃpattidhanadhatyavivarddhanam \|*  
*strīṇāṃ maṃgalasaubhāgyasaṃtānasukhasādhanam \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. It increases longevity, health, riches and grain-stock. It makes women achieve auspicious conjugal bliss, progeny and happiness.

## \|\| 3.19.100 \|\|

*etanmahākhyānamaghaughanāśanaṃ gaurīmaheśavratapuṇyakīrtanam \|*  
*bhaktyā sakṛdyaḥ śṛṇuyācca kīrttayedbhuktvā sa bhogānpadameti śāśvatam \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. He who devoutly listens to or glorifies even once, this great narrative that lauds the merit of Gaurīmaheśa Vrata, that destroys mass of sins, enjoys all pleasures and then attains the eternal position.

## Chapter 20 - The Great Efficacy of Rudrākṣa: The Story of Mahānandā

## \|\| 3.20.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*atha rudrākṣamāhātmyaṃ varṇayāmi samāsataḥ \|*  
*sarvapāpakṣayakaraṃ śṛṇvatāṃ paṭhatāmapi \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: Rudrākṣa is the berry of Elaeocarpus ganitrus used for making rosaries. The berry is specially sacred to Rudra. The present chapter states how a monkey and a cock were born in royal families as they were made to wear Rudrākṣa.—VV 1-15 describe the sacred efficacy of Rudrākṣa.

Sūta said:

1\. Now I shall describe the greatness of Rudrākṣa succinctly. It is destructive of all sins of the listeners and readers.

## \|\| 3.20.2 \|\|

*abhakto vāpi bhakto vā nīco nīcataropi vā \|*  
*rudrākṣāndhārayedyastu mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. One may or may not be a devotee, he may be a mean fellow, may be the meanest one (but), if he wears Rudrākṣas, he gets released from all sins.

## \|\| 3.20.3 \|\|

*rudrākṣadhāraṇaṃ puṇyaṃ kena vā sadṛśaṃ bhavet \|*  
*mahāvratamidaṃ prāhurmunayastattvadarśinaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The wearing of Rudrākṣa is meritorious. It has no equal. Sages, the seers of reality, call this (wearing) a great Vrata.

## \|\| 3.20.4 \|\|

*sahasraṃ dhārayedyastu rudrākṣāṇāṃ dhṛtavrataḥ \|*  
*taṃ namaṃti surāḥ sarve yathā rudrastathaiva saḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. One who strictly adheres to Vratas and wears a thousand Rudrākṣas is on a par with Rudra. All the Suras bow down to him.

## \|\| 3.20.5-6 \|\|

*abhāve tu sahasrasya bāhvoḥ ṣoḍaśa ṣoḍaśa \|*  
*ekaṃ śikhāyāṃ karayordvādaśa dvādaśaiva hi \|\| 5 \|\|*

*dvātriṃśatkaṃṭhadeśe tu catvāriṃśattu mastake \|*  
*ekaika karṇayoḥ ṣaṭ ṣaṭ vakṣasyaṣṭottaraṃ śatam \|*  
*yo dhārayati rudrākṣānrudravatsopi pūjyate \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. If a thousand (Rudrākṣas) are not possible, a devotee (can wear a couple of hundreds like this): sixteen on each of the arms, one on the tuft, twelve on each of the hands, thirty-two round the neck, forty on the forehead, six in each of the ears and one hundred and eight on the chest. He who wears Rudrākṣas thus is also worshipped like Rudra.

## \|\| 3.20.7 \|\|

*muktāpravālasphaṭikaraupyavaidūryakāṃcanaiḥ \|*  
*sametāndhārayedyastu rudrākṣānsa śivo bhavet \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. He who wears Rudrākṣas set with pearls, coral, crystal, silver, lapis lazuli or gold shall be Śiva himself.

## \|\| 3.20.8 \|\|

*kevalānapi rudrākṣānyathālābhaṃ bibharti yaḥ \|*  
*taṃ na spṛśaṃti pāpāni tamāṃsīva vibhāvasum \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Just as darkness does not touch the Sun so also sins do not touch him who wears the Rudrākṣas alone as and when he gets them.

## \|\| 3.20.9 \|\|

*rudrākṣamālayā japto maṃtro'naṃtaphalapradaḥ \|*  
*arudrākṣo japaḥ puṃsāṃ tāvanmātraphalapradaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. A Mantra repeated with the use of a Rudrākṣa rosary gives endless fruits. A Japa without Rudrākṣa accords only meagre fruits.

## \|\| 3.20.10 \|\|

*yasyāṃge nāsti rudrākṣa ekopi bahupuṇyadaḥ \|*  
*tasya janma nirarthaṃ syāttripuṃḍrarahitaṃ yadi \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. If there is not a single Rudrākṣa, the bestower of many merits, on any one’s limbs, and if he has no Tripuṇḍra, his birth is fruitless.

## \|\| 3.20.11 \|\|

*rudrākṣaṃ mastake baddhvā śiraḥsnānaṃ karoti yaḥ \|*  
*gaṃgāsnānaphalaṃ tasya jāyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. One who takes a head-bath with a Rudrākṣa tied to his head, shall undoubtedly get the merit of a holy bath in Gaṅgā.

## \|\| 3.20.12 \|\|

*rudrākṣaṃ pūjayedyastu vinā toyābhiṣecanam \|*  
*yatphalaṃ liṃgapūjāyāstadevāpnoti niścitam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. If any one worships Rudrākṣa even without washing, he shall certainly obtain merit equal to that of adoration of the Liṅga.

## \|\| 3.20.13 \|\|

*ekavaktrāḥ paṃcavaktrā ekādaśamukhāḥ pare \|*  
*caturdaśamukhāḥ kecidrudrākṣā lokapūjitāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. These Rudrākṣas that are worshipped in the world (are of various sorts). Some are single-faced, some five-faced, others elevenfaced and some fourteen-faced.

## \|\| 3.20.14 \|\|

*bhaktyā saṃpūjito nityaṃ rudrākṣaḥ śaṃkarātmakaḥ \|*  
*daridraṃ vāpi kurute rājarājaśriyānvitam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. If devoutly worshipped daily, Rudrākṣa that can be identified with Śaṅkara makes even the poorest man endowed with the prosperity and glory of Rājarāja (Kubera).

## \|\| 3.20.15 \|\|

*atredaṃ puṇyamākhyānaṃ varṇayaṃti manīṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*mahāpāpakṣayakaraṃ śravaṇātkīrttanādapi \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Learned men recount a meritorious story in this context. It destroys all great sins on being listened to or recited.

## \|\| 3.20.16 \|\|

*rājā kāśmīradeśasya bhadrasena iti śrutaḥ \|*  
*tasya putro 'bhavaddhīmānsudharmānāma vīryavān \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Bhadrasena, a king of Kāśmīra land, was very famous. He had a heroic son of great intelligence named Sudharmā.

## \|\| 3.20.17 \|\|

*tasyāmātyasutaḥ kaścittārako nāma sadguṇaḥ \|*  
*babhūva rājaputrasya sakhā paramaśobhanaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The virtuous son of the minister was a very nice friend of the prince. His name was Tāraka.

## \|\| 3.20.18 \|\|

*tāvubhau paramasnigdhau kumārau rūpasundarau \|*  
*vidyābhyāsaparau bālye saha krīḍāṃ pracakratuḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Those two boys of very handsome features were very friendly to each other. They were engaged in learning the different arts and sciences from childhood. They also played together.

## \|\| 3.20.19 \|\|

*tau sadā sarvagātreṣu rudrākṣakṛtabhūṣaṇau \|*  
*viceraturudārāṃgau satataṃ bhasmadhāriṇau \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. They used to embellish their limbs with Rudrākṣas. Smearing themselves with Bhasma (holy ash), they moved about with the limbs nicely developed.

## \|\| 3.20.20 \|\|

*hārakeyūrakaṭakakuṃḍalādivibhūṣaṇam \|*  
*hemaratnamayaṃ tyaktvā rudrākṣāndadhatuśca tau \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Discarding jewels and gold ornaments like necklace, arm-lets, bracelets, ear-rings etc., they wore Rudrākṣas.

## \|\| 3.20.21 \|\|

*rudrākṣamālitau nityaṃ rudrākṣakarakaṃkaṇau \|*  
*rudrākṣakaṃṭhābharaṇau sadā rudrākṣakuṃḍalau \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. They always wore strings of Rudrākṣa beads as their necklace and Rudrākṣa bracelets on their wrists. They considered Rudrākṣas as a good ornament for the neck and they had Rudrākṣas in their ear-rings.

## \|\| 3.20.22 \|\|

*hemaratnādyalaṃkāre loṣṭapāṣāṇadarśanau \|*  
*bodhyamānāvapi janairna rudrākṣānvyamuṃcatām \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. They looked upon ornaments of gold and jewels like a lump of earth and stone. Though the people dissuaded them, they did not stop wearing Rudrākṣas.

## \|\| 3.20.23 \|\|

*tasya kāśmīrarājasya gṛhaṃ prāpto yadṛcchayā \|*  
*parāśaro munivaraḥ sākṣādiva pitāmahaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Once, by chance, the excellent sage Parāśara who was like God Brahmā himself, happened to come to the abode of the king of Kāśmīra.

## \|\| 3.20.24 \|\|

*tamarcayitvā vidhivadrājā dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ \|*  
*prapaccha sukhamāsīnaṃ trikālajñaṃ mahāmunim \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. When the great sage capable of knowing the three divisions of time (past, present and future) was comfortably seated, the king, the most excellent one among men of piety, duly honoured him and asked:

## \|\| 3.20.25-27 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*bhagavanneṣa putro me sopi maṃtrisutaśca me \|*  
*rudrākṣadhāriṇau nityaṃ ratnābharaṇaniḥspṛhau \|\| 25 \|\|*

*śāsyamānāvapi sadā ratnākalpaparigrahe \|*  
*vilaṃghitāsmadvacanau rudrākṣeṣveva tatparau \|\| 26 \|\|*

*nopadiṣṭāvimau bālau kadācidapi kenacit \|*  
*eṣā svābhāvikī vṛttiḥ kathamāsītkumārayoḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

The king said:

25-27. O holy Sir, my son here and the son of my minister always wear Rudrākṣas. They don’t like jewel-set ornaments. Though bidden by me always to make use of jewel-set ornaments, they continue to ignore my words and show their preference for Rudrākṣas. These two boys have never been advised by anyone (in this regard). How did the boys happen to have this natural tendency?

## \|\| 3.20.28 \|\|

*parāśara uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu rājanpravakṣyāmi tava putrasya dhīmataḥ \|*  
*yathā tvaṃ maṃtriputrasya prāgvṛttaṃ vismayāvaham \|\| 28 \|\|*

Parāśara said:

28\. Listen, O king, I shall narrate the previous life story of your intelligent son, as well as that of the son of the minister. It will give you some surprise.

## \|\| 3.20.29 \|\|

*naṃdigrāme purā kācinmahānaṃdeti viśrutā \|*  
*babhūva vāravanitā śṛṃgāralalitākṛtiḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Formerly there was a well-known harlot in Nandigrāma village, named Mahānandā. She had charming features conducive to lust.

## \|\| 3.20.30-36 \|\|

*chatraṃ pūrṇeṃdusaṃkāśaṃ yānaṃ svarṇavirājitam \|*  
*cāmarāṇi sudaṃḍāni pāduke ca hiraṇmaye \|\| 30 \|\|*

*aṃbarāṇi vicitrāṇi mahārhāṇi dyumaṃti ca \|*  
*caṃdraraśminibhāḥ śayyā paryaṃkāśca hiraṇmayāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*gāvo mahiṣyaḥ śataśo dāsāśca śataśastathā \|\| 32 \|\|*

*sarvābharaṇadīptāṃgyo dāsyaśca navayauvanā \|*  
*bhūṣaṇāni parārdhyāṇi navaratnojjvalāni ca \|\| 33 \|\|*

*gandhakuṃkumakastūrīkarpūrāgurulepanam \|*  
*citramālyāvataṃsaśca yatheṣṭaṃ mṛṣṭabhojanam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*nānācitravitānāḍhyaṃ nānādhānyamayaṃ gṛham \|*  
*bahuratnasahasrāḍhyaṃ koṭisaṃkhyādhikaṃ dhanam \|\| 35 \|\|*

*evaṃ vibhavasaṃpannā veśyā kāmavihāriṇī \|*  
*śivapūjāratā nityaṃ satyadharmaparāyaṇā \|\| 36 \|\|*

30-36. The harlot was extremely rich. (She used to display) an umbrella white like the full moon, a vehicle shining with gold, chowries with splendid handles and golden sandals. The garments were of various colours, very valuable and extremely brilliant. The beds vied with the rays of the moon and the cots and palanquins were golden. She had hundreds of cows and buffaloes, and slaves too in hundreds. The slave girls were in the prime of their youth with their limbs brightly illuminated with all sorts of ornaments. The ornaments were of very great value with all the nine gems shedding their brilliance. Sweet scents, saffron, musk, camphor and agallochum made the unguents remarkable. Garlands of diverse colours embellished them. They had nice good food. The abode had variegated canopies and abounded in the stock of grains. (She had) thousands of gems and wealth to be reckoned in crores. The harlot possessed all these rich assets and sported about as she pleased. Yet she was extremely devoted to truth and piety. She was always engaged in the adoration of Śiva.

## \|\| 3.20.37 \|\|

*sadāśivakathāsaktā śivanāmakathotsukā \|*  
*śivabhaktāṃghryavanatā śivabhaktiratāniśam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. She was always interested in Śiva legends, eager to hear names of Śiva and discourses on Śiva. She used to bow down at the feet of Śiva’s devotees. She was always engrossed in the devotion to Śiva.

## \|\| 3.20.38-39 \|\|

*vinodahetoḥ sā veśyā nāṭyamaṇḍapamadhyataḥ \|*  
*rudrākṣaibhūṣayitvaikaṃ markaṭaṃ caiva kukkuṭam \|\| 38 \|\|*

*karatālaiśca gītaiśca sadā nartayati svayam \|*  
*punaśca vihasaṃtyuccaiḥ sakhībhiḥ parivāritā \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. That harlot had a monkey and a cock to humour herself. She used to embellish them with Rudrākṣas and make them dance in the middle of the dance-pavilion inducing them with the clappings of her hands and songs (sung sweetly). Surrounded by her female companions, she used to laugh loudly (viewing these).

## \|\| 3.20.40 \|\|

*yugmam \|*  
*rudrākṣaiḥ kṛtakeyūrakarṇābharaṇabhūṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*markaṭaḥ śikṣayā tasyāḥ sadā nṛtyati bālavat \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. With adequate training given by her, the monkey which had Rudrākṣas for armlets, ear-rings and other ornaments could dance like a boy.

## \|\| 3.20.41 \|\|

*śikhāyāṃ baddharudrākṣaḥ kukkuṭaḥ kapinā saha \|*  
*ciraṃ nṛtyati nṛtyajñaḥ paśyatāṃ citramāvahan \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The cock had Rudrākṣas tied to its crest and it danced along with the monkey like a well-trained dancer, delighting everyone who watched.

## \|\| 3.20.42 \|\|

*ekadā bhavanaṃ tasyāḥ kaścidvaiśyaḥ śivavratī \|*  
*ājagāma sarudrākṣastripuṃḍrī nirmamaḥ kṛtī \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Once a certain Vaiśya who used to observe the holy vows of Śiva, came to her house. He had the Tripuṇḍra (on the forehead) and Rudrākṣas (round the neck etc.). He (seemed to be) a contented man, free from the sense of possessiveness.

## \|\| 3.20.43 \|\|

*sa bibhradbhasma viśade prakoṣṭhe varakaṃkaṇam \|*  
*mahāratnaparistīrṇaṃ jvalaṃtaṃ taruṇārkavat \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. On his spotless wrist he had worn an excellent bracelet set with a great jewel. It was blazing like the midday sun.

## \|\| 3.20.44 \|\|

*tamāgataṃ sā gaṇikā saṃpūjya parayā mudā \|*  
*tatprakoṣṭhagataṃ vīkṣya kaṃkaṇaṃ prāha vismitā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. On his arrival, the harlot honoured him with great delight. Looking at the bracelet on his wrist, she spoke with a sense of wonder:

## \|\| 3.20.45 \|\|

*mahāratnamayaḥ so'yaṃ kaṃkaṇastvatkare sthitaḥ \|*  
*mano harati me sādhau divyastrībhūṣaṇocitaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. “This bracelet on your wrist has been set with great jewels, O good man; it captivates my mind. It really deserves to be an ornament of a celestial damsel.”

## \|\| 3.20.46 \|\|

*iti tāṃ vararatnāḍhya saspṛhāṃ karabhūṣaṇe \|*  
*vākṣyodāramatirvaiśyaḥ sasmitaṃ samabhāṣata \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. On seeing her enamoured of the bracelet set with excellent jewels the liberal-minded Vaiśya spoke with a smile:

## \|\| 3.20.47 \|\|

*vaiśya uvāca \|*  
*asminratnavare divye yadi te saspṛhaṃ manaḥ \|*  
*tamevādatsva suprītā maulyamasya dadāsi kim \|\| 47 \|\|*

The Vaiśya said:

47\. If your mind has any ardent wish (to have) this excellent jewel of divine features, you take this and be glad. Well, what will you give me by way of its price?

## \|\| 3.20.48-49 \|\|

*veśyo vāca \|*  
*vayaṃ tu svairacāriṇyo veśyāstu na pativratāḥ \|*  
*asmatkulocito dharmo vyabhicāro na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*yadyetadratnakhacitaṃ dadāsi karabhūṣaṇam \|*  
*dinatrayamahorātraṃ tava patnī bhavāmyaham \|\| 49 \|\|*

(Mahānandā said:)

48-49. “We are self-willed harlots and not chaste ladies; promiscuous sexual activity is a duty befitting our families. If you give me this gemset bangle, I shall be your wife for three days and nights.”

## \|\| 3.20.50 \|\|

*vaiśya uvāca \|*  
*tathāstu yadi te satyaṃ vacanaṃ vāravallabhe \|*  
*dadāmi ratnavalayaṃ trirātraṃ bhava madvadhūḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

The Vaiśya said:

50\. So be it, if you are bound by your words, O wanton lady, I shall give you the gemset bracelet; be my wife for three nights.

## \|\| 3.20.51 \|\|

*etasminvyavahāre tu pramāṇaṃ śaśibhāskarau \|*  
*trivāraṃ satyamityuktvā hṛdayaṃ me spṛśa priye \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. In this transaction, the moon and the sun are the witnesses. Say “True” three times and touch my heart, O my beloved.

## \|\| 3.20.52 \|\|

*veśyovāca \|*  
*dinatrayamahorātraṃ patnī bhūtvā tava prabho \|*  
*sahadharmaṃ carāmīti sā taddhṛdayamaspṛśat \|\| 52 \|\|*

The harlot said:

52\. O my lord, I shall become your wife for three days and nights and shall pursue my duties and obligations in your company.

## \|\| 3.20.53 \|\|

*atha tasyai sa vaiśyastu pradadau ratnakaṅkaṇam \|*  
*liṃgaṃ ratnamayaṃ cāsyā haste dattvedamabravīt \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Saying this she touched his heart. The Vaiśya gave her the gem-set bracelet. Handing over a Liṅga full of jewels, he spoke thus:

## \|\| 3.20.54 \|\|

*idaṃ ratnamayaṃ śaivaṃ liṃgaṃ matprāṇasaṃnibham \|*  
*rakṣaṇīyaṃ tvayā kāṃte tasya hānirmṛtirmama \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. “O my beloved, this Śiva Liṅga, full of jewels, is like my own vital breaths. It should be preserved. Its loss is the loss of my life.”

## \|\| 3.20.55 \|\|

*evamastviti sā kāṃtā liṃgamādāya ratnajam \|*  
*nāṭyamaṇḍapikāstaṃbhe nidhāya prāviśadgṛham \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Saying “It shall be so”, that woman took the jewel-set Liṅga and placed it on a pillar in the dance pavilion. Then she went into her house.

## \|\| 3.20.56 \|\|

*sā tena saṃgatā rātrau vaiśyena viṭadharmiṇā \|*  
*sukhaṃ suṣvāpa paryaṃke mṛdutalpopaśobhite \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. In intimate contact with that Vaiśya who behaved like a sensualist, she slept gladly on the palanquin rendered splendid by a soft bed.

## \|\| 3.20.57 \|\|

*tato niśīthasamaye nāṭyamaṇḍapikāṃtare \|*  
*akasmādutthito vahnistameva sahasāvṛṇot \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Then at midnight, the dance pavilion caught fire all of a sudden, which enveloped everything.

## \|\| 3.20.58 \|\|

*maṇḍape dahyamāne tu sahasotthāya saṃbhramāt \|*  
*sā veśyā markaṭaṃ tatra mocayāmāsa baṃdhanāt \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. When the pavilion began to burn, the harlot got up with great bewilderment and set the monkey free.

## \|\| 3.20.59 \|\|

*sa markaṭo muktabaṃdhaḥ kukkuṭena sahāmunā \|*  
*bhīto dūraṃ pradudrāva vidhūyāgnikaṇānbahūn \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. When set free along with the cock, the monkey ran off with great fright scattering sparks of fire.

## \|\| 3.20.60 \|\|

*staṃbhena saha nirdagdhaṃ talliṃgaṃ śakalīkṛtam \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā veśyā ca vaiśyaśca duraṃtaṃ duḥkhamāpatuḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Seeing that the Liṅga too was completely burnt and reduced to pieces, the harlot and the Vaiśya suffered from unlimited misery.

## \|\| 3.20.61 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā prāṇasamaṃ liṃgaṃ dagdhaṃ vaiśyapatistathā \|*  
*svayamapyāptanirvedo maraṇāya matiṃ dadhau \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. On seeing the Liṅga which he valued like his own life, burnt completely, the eminent Vaiśya became dejected and despondent. He set his heart on suicide.

## \|\| 3.20.62-64 \|\|

*nirvedadānnitarāṃ khedādvaiśyastāmāha duḥkhitām \|*  
*śivaliṃge tu nirbhinne nāhaṃ jīvitumutsahe \|\| 62 \|\|*

*citāṃ kāraya me bhadre tava bhṛtyairbalādhikaiḥ \|*  
*śive manaḥ samāveśya praviśāmi hutāśanam \|\| 63 \|\|*

*yadi brahmeṃdraviṣṇvādyā vārayeyuḥ sametya mām \|*  
*tathāpyasminkṣaṇe dhīraḥ praviśyāgniṃ tyajāmyasūn \|\| 64 \|\|*

62-64. Due to acute grief leading to indifference to worldly matters, the Vaiśya spoke to her who was also miserable: “Now that the Śivaliṅga is reduced to pieces, I do not want to live.” Get a funeral pyre made for me, O gentle lady, by your powerful servants. I shall enter fire with my mind resting in Siva. Even if Brahmā, Indra, Viṣṇu and others were to prevent me collectively, I will refuse to be discouraged in entering the fire and give up my life.”

## \|\| 3.20.65 \|\|

*tamevaṃ dṛḍhabaṃdhaṃ sā vijñāya bahuduḥkhitā \|*  
*svabhṛtyaiḥ kārayāmāsa citāṃ svanagarādbahiḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Realizing how determined he was, she became extremely miserable. Just at the outskirts of the city she got a funeral pyre ready through her servants.

## \|\| 3.20.66 \|\|

*tataḥ sa vaiśyaḥ śivabhaktipūtaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya samiddhamagnim \|*  
*viveśa paśyatsu janeṣu dhīraḥ sā cānutāpaṃ yuvatī prapede \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Thereafter the Vaiśya sanctified by devotion to Śiva circumambulated the fire and entered it patiently even as people stood watching. The young woman sympathized with him.

## \|\| 3.20.67 \|\|

*atha sā duḥkhitā nārī smṛtvā dharmaṃ sunirmalam \|*  
*sarvānbandhūnsamīkṣyaiva babhāṣe karuṇaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Then that miserable woman recollected her sacred obligation. Facing all her relatives she spoke these moving words:

## \|\| 3.20.68-71 \|\|

*ratnakaṃkaṇamādāya mayā satyamudāhṛtam \|*  
*dinatrayamahaṃ patnī vaiśyasyāmuṣya saṃmatā \|\| 68 \|\|*

*karmaṇā matkṛtenāyaṃ mṛto vaiśyaḥ śivavratī \|*  
*tasmādahaṃ pravekṣyāmi sahānena hutāśanam \|*  
*sadharmacāriṇītyuktaṃ satyametaddhi paśyatha \|\| 69 \|\|*

*satyena prītimāyāṃti devāstribhuvaneśvarāḥ \|*  
*satyāsaktiḥ paro dharmaḥ satye sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam \|\| 70 \|\|*

*satyena svargamokṣau ca nāsatyena parā gatiḥ \|*  
*tasmāsatyaṃ samāśritya pravekṣyāmi hutāśanam \|\| 71 \|\|*

68-71. “Accepting the gemset bracelet, a promise was made by me that I shall be the committed wife of this Vaiśya for three days. It was on account of my negligent act (that) this Vaiśya died. Hence I shall enter the fire along with him. What has been promised by me that ‘I will be fulfilling my wifely duties to him’, you can see as true.

The Devas, the lords of the three worlds become pleased with truth. Devotion to truth is the greatest duty. Everything is well-established in truth. Heavenly pleasures and salvation can be obtained through truth. Greatest goal cannot be reached through untruth. Hence, relying on truth, I shall enter the fire.”

## \|\| 3.20.72 \|\|

*iti sā dṛḍhanirbaṃdhā vāryamāṇāpi baṃdhubhiḥ \|*  
*satyalopabhayānnārī prāṇāṃstyaktuṃ mano dadhe \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Firm in her resolve though dissuaded by her relatives, the woman set her heart on abandoning her life, as she was afraid that she would deviate from Satya (truth).

## \|\| 3.20.73 \|\|

*sarvasvaṃ śivabhaktebhyo dattvā dhyātvā sadāśivam \|*  
*tamagniṃ triḥ parikramya pradeśābhimukhī sthitā \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. She made a gift of all her possessions to the devotees of Śiva. While meditating on Sadāśiva, she circumambulating the fire three times stood ready to enter the fire.

## \|\| 3.20.74 \|\|

*tāṃ pataṃtīṃ samiddhe'gnau svapadārpitamānasām \|*  
*vārayāmāsa viśvātmā prādurbhūtaḥ śivaḥ svayam \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Śiva, the immanent soul of the universe, manifested himself and prevented that woman who had dedicated her mind at his own feet, from falling into the blazing fire.

## \|\| 3.20.75 \|\|

*sā taṃ vilokyākhiladeva devaṃ trilocanaṃ candrakalāvataṃsam \|*  
*śaśāṃkasūryānalakoṭibhāsaṃ stabdheva bhīteva tathaiva tasthau \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. On seeing the Three-eyed Lord of all the Devas who had the digit of the moon for an ornament and who had the lustre of ten millions of moons and suns and fires, she stood as if stunned and frightened.

## \|\| 3.20.76 \|\|

*tāṃ vihvalāṃ paritrastāṃ vepamānāṃ jaḍī kṛtām \|*  
*samāśvāsya galadbāṣpāṃ kare gṛhyābravīdvacaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Consoling that agitated trembling lady who was benumbed and who shed tears, the Lord took her by the hand and said:

## \|\| 3.20.77 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*satyaṃ dharmaṃ ca te dhairyaṃ bhaktiṃ ca mayi niścalām \|*  
*nirīkṣituṃ tvatsakāśaṃ vaiśyo bhūtvāhamāgataḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

Śiva said:

77\. It was I who became a Vaiśya and came to you in order to test and see for myself your steadfastness to truth, piety, courage and unwavering devotion to me.

## \|\| 3.20.78 \|\|

*māyayāgniṃ samutthāpya dagdhavānnāṭyamaṃḍapam \|*  
*dagdhaṃ kṛtvā ratnaliṃgaṃ pravṛṣṭosmi hutāśanam \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. I created fire through my Māyā and burnt down the dance-pavilion. After making the gemset Liṅga burnt down, I entered the fire myself.

## \|\| 3.20.79 \|\|

*veśyāḥ kaitavakāriṇyaḥ svairiṇyo janavaṃcakāḥ \|*  
*sā tvaṃ satyamanusmṛtya praviṣṭāgniṃ mayā saha \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Harlots are usually deceitful, adulterous and hoodwinkers of the common people. But you (on the contrary) entered the fire along with me on recollecting your promises.

## \|\| 3.20.80 \|\|

*ataste saṃpradāsyāmi bhogāṃstridaśadurlabhān \|*  
*āyuśca paramaṃ dīrghamārogyaṃ ca prajonnatim \|*  
*yadyadicchasi suśroṇi tattadeva dadāmi te \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. Hence I will give you all types of enjoyment of pleasures rare even unto gods, longevity, health and increase of progeny. O lady of big hips, whatever you wish I shall give that unto you.

## \|\| 3.20.81-84 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*iti bruvati gaurīśe sā veśyā pratyabhāṣata \|\| 81 \|\|*

*veśyovāca \|*  
*na me vāṃchāsti bhogeṣu bhūmau svarge rasātale \|*  
*tava pādāṃbujasparśādanyatkiṃcinna vai vṛṇe \|\| 82 \|\|*

*ete bhṛtyāśca dāsyaśca ye cānye mama bāṃdhavāḥ \|*  
*sarve tvadarcanaparāstvayi saṃnyastavṛttayaḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

*sarvānetānmayā sārdhaṃ nītvā tava paraṃ padam \|*  
*punarjanmabhayaṃ ghoraṃ vimocaya namostu te \|\| 84 \|\|*

Sūta said:

81-84. When-the Lord of Gaurī said thus, she replied:

## \|\| 3.20.85 \|\|

*tatheti tasyā vacanaṃ pratinaṃdya maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*tānsarvāṃśca tayā sārdhaṃ nināya paramaṃ padam \|\| 85 \|\|*

The harlot said:

I have no desire for any of the pleasures on the earth, in heaven or in nether worlds. I do not seek or woo anything else, except (the opportunity to) touch your lotus-like feet.

All these servants, slave girls and all of my relatives are engrossed in worshipping you. They have dedicated their actions to you.

Along with me, take all these to your greatest region. Take away the terrible fear of taking another birth. Obeisance to you.

85\. Saying “So (be it)”, Maheśvara approved of her words. He took all of them, along with her to his greatest region.

## \|\| 3.20.86 \|\|

*parāśara uvāca \|*  
*nāṭyamaṃḍapikādāhe yau dūraṃ vidrutau purā \|*  
*tatrāvaśiṣṭau tāveva kukkuṭo markaṭastathā \|\| 86 \|\|*

Parāśara said:

86\. While the dance pavilion was on fire, the cock and the monkey survived because they had run away.

## \|\| 3.20.87 \|\|

*kālena nidhanaṃ yāto yastasyā nāṭyamarkaṭaḥ \|*  
*sobhūttava kumāro'sau kuvakuṭo maṃtriṇaḥ sutaḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Her dancing pet, the monkey, passed away in due course and was born as your prince and the minister’s son was the cock in the previous birth.

## \|\| 3.20.88 \|\|

*rudrākṣadhāraṇodbhūtātpuṇyātpūrvabhavārjitāt \|*  
*kule mahati saṃjātau vartete bālakāvimau \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. Due to the merit of wearing the Rudrākṣas which they earned in the previous birth, they are born in a noble family as these boys.

## \|\| 3.20.89-90 \|\|

*pūrvābhyāsena rudrākṣāndadhāte śuddhamānasau \|*  
*asmiñjanmani taṃ lokaṃ śivaṃ saṃpūjya yāsya taḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

*eṣā pravṛttistvanayorbālayoḥ samudāhṛtā \|*  
*kathā ca śivabhaktāyā kimanyatpraṣṭumicchasi \|\| 90 \|\|*

89-90. Due to their previous practice, they are even now wearing the Rudrākṣas. They have preserved the purity of their minds. They will worship Śiva in this birth and ultimately go to him.

Such is the tendency of these two boys as I have narrated. The story of the lady devotee of Śiva was also recounted. What else do you wish to ask?

## Chapter 21 - The Greatness of Rudrādhyāya

## \|\| 3.21.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ brahmarṣiṇā proktāṃ vāṇīṃ pīyūṣasannibhām \|*  
*ākarṇya mudito rājā prāṃjaliḥ punarabravīt \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1\. On hearing these nectar-like words uttered by the Brāhmaṇa-sage, the king became happy. With palms joined in reverence, he spoke again:

## \|\| 3.21.2 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*aho satsaṃgamaḥ puṃsāmaśeṣāghapraśodhanaḥ \|*  
*kāmakrodhanihaṃtā ca iṣṭadogdhā janasya hi \|\| 2 \|\|*

The king said:

2\. How wonderful it is! The association with saintly people is destructive of all sins. It eradicates sexual urge and anger. It can yield whatever is desirable.

## \|\| 3.21.3 \|\|

*mama māyātamo naṣṭaṃ jñānadṛṣṭiḥ prakāśitā \|*  
*tava darśanamātreṇa prāyohamamarottamaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. My ignorance born of Māyā has perished. The vision of knowledge has been brightened. Merely by seeing you I have become almost an excellent immortal.

## \|\| 3.21.4 \|\|

*śrutaṃ ca pūrvacaritaṃ bālayoḥ samyagetayoḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyadapi pṛcchāmi matputrācaraṇaṃ mune \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The story of the previous life of these two boys has been heard completely. O sage, I shall ask you about the future too of my son.

## \|\| 3.21.5 \|\|

*asyāyuḥ kati varṣāṇi bhāgyaṃ vada ca kīdṛ śam \|*  
*vidyā kīrtiśca śaktiśca śraddhā bhaktiśca kīdṛśī \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. How many years will he live? Of what nature is his fortune? Learning, reputation, power, faith and devotion—what will be the position of these?

## \|\| 3.21.6 \|\|

*etatsarvamaśeṣeṇa mune tvaṃ vaktumarhasi \|*  
*tava śiṣyosmi bhṛtyosmi śaraṇaṃ tvāṃ gatosmayaham \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O sage, it behoves you to narrate all these fully. I am your disciple, servant and a seeker of refuge in you.

## \|\| 3.21.7 \|\|

*parāśara uvāca \|*  
*atrāvācyaṃ hi yatkiṃcitkathaṃ śaktosmi śaṃsitum \|*  
*yacchrutvā dhṛtimaṃtopi viṣādaṃ prāpnuyurjanāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

Parāśara said:

7\. In this regard there is something that cannot be spoken. How will I be able to speak out? On hearing that, even men of great courage may become distressed.

## \|\| 3.21.8 \|\|

*tathāpi nirvyalīkena bhāvena paripṛcchataḥ \|*  
*avācyamapi vakṣyāmi tava snehānmahīpate \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Still, as you ask sincerely without any fraudulent intention, O king, I am urged by the love unto you to speak out even those things which should not be disclosed ordinarily.

## \|\| 3.21.9 \|\|

*amuṣya tvatkumārasya varṣāṇi dvādaśātyayuḥ \|*  
*itaḥ paraṃ prapadyeta saptame divase mṛtim \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. This your prince has passed his twelfth year. Seven days hence he will die.

## \|\| 3.21.10 \|\|

*iti tasya vacaḥ śrutvā kālakūṭamivoditam \|*  
*mūrcchitaḥ sahasā bhūmau patito nṛpatiḥ śucā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. On hearing these words of his which were like the Kālakūṭa poison, the king suddenly lost consciousness and fell on the ground with excessive grief.

## \|\| 3.21.11 \|\|

*tamutthāpya samāśvāsya sa muniḥ karuṇārdradhīḥ \|*  
*uvāca mā bhairnṛpate punarvakṣyāmi te hitam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The sage with his mind melting with pity lifted him up and consoled him. He then said: “O king, do not be afraid. I shall speak what is beneficial to you.

## \|\| 3.21.12 \|\|

*sargātpurā nirālokaṃ yadekaṃ niṣkalaṃ param \|*  
*cidānaṃdamayaṃ jyotiḥ sa ādyaḥ kevalaḥ śivaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Prior to creation there was darkness everywhere, but the single, supreme, pure (unsullied) Being, the refulgence of knowledge and bliss persisted. That is the primordial Śiva himself.

## \|\| 3.21.13 \|\|

*sa evādau rajorūpaṃ sṛṣṭvā brahmāṇamātmanā \|*  
*sṛṣṭikarmaniyuktāya tasmai vedāṃśca dattavān \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. He alone at the outset created Brahma of Rājasika form. He gave the Vedas to him who was employed in the job of creation.

## \|\| 3.21.14 \|\|

*punaśca dattavānīśa ātmatattvaikasaṃgraham \|*  
*sarvopaniṣadāṃ sāraṃ rudrādhyāyaṃ ca dattavān \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Further the Lord gave him the Rudrādhyāya which is the sole compendium of all the principles of Ātman and the essence of all the Upaniṣads.

## \|\| 3.21.15 \|\|

*yadekamavyayaṃ sākṣādbrahmajyotiḥ sanātanam \|*  
*śivātmakaṃ paraṃ tattvaṃ rudrādhyāye pratiṣṭhitam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The single immutable refulgence of the Absolute, the eternal truth of the nature of Śiva, is established in Rudrādhyāya.

## \|\| 3.21.16 \|\|

*sa ātmabhūḥ sṛjadviśvaṃ caturbhirvadanairvirāṭ \|*  
*sasarja vedāṃścaturo lokānāṃ sthitihetave \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The illustrious Self-born Brahmā, in the course of his creation of the universe, breathed out the four Vedas through his four mouths for the sake of the sustenance of the worlds.

## \|\| 3.21.17 \|\|

*tatrāyaṃ yajuṣāṃ madhye brahmaṇo dakṣiṇānmukhāt \|*  
*aśeṣopaniṣatsāro rudrādhyāyaḥ samudgataḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Out of them, amongst the Yajur Mantras, Rudrādhyāya, the sum and substance of all the Upaniṣads, came out of his right (southern) mouth.

## \|\| 3.21.18 \|\|

*sa eṣa munibhiḥ sarvairmarīcyatripurogamaiḥ \|*  
*saha devairdhṛtastebhyastacchiṣyā jagṛhuśca tam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The same was received and retained by all the sages including Marīci and Atri, along with the Devas. From them their disciples got it.

## \|\| 3.21.19 \|\|

*tacchiṣyaśiṣyaistatputraistatputraiśca kramāgataiḥ \|*  
*dhṛto rudrātmakaḥ so'yaṃ vedasāraḥ prasāditaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. It was duly handed over through the disciples of those disciples, to their sons and their sons’ sons. This essence of the Vedas, i.e. Rudrādhyāya, was received and retained and propitiated.

## \|\| 3.21.20 \|\|

*eṣa eva paro mantra eṣa eva paraṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*rudrādhyāyajapaḥ puṃsāṃ paraṃ kaivalyasādhanam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. This is the greatest Mantra, the greatest austerity. The Japa (repetition) of Rudrādhyāya is the greatest means of attaining salvation unto all men.

## \|\| 3.21.21 \|\|

*mahāpātakinaḥ proktā upapātakinaśca ye \|*  
*rudrādhyāyajapātsadyaste'pi yāṃti parāṃ gatim \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Those who are said to have committed major sins as well as those who perpetrate minor sins, attain the great goal through the Japa of Rudrādhyāya.

## \|\| 3.21.22 \|\|

*bhūyopi brahmaṇā sṛṣṭāḥ sadasanmiśrayonayaḥ \|*  
*devatiryaṅmanuṣyādyāstataḥ saṃpūritaṃ jagat \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Beings with a mixture of Sat (good) and Asat (evil) were further created by Brahmā, viz. Devas, brutes, human beings etc. The universe got filled with them.

## \|\| 3.21.23 \|\|

*teṣāṃ karmāṇi sṛṣṭāni svajanmānuguṇāni ca \|*  
*lokāsteṣu pravartaṃte bhuṃjate caiva tatphalam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Their activities (and obligations) were created (were laid down) befitting their own nativity (and natural propensities). The people work thereat and experience their results.

## \|\| 3.21.24 \|\|

*lokasṛṣṭipravāhārthaṃ svayameva prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*dharmādharmau sasarjāgre svavakṣaḥpṛṣṭhabhāgataḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. At the outset, for the continuity of the creation, Prajāpati (Brahmā, the creator) wrought Dharma (piety) and Adharma (impiety) out of his chest and back respectively.

## \|\| 3.21.25 \|\|

*dharmamevānutiṣṭhaṃtaḥ puṇyaṃ viṃdaṃti tatphalam \|*  
*adharmamanutiṣṭhaṃtaste pāpaphalabhoginaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Those who pursue only Dharma derive merit as the fruit thereof. Those who resort to Adharma reap the fruits of sin.

## \|\| 3.21.26 \|\|

*puṇyakarmaphala svargo narakastadviparyayaḥ \|*  
*tayordvāvadhipau dhātrā kṛtau śatamakhāṃtakau \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Heavenly pleasure is the fruit of pious activities and hellish experience that of the opposite. The rulers of heaven and hell are Indra and Yama, and they are created by Brahmā.

## \|\| 3.21.27 \|\|

*kāmaḥ krodhaśca lobhaśca madamānādayaḥ pare \|*  
*adharmasya sutā āsansarve narakanāyakāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Lust, anger, greed, pride, jealousy etc. are the sons of Adharma. They lead to Naraka.

## \|\| 3.21.28 \|\|

*gurutalpaḥ surāpānaṃ tathānyaḥ pulkasīgamaḥ \|*  
*kāmasya tanayā hyete pradhānāḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Defiling preceptor’s bed, imbibing liquor, carnal approach to Pulkasī (a tribal woman)—these are the chief sons of Kāma (Lust).

## \|\| 3.21.29 \|\|

*krodhātpitṛvadho jātastathā mātṛvadhaḥ paraḥ \|*  
*brahmahatyā ca kanyaikā krodhasya tanayā amī \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Pitṛvadha (Patricide) was born of Krodha (anger) and also Mātṛvadha (Matricide). There is one daughter named Brahmahatyā (Brāhmaṇa-slaughter). These are the children of Krodha (Anger).

## \|\| 3.21.30 \|\|

*devasvaharaṇaścaiva brahmasvaharaṇastathā \|*  
*svarṇasteya iti tvete lobhasya tanayāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Devasvaharaṇa (Misappropriation of temple property), Brahmasvaharaṇa (Misappropriation of the assets of Brāhmaṇas) and Svarṇasteya (Stealing of gold)—these are known as the sons of Lobha (Covetousness).

## \|\| 3.21.31 \|\|

*etānāhūya cāṃḍālānyamaḥ pātakanāyakān \|*  
*narakasya vivṛddhyarthamādhipatyaṃ cakāra ha \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Yama summoned all these Cāṇḍālas, the leaders of sins and ruled over Naraka in order to make it flourish.

## \|\| 3.21.32-34 \|\|

*te yamena samādiṣṭā nava pātakanāyakāḥ \|*  
*te sarve saṃgatā bhūyo ghorāḥ pātakanāyakāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*narakānpālayāmāsuḥ svabhṛtyaiścopapātakaiḥ \|*  
*rudrādhyāye bhuvi prāpte sākṣātkaivalyasādhane \|\| 33 \|\|*

*bhītāḥ pradudruvuḥ sarve te'mī pātakanāyakāḥ \|*  
*yamaṃ vijñāpayāmāsuḥ sahānyairupapātakaiḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

32-34. There are nine such leaders of sins. Commanded by Yama, all these terrible leaders of sins assembled together and protected the Narakas (Hells) assisted by their servants, the Upapātakas (Minor Sins). After the advent of Rudrādhyāya on the earth as the sole and direct means of attaining salvation (Mokṣa), all these leaders of sins became frightened and fled. Approaching Yama along with the Minor Sins, they prayed to Yama:

## \|\| 3.21.35-40 \|\|

*jaya deva mahārāja vayaṃ hi tava kiṃkarāḥ \|*  
*narakasya vivṛddhyarthaṃ sādhikārāḥ kṛtāstvayā \|\| 35 \|\|*

*adhunā vartituṃ loke na śaktāḥ smo vayaṃ prabho \|*  
*rudrādhyāyānubhāvena nirdagdhāścaiva vidrutāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*grāmegrāme nadīkūle puṇyeṣvāyataneṣu ca \|*  
*rudrajāpye tu paryāpte kathaṃ loke caremahi \|\| 37 \|\|*

*prāyaścittasahasraṃ vai gaṇayāmo na kiṃcana \|*  
*rudrajāpyākṣarāṇyeva soḍhuṃ bata na śaknumaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*mahāpātakamukhyānāmasmākaṃ lokaghātinām \|*  
*rudrajāpyaṃ bhayaṃ ghoraṃ rudrajāpyaṃ mahadviṣam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*ato durviṣahaṃ ghoramasmāka vyasanaṃ mahat \|*  
*rudrajāpyena saṃprāptamapanetuṃ tvamarhasi \|\| 40 \|\|*

35-40. ‘O great king, be victorious. Indeed we are your servants. For the prosperity of Narakas we have been appointed officials with rights and obligations. O lord, we are helpless and incapable of staying in the world now. By the majestic power of Rudrādhyāya, we are scorched and driven away.

How can we move about in the world when the recitation of Rudrādhyāya is sufficiently widespread in every village, on the banks of the rivers and sacred spots and shrines?

We do not at all mind a thousand expiatory rites, but we are unable to bear the very syllables of Rudrādhyāya.

We, the chiefs among Major Sins, the destroyers of the worlds, are greatly frightened by Rudrādhyāya. It is a great poison unto us.

Thus a terribly unbearable disaster has befallen us on account of Rudrādhyāya. It behoves you to ward it off.’

## \|\| 3.21.41 \|\|

*iti vijñāpitaḥ sākṣādyamaḥ pātakanāyakaiḥ \|*  
*brahmaṇoṃ'tikamāsādya tasmai sarvaṃ nyavedayat \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Thus directly appealed by the leaders of sins, Yama went to Brahmā and submitted to him everything:

## \|\| 3.21.42-45 \|\|

*devadeva jagannātha tvāmeva śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*tvayā niyukto martyānāṃ nigrahe pāpakāriṇām \|\| 42 \|\|*

*adhunā pāpino martyā na saṃti pṛthivītale \|*  
*rudrādhyāyena nihataṃ pātakānāṃ mahatkulam \|\| 43 \|\|*

*pātakānāṃ kule naṣṭe narakāḥ śūnyatāṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*narake śūnyatāṃ yāte mama rājyaṃ hi niṣphalam \|\| 44 \|\|*

*tasmāttvayaiva bhagavannupāyaḥ paricintyatām \|*  
*yathā me na vihanyeta svāmitvaṃ martyadehinām \|\| 45 \|\|*

42-45. ‘O Lord of Devas, O Lord of the universe, I seek refuge in you. I have been employed by you for the task of restraining men who perpetrate sins. Now there are no sinners among men all over the world. The entire horde of sins has been wiped off by Rudrādhyāya. Since the masses of sins have perished, the Narakas have become empty. In the event of the voidness of Narakas, my rule has become futile. Hence, O holy Sir, let the means be thought over by you alone, lest I should lose the mastery over embodied human beings.’

## \|\| 3.21.46 \|\|

*iti vijñāpito dhātā yamena parikhidyatā \|*  
*rudrajāpyavighātārthamupāyaṃ paryakalpayat \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Thus informed by Yama who was extremely distressed, the Creator evolved means of preventing the popularity of Rudrajapa.

## \|\| 3.21.47 \|\|

*aśraddhāṃ caiva durmedhāmavidyāyāḥ sute ubhe \|*  
*śraddhāmedhāvighātinyau martyeṣu paryacodayat \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. He let loose among human beings the two daughters of Avidyā (Ignorance), viz. Aśraddhā (Lack of faith) and Durmedhā (Silliness) intended to be the opponents of Śraddhā (Faith) and Medhā (Intellect).

## \|\| 3.21.48 \|\|

*tābhyāṃ vimohite loke rudrādhyāyaparāṅmukhe \|*  
*yamaḥ svasthānamāsādya kṛtārtha iva so'bhavat \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Deluded by those two, the world became indifferent towards Rudrādhyāya. So Yama came back to his post apparently contented.

## \|\| 3.21.49 \|\|

*pūrvajanmakṛtaiḥ pāpairjāyaṃte'lpāyuṣo janāḥ \|*  
*tāni pāpāni naśyaṃti rudraṃ japtavatāṃ nṛṇām \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Due to the sins committed in previous births, people become short-lived. Those sins perish in the case of men who perform Rudrajapa.

## \|\| 3.21.50 \|\|

*kṣīṇeṣu sarvapāpeṣu dīrghamāyurbalaṃ dhṛtiḥ \|*  
*ārogyaṃ jñānamaiśvaryaṃ vardhate sarvadehinām \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. When all the sins subside, longevity, strength, fortitude, health, wisdom and prosperity of all embodied beings get increased.

## \|\| 3.21.51 \|\|

*rudrādhyāyena ye devaṃ snāpayaṃti maheśvaram \|*  
*tajjalaiḥ kurvataḥ snānaṃ te mṛtyuṃ saṃtaraṃti ca \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Persons who after bathing Lord Maheśvara by means of Rudrādhyāya make use of that water for their own ablution, surmount the eventuality of death.

## \|\| 3.21.52 \|\|

*rudrādhyāyābhijaptena snānaṃ kurvaṃti yeṃ'bhasā \|*  
*teṣāṃ mṛtyubhayaṃ nāsti śivalo ke mahīyate \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. No fear of death shall torment those people who bathe in waters sanctified with the Mantras of Rudrāḍhyāya. They are honoured in the world of Śiva.

## \|\| 3.21.53 \|\|

*śatarudrābhiṣekeṇa śatāyurjāyate naraḥ \|*  
*aśeṣapāpanirmuktaḥ śivasya dayito bhavet \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Through Śatarudrābhiṣeka a man becomes capable of living up to the age of a hundred years. Getting himself freed of all sins, he shall become a favourite of Śiva.

## \|\| 3.21.54 \|\|

*eṣa rudrāyutasnānaṃ karotu tava putrakaḥ \|*  
*daśavarṣasahasrāṇi modate bhuvi śakravat \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Let this son of yours take the ablution after ten thousand Japas of Rudrādhyāya. He will live joyously on the earth like Indra for ten thousand years.

## \|\| 3.21.55 \|\|

*avyāhatabalaiśvaryo hataśatrurnirāmayaḥ \|*  
*nirdhūtākhilapāpaughaḥ śāstā rājyamakaṃṭakam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. He will possess unobstructed strength and unmitigated prosperity. All his enemies will be killed. He shall be free from ailments. Shaking off the entire range of sins, he will rule the kingdom free from vexation.

## \|\| 3.21.56-57 \|\|

*viprā vedavidaḥ śāṃtāḥ kṛtinaḥ śaṃsitavratāḥ \|*  
*jñānayajñataponiṣṭhāḥ śivabhaktiparāyaṇāḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*rudrādhyāya japaṃ samyakkurvaṃtu vimalāśayāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ japānubhāvena sadyaḥ śreyo bhaviṣyati \|\| 57 \|\|*

56-57. Brāhmaṇas of very high order, fully conversant with the Vedas, quiet and confident of what they can do, of praiseworthy holy observances, established in the practice of Yajña, austerities and pursuit of knowledge and considering devotion to Śiva as their sole goal, must perform the Japa of Rudrādhyāya with purity of mind. By the power of their Japa welfare will immediately result.”

## \|\| 3.21.58 \|\|

*ityuktavaṃtaṃ nṛpatirmahāmuniṃ tameva vavre prathamaṃ kriyāgurum \|*  
*athāparāṃstyaktadhanāśayānmunīnāvāhayāmāsa sahasraśaḥ kṣaṇāt \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. As the great sage said thus, the king chose him alone as the first preceptor for the requisite rite. Very soon he invited thousands of other sages devoid of greed for wealth.

## \|\| 3.21.59-60 \|\|

*te viprāḥ śāṃtamanasaḥ sahasraparisaṃmitāḥ \|*  
*kalaśānāṃ śataṃ sthāpya puṇya vṛkṣarasairyutam \|\| 59 \|\|*

*rudrādhyāyena saṃsnāpya tamurvīpatiputrakam \|*  
*vidhivatsnāpayāmāsuḥ saṃprāpte saptame dine \|\| 60 \|\|*

59-60. Those Brāhmaṇas of quiescent minds numbering thousands placed a hundred pots filled with the exudation of holy trees. After duly bathing the prince with the Rudrādhyāya (charged holy water), they bathed him (with the exudations) on the seventh day.

## \|\| 3.21.61 \|\|

*snāpyamāno munijanaiḥ sa rājanyakumārakaḥ \|*  
*akasmādeva saṃtrastaḥ kṣaṇaṃ mūrcchāmavāpa ha \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Being bathed by the sages, that prince appeared to be frightened suddenly and fell into a swoon.

## \|\| 3.21.62-64 \|\|

*sahasaiva prabuddho'sau munibhiḥ kṛtarakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*provāca kaścitpuruṣo daṃḍahastaḥ samāgataḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*māṃ prahartuṃ kṛtamatirbhīmadaṇḍo bhayānakaḥ \|*  
*so'pi cānyairmahāvīrai puruṣairabhitāḍitaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

*baddhvā pāśena mahatā dūraṃ nīta ivābhavat \|*  
*etāvadahamadrākṣaṃ bhavadbhiḥ kṛtarakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

62-64. He regained consciousness suddenly and was afforded protection by sages. He spoke: “A certain man of a very huge body came to hit me with a big stick in his hand. He was excessively terrifying, but he was beaten by other heroic persons. He was bound with a big rope and it appeared as though he was taken very far away. I saw only this much and I have been saved by you all.”

## \|\| 3.21.65 \|\|

*ityuktavaṃtaṃ nṛpatestanūjaṃ dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*āśīrbhiḥ pūjayāmāsurbhayaṃ rājñe nyavedayan \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. When the prince spoke thus, the excellent Brāhmaṇas blessed him and intimated to the king how he was frightened.

## \|\| 3.21.66-67 \|\|

*atha sarvānṛṣīñchreṣṭhāndakṣiṇābhirnṛpottamaḥ \|*  
*pūjayitvā varānnena bhojayitvā ca bhaktitaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*pratigṛhyāśiṣasteṣāṃ munīnāṃ brahmavādi nām \|*  
*bhaktyā baṃdhujanaiḥ sārdhaṃ sabhāyāṃ samupāviśat \|\| 67 \|\|*

66-67. The excellent king honoured all the excellent sages with monetary gifts and devoutly fed them with excellent cooked food. He then received the blessings of those sages, the expounders of Vedas. Thereafter, he came to the assembly and sat there along with his kinsmen with great devotion.

## \|\| 3.21.68 \|\|

*tasminsamāgate vīre munibhiḥ saha pārthive \|*  
*ājagāma mahāyogī devarṣirnāradaḥ svayam \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. When the heroic king came along with the sages, the celestial sage Nārada, the great Yogin himself, came there.

## \|\| 3.21.69 \|\|

*tamāgataṃ prekṣya guruṃ munīnāṃ sārdhaṃ sadasyairakhilairmunīṃdraiḥ \|*  
*praṇamya bhaktyā viniveśya pīṭhe kṛtopacāraṃ nṛpatirbabhāṣe \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. On seeing the preceptor of all sages stepping in, the king devoutly bowed to him along with all the eminent sages assembled there. He made him seated on a pedestal offering all requisite services. Then the king spoke:

## \|\| 3.21.70 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*dṛṣṭaṃ kimasti te brahmastrilokyāṃ kiṃcidadbhutam \|*  
*tanno brūhi vayaṃ sarve tvadvākyāmṛtalālasāḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

The king said:

70\. O holy Sir, is there anything miraculous seen by you any where in the three worlds? Recount that to us. All of us are eager to imbibe the nectar of your speech.

## \|\| 3.21.71 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*adya citraṃ mahaddṛṣṭaṃ vyomnovataratā mayā \|*  
*tacchṛṇuṣva mahārāja sahaibhirmunipuṃgavaiḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

Nārada said:

71\. O great king, a very wonderful thing was seen by me today as I was coming down from the sky. Listen to it along with these eminent sages.

## \|\| 3.21.72 \|\|

*adya mṛtyurihāyāto nihaṃtuṃ tava putrakam \|*  
*daṃḍahasto durādharṣo lokamudbādhayansadā \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Mṛtyu (god of Death) who is unassailable and who always harasses the entire world had, with a staff in his hand, come today to kill your son.

## \|\| 3.21.73-74 \|\|

*īśvaropi viditvainaṃ tvatputraṃ haṃtumāgatam \|*  
*sahaiva pārṣadaiḥ kaṃcidvīrabhadramacodayat \|\| 73 \|\|*

*sa āgatya haṭhānmṛtyuṃ tvatputraṃ haṃtumāgatam \|*  
*gṛhītvā sudṛḍhaṃ baddhvā daṃḍenābhyahanadruṣā \|\| 74 \|\|*

73-74. Īśvara came to know that he had come to kill your son. He directed Vīrabhadra, one of his attendants, along with his assistants (towards him). He came and firmly bound Mṛtyu who had come to kill your son and angrily beat him with a stick.

## \|\| 3.21.75 \|\|

*taṃ nīyamānaṃ jagadīśasannidhiṃ śīghraṃ viditvā bhagavānyamaḥ svayam \|*  
*kṛtāṃjalirdeva jayetyudīrayanpraṇamya mūrdhnā nijagāda śūlinam \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. On coming to know that he was being taken to the presence of the Lord of the universe, Lord Yama shouted words of victory to Lord Śiva with palms joined in reverence. Bowing down his head, he spoke to the Trident-bearing Lord.

## \|\| 3.21.76 \|\|

*yama uvāca \|*  
*devadeva mahārudra vīrabhadra namo'stu te \|*  
*nirāgasi kathaṃ mṛtyau kopastava samutthitaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

Yama said:

76\. O Lord of Devas, O Mahā Rudra, O Vīrabhadra, obeisance to you. How is it that you have become angry with Mṛtyu who has not committed any offence?

## \|\| 3.21.77 \|\|

*nijakarmānubaṃdhena rājaputraṃ gatāyuṣam \|*  
*prahartumudyate mṛtyau koparādho vada prabho \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Mṛtyu was about to strike the prince whose life span had come to an end in accordance with his Karmas. O Lord, tell me, is this an offence?

## \|\| 3.21.78 \|\|

*vīrabhadra uvāca \|*  
*daśavarṣasahasrāyuḥ sa rājatanayaḥ katham \|*  
*vipattimaṃtarāyāti rudrasnānahatāśubhaḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

Vīrabhadra said:

78\. The ablution of Rudra has eradicated everything inauspicious in regard to the prince. He is now endowed with a life span of ten thousand years. What calamity can endanger his life?

## \|\| 3.21.79 \|\|

*asti cettava saṃdeho madvākye'pyanivārite \|*  
*citraguptaṃ samāhūya praṣṭavyo'dyaiva mā ciram \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. If you have any doubt in regard to my irrefutable statement, call Citragupta presently. Let him be asked without any delay.

## \|\| 3.21.80 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*athāhūtaścitragupto yamena sahasāgataḥ \|*  
*āyuḥpramāṇa tvatsūnoḥ paripṛṣṭaḥ sa cābravīt \|\| 80 \|\|*

Nārada said:

80\. On being summoned by Yama, Citragupta came there promptly. On being asked about the span of your son’s life he said:

## \|\| 3.21.81 \|\|

*dvādaśābdaṃ ca tasyāyurityuktvātha vimṛśya ca \|*  
*punarlekhyagataṃ prāha sa varṣāyutajīvitam \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. First he said “twelve years”, but after reflecting and checking the records, he admitted that the boy had ten thousand years more to live.

## \|\| 3.21.82 \|\|

*atha bhīto yamo rājā vīrabhadraṃ praṇamya ca \|*  
*kathaṃcinmocayāmāsa mṛtyuṃ durvārabaṃdhanāt \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Thereafter, the frightened King Yama bowed down to Vīrabhadra and somehow got Mṛtyu released from his captivity that could not have been warded off (otherwise).

## \|\| 3.21.83 \|\|

*vīrabhadreṇa mukto'tha yamo'gānnijamaṃdiram \|*  
*vīrabhadraśca kailāsamahaṃ prāptastavāṃtikam \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Released by Vīrabhadra, Yama went back to his palace, Vīrabhadra to Kailāsa and I have come to your presence.

## \|\| 3.21.84 \|\|

*atastava kumāro'yaṃ rudrajāpyānubhāvataḥ \|*  
*mṛtyorbhayaṃ samuttīrya sukhī jāto'yutaṃ samāḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Hence this prince of yours has surmounted the danger of death due to Rudrajapa. He shall be happy for ten thousand years.

## \|\| 3.21.85 \|\|

*ityuktvā nṛpamāmaṃtrya nārade tridivaṃ gate \|*  
*viprāḥ sarve pramuditāḥ svasvajagmurathāśramam \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. After saying this, Nārada went to heaven. The delighted Brāhmaṇas went to their respective hermitages.

## \|\| 3.21.86 \|\|

*itthaṃ kāśmīranṛpatī rudrādhyāyaprabhāvataḥ \|*  
*nistīryāśeṣaduḥ khāni kṛtārthobhūtsaputrakaḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Thus the king of Kāśmīra surmounted all miseries due to the power of Rudrādhyāya and became happy along with his son.

## \|\| 3.21.87 \|\|

*ye kīrtayaṃti manujāḥ parameśvarasya māhātmyametadatha karṇapuṭaiḥ pibaṃti \|*  
*te janmakoṭikṛtapāpagaṇairvimuktāḥ śāṃtāḥ prayāṃti paramaṃ padamiṃdumauleḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Those men who glorify this greatness of Parameśvara and imbibe it through their ears, will be rid of the numerous sins committed in the course of crores of births. They will become peaceful and attain the highest place of the Moon-crested Lord.

## Chapter 22 - The Efficacy of Listening to the Purāṇa

## \|\| 3.22.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ śivatamaḥ paṃthāḥ śivenaiva pradarśitaḥ \|*  
*nṛṇāṃ saṃsṛtibaddhānāṃ sadyomuktikaraḥ paraḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: VV 1-48 describe the efficacy of listening to this Purāṇa.

Sūta said:

1\. Thus the most auspicious and beneficial path has been shown clearly by Śiva himself. It is the most efficient means of bringing about the immediate liberation of men shackled to the world.

## \|\| 3.22.2-3 \|\|

*atha durmedhasāṃ puṃsāṃ vedeṣvanadhikāriṇām \|*  
*strīṇāṃ dvijātibaṃdhūnāṃ sarveṣāṃ ca śarīriṇām \|\| 2 \|\|*

*eṣa sādhāraṇaḥ paṃthāḥ sākṣātkaivalyasādhanaḥ \|*  
*mahāmunijanaiḥ sevyo devairapi supūjitaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Further, this is the common path for the direct achievement of emancipation (Mokṣa) for dull-witted men, ṃose unauthorised for the study of the Vedas, for women, for all embodied ones belonging to the twice-born classes. It deserves to be resorted to by great sages and it is honoured even by Devas.

## \|\| 3.22.4 \|\|

*yatkathāśravaṇaṃ śaṃbhoḥ saṃsārabhayanāśanam \|*  
*sadyomuktikaraṃ ślāghyaṃ pavitraṃ sarvadehinām \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Listening to the stories of Śaṃbhu is destructive of the danger of worldly existence. It affords us immediate liberation, it is praiseworthy and sacred for all embodied beings.

## \|\| 3.22.5 \|\|

*ajñānatimirāṃdhānāṃ dīpo'yaṃ jñānasiddhidaḥ \|*  
*bhavaroganibaddhānāṃ susevyaṃ paramauṣadham \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Unto those blinded by the darkness of ignorance, this is a lamp affording the acquisition of knowledge. It is the greatest medicine for those affected with the ailment of worldly existence.

## \|\| 3.22.6 \|\|

*mahāpātakaśailānāṃ vajraghātasudāruṇam \|*  
*bharjanaṃ karmabījānāṃ sādhanaṃ sarva saṃpadām \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. To mountains of great sins, it is a terrible blow like that of thunderbolt to mountains; it roasts up the seeds of Karinas and brings about all riches and prosperity.

## \|\| 3.22.7 \|\|

*ye śṛṇvaṃti sadā śambhoḥ kathāṃ bhuvanapāvanīm \|*  
*te vai manuṣyā lokesminrudrā eva na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Those men who always listen to Śaṃbhu’s stories that sanctify all the worlds, are certainly Rudras in the world.

## \|\| 3.22.8 \|\|

*śṛṇvatāṃ śūlino gāthāṃ tathā kīrtayatāṃ satām \|*  
*teṣāṃ pādarajāṃsyeva tīrthāni munayo jaguḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Sages have extolled the dust particles sticking to the feet of those men who listen to the stories of the Trident-bearing Lord and who glorify them as themselves holy places and shrines.

## \|\| 3.22.9 \|\|

*tasmānniśreyasaṃ gantuṃ yebhivāṃchaṃti dehinaḥ \|*  
*te śṛṇvaṃtu sadā bhaktyā śaivīṃ paurāṇikīṃ kathām \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Hence, let those embodied beings who wish for the achievement of salvation, always devoutly listen to the ancient (Purāṇic) stories of Śiva.

## \|\| 3.22.10 \|\|

*yadyaśaktaḥ sadā śrotuṃ kathāṃ paurāṇikīṃ naraḥ \|*  
*muhūrtaṃ vāpi śṛṇuyānniyatātmā dinedine \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. If any man is unable to listen to the Purāṇa-stories always, let him listen to it at least for a short while everyday.

## \|\| 3.22.11 \|\|

*atha pratidinaṃ śrotumaśakto yadi mānavaḥ \|*  
*puṇyamāseṣu vā puṇye dine puṇyatithiṣvapi \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. If the man is unable to listen to it everyday, let him listen to it on any auspicious day, or meritorious Tithis or in sacred months.

## \|\| 3.22.12 \|\|

*yaḥ śṛṇoti kathāṃ ramyāṃ purāṇaiḥ samudīritām \|*  
*sa nistarati saṃsāraṃ dagdhvā karmamahāṭavīm \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. He who listens to the fascinating narratives occurring in the Purāṇas crosses the (ocean of) worldly existence after burning down the great forest of Karmas.

## \|\| 3.22.13 \|\|

*muhūrttaṃ vā tadarddhaṃ vā kṣaṇaṃ vā pāvanīṃ kathām \|*  
*ye śṛṇvaṃti sadā bhaktyā na teṣāmasti durgatiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. If people listen to the sacred story for a Muhūrta or for half that time, nay even for a moment with devotion, they will never face misfortune or hell.

## \|\| 3.22.14 \|\|

*yatphalaṃ sarvayajñeṣu sarvadāneṣu yatphalam \|*  
*sakṛtpurāṇaśravaṇāttatphalaṃ viṃdate naraḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. A man obtains by listening to the Purāṇas once that benefit which accrues from all the Yajñas or all the religious gifts.

## \|\| 3.22.15 \|\|

*kalau yuge viśeṣeṇa purāṇaśravaṇādṛte \|*  
*nāsti dharmaḥ paraḥ puṃsāṃ nāsti muktipathaḥ paraḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Particularly in Kali age, apart from listening to the Purāṇas, there is no greater pious practice for men nor a better path of redemption.

## \|\| 3.22.16 \|\|

*purāṇaśravaṇācchaṃbhornāsti saṃkīrtanaṃ param \|*  
*ata eva manuṣyāṇāṃ kalpadrumamahāphalam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. There is no better way of glorification of Śaṃbhu than listening to the Purāṇas. Hence it yields to men great benefits like the celestial wish-yielding tree.

## \|\| 3.22.17-18 \|\|

*kalau hīnāyuṣo martyā durbalāḥ śramapīḍitāḥ \|*  
*durmedhaso duḥkhabhājo dharmācāravivarjitāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*iti saṃciṃtya kṛpayā bhagavānbādarāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*hitāya teṣāṃ vidadhe purāṇākhyaṃ sudhārasam \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. ‘Men in Kali age are short-lived, weak and oppressed by fatigue. They are dull-witted and miserable. They are devoid of pious practices.’ Thinking thus, the holy sage Bāḍarāyaṇa was moved with pity. For the sake of the welfare of those men, he prepared the nectarine juice in the form of Purāṇas.

## \|\| 3.22.19 \|\|

*pibannevāmṛtaṃ yatnādetatsyādajarāmaraḥ \|*  
*śambhoḥ kathāmṛtaṃ kuryātkulamevājarāmaram \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. If one succeeds in drinking ambrosia, he alone becomes immortal and free from old age. But the ambrosia of the story of Śaṃbhu will render the entire family immortal and free from old age.

## \|\| 3.22.20 \|\|

*bālo yuvā daridro vā vṛddho vā durbalo'pi vā \|*  
*purāṇajñaḥ sadā vandyaḥ pūjyaśca sukṛtārthibhiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. A person conversant with the Purāṇas, whether he be a boy, a youth, an old man or a weak-bodied poor fellow, should always be saluted and adored by people who seek merit.

## \|\| 3.22.21 \|\|

*nīcabuddhiṃ na kurvīta purāṇajñe kadācana \|*  
*yasya vaktrāṃbujādvāṇī kāmadhenuḥ śarīriṇām \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. No one should demean or speak ill of a person conversant with the Purāṇas, the words from whose lotus-like mouth are like Kāmadhenu (‘wish-yielding cow’) unto all embodied beings.

## \|\| 3.22.22 \|\|

*guravaḥ saṃti lokeṣu janmato guṇatastathā \|*  
*teṣāmapi ca sarveṣāṃ purāṇajñaḥ paro guruḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. There are Gurus (elders, preceptors, venerable ones) in all the worlds, by birth or by the qualities they possess. Among all of them, a person conversant with the Purāṇas is the greatest Guru.

## \|\| 3.22.23 \|\|

*bhavakoṭisahasreṣu bhūtvābhūtvāvasīdati \|*  
*yo dadātyapunarvṛttiṃ ko'nyastasmātparo guruḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Man feels exhausted and depressed by frequent births in the course of crores and thousands of transmigrations. That being the case, who else can be a better Guru than the one who accords us the benefit of no return (to Saṃsāra).

## \|\| 3.22.24 \|\|

*purāṇajñaḥ śucirdāṃtaḥ śāṃto vijitamatsaraḥ \|*  
*sādhuḥ kāruṇyavānvāgmī vadetpuṇyakathāṃ sudhī \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. A man conversant with the Purāṇas shall be pure and quiescent. He shall have control over his passions. He shall be free from feelings of jealousy etc. He shall be well-behaved and sympathetic. He shall be eloquent and shall sensibly recount the meritorious story.

## \|\| 3.22.25 \|\|

*vyāsāsanaṃ samārūḍho yadā paurāṇiko dvijaḥ \|*  
*asamāptaprasaṃgaśca namaskuryānna kasya cit \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. When a Brāhmaṇa expounding the Purāṇas has occupied the Vyāsa-seat, he shall not bow down to anyone till the stipulated portion of the story is not completed.

## \|\| 3.22.26 \|\|

*ye dhūrtā ye ca durvṛttā ye cānye vijigīṣavaḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ kuṭilavṛttīnāmagre naiva vadetkathām \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. He should not expound the story before men of crooked behaviour, who are rogues, wicked or men of competitive spirit desirous of defeating others in argument.

## \|\| 3.22.27 \|\|

*na durjanasamākīrṇe na śūdraśvāpadāvṛte \|*  
*deśe na dyūtasadane vadetpuṇyakathāṃ sudhīḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. A wise expounder should not narrate the holy story in a place abounding in wicked men, or in a land infested by beasts of prey, or in a region where gambling is popular.

## \|\| 3.22.28 \|\|

*sadgrāme sujanākīrṇe sukṣetre devatālaye \|*  
*puṇye nadanadītīre vadetpuṇyakathāṃ sudhīḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. A learned expounder should narrate the holy story in a good village abounding in good people, in a holy place, in a temple, on the holy banks of rivers etc.

## \|\| 3.22.29 \|\|

*śivabhaktisamāyuktā nānyakāryeṣu lālasā \|*  
*vāgyatāḥ suśravo'vyagrāḥ śrotāraḥ puṇyabhāginaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Listeners endowed with devotion to Śiva, who are not interested in other activities, who control their speech, who have good auditory power and who are never perturbed shall earn merit.

## \|\| 3.22.30 \|\|

*abhaktā ye kathāṃ puṇyāṃ śṛṇvaṃti manujādhamāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ puṇyaphalaṃ nāsti duḥkhaṃ syājjanmajanmani \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Those base men who listen to the holy story without devotion, shall not derive meritorious benefits. In every birth they will be miserable.

## \|\| 3.22.31 \|\|

*purāṇaṃ ye tvasaṃpūjya tāṃbūlādyairupāyanaiḥ \|*  
*śṛṇvaṃti ca kathāṃ bhaktyā daridrāḥ syurna pāpinaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Those who listen devoutly to a Purāṇa without first adoring it with betel leaves and other offerings, may become poor, though they are not sinners.

## \|\| 3.22.32 \|\|

*kathāyāṃ kīrtyamānāyāṃ ye gacchaṃtyanyato narāḥ \|*  
*bhogāṃtare praṇaśyaṃti teṣāṃ dārāśca saṃpadaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. If men go elsewhere in the middle when the story is in progress, their wives and riches die or perish in the middle of the enjoyment of pleasures.

## \|\| 3.22.33 \|\|

*soṣṇīṣamastakā ye ca kathāṃ śṛṇvaṃti pāvanīm \|*  
*te balākāḥ prajāyante pāpino manujādhamāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Those base men who listen to the holy story with turbans on their heads are reborn as cranes. They are sinful persons.

## \|\| 3.22.34 \|\|

*tāṃbūlaṃ bhakṣayanto ye kathāṃ śṛṇvaṃti pāvanīm \|*  
*svaviṣṭhāṃ khādayaṃtyetānnarake yamakiṃkarāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Those who listen to the holy story while chewing betel leaves will be compelled to swallow their own excreta by the servants of Yama in Naraka.

## \|\| 3.22.35 \|\|

*ye ca tuṃgāsanārūḍhāḥ kathāṃ śṛṇvaṃti dāṃbhikāḥ \|*  
*akṣayānnarakānbhuktvā te bhavaṃtyeva vāyasāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Those haughty persons who listen to the story while occupying a very high seat, will experience endless miseries in hell and ultimately be born as crows.

## \|\| 3.22.36 \|\|
